She spent much of the past decade trying to bring it to the big screen — a previous film version, starring Katharine Hepburn, was released in 1962 — and encountered almost as much drama as is featured in the play itself. Financing came together and fell apart numerous times, including even after the cast and crew were on set in Ireland. But ultimately, she got it across the finish line in collaboration with writer David Lindsay-Abaire and director Jonathan Kent, and she is immensely proud of the finished product.
paras.zh: 但最让她着迷的角色莫过于《长日行进夜》中的蒂龙，她于 2000 年首次在伦敦舞台上演出（成为第一位获得奥利弗奖提名的美国女演员），然后于 2016 年在百老汇重演（获得托尼奖）。她在过去十年的大部分时间里都在尝试将其搬上大银幕（之前的电影版本由凯瑟琳·赫本主演，于 1962 年上映），但遇到的戏剧性几乎与戏剧本身一样多。融资多次来来去去，甚至在演员和工作人员到达爱尔兰片场之后也是如此。但最终，她与编剧大卫·林赛-阿贝尔和导演乔纳森·肯特合作跨过终点线，她对成品感到非常自豪。

paras.en: Now, as Long Day’s Journey Into Night plays at film festivals and in select theaters courtesy of a tiny distributor, Lange is hustling to make sure people know about it and see it. And having also recently returned to American Horror Story for its 13th season, which rolled out between Sept. 24 and Oct. 29, she finds herself back in contention for both an Oscar and an Emmy.
paras.zh: 现在，当《漫漫长夜之旅》在电影节和由一家小发行商提供的精选影院上映时，兰格正在努力确保人们了解并观看它。最近，她又重返《美国恐怖故事》第 13 季（该剧于 9 月 24 日至 10 月 29 日之间推出），她发现自己又重新回到了奥斯卡奖和艾美奖的争夺之中。

paras.en: For now, at least, Jessica Lange isn’t going anywhere.
paras.zh: 至少现在，杰西卡·兰格不会去任何地方。

articles.title: Trump questions midterm election results, revives voting-machine conspiracy

paras.en: President Donald Trump on Monday questioned the legitimacy of the midterm election results, resurrecting his pattern of raising doubts about electoral losses for himself and other Republicans.
paras.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统周一质疑中期选举结果的合法性，再次对自己和其他共和党人的选举失败提出质疑。

paras.en: Trump's social media post raising questions about the election came six days after his fellow Republicans suffered historic defeats at the polls nationwide, including in several GOP strongholds like Texas and South Carolina.
paras.zh: 特朗普在社交媒体上发帖提出了对选举的质疑，六天前他的共和党同僚在全国范围内的民意调查中遭遇历史性失败，其中包括德克萨斯州和南卡罗来纳州等几个共和党据点。

paras.en: "Does anybody really believe that this 'Election' was honest," Trump wrote on Truth Social.
paras.zh: 特朗普在《真相社会》上写道：“有人真的相信这次‘选举’是诚实的吗？”

paras.en: "How could the Polls be so wrong??? Some early voting 'dumps' were so large that it was impossible to win, no matter how many people went to vote," the president said. "It's all about the machines, which are far more important than the voter!"
paras.zh: “民意调查怎么会如此错误？？？一些提前投票的‘垃圾场’规模如此之大，以至于无论有多少人去投票，都不可能获胜，”总统说。 “一切都与机器有关，机器比选民重要得多！”

paras.en: Trump's post was a sharp pivot from what has been a conciliatory tone after last Tuesday's thumping of Republican candidates, which resulted in Democrats regaining majorities in both the Senate and House of Representatives.
paras.zh: 特朗普的立场与上周二共和党候选人的重击导致民主党重新获得参议院和众议院多数席位后的和解语气截然不同。

paras.en: On Election Night, Trump told The New York Times that he was "absolutely willing" to accept the results of the midterms, and that he was willing to work with Democrats.
paras.zh: 选举之夜，特朗普对《纽约时报》表示，他“绝对愿意”接受中期选举的结果，并且愿意与民主党合作。

paras.en: "We'll, you know, look forward to working with them," Trump told The Times. "We'll probably work something out."
paras.zh: “你知道，我们期待与他们合作，”特朗普告诉《泰晤士报》。 “我们可能会想出办法。”

paras.en: The next day, Trump said, "I'll get along probably with the Democrats unless they want to be destructive."
paras.zh: 第二天，特朗普表示，“我可能会与民主党相处，除非他们想要破坏性的。”

paras.en: Later in the week, he announced he was replacing White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles with her deputy, Stephen Miller, the architect of the administration's aggressive immigration enforcement crackdown, which has drawn widespread criticism from Democrats.
paras.zh: 本周晚些时候，他宣布将用副手史蒂芬·米勒(Stephen Miller)取代白宫办公厅主任苏西·威尔斯(Susie Wiles)。米勒是政府激进的移民执法镇压行动的策划者，此举引起了民主党人的广泛批评。

paras.en: Sen. Chuck Schumer, a New York Democrat who could be the majority leader in the Senate in January, said in a post on X, "Donald Trump's pathetic return to election denialism was inevitable."
paras.zh: 纽约民主党参议员查克·舒默(Chuck Schumer)可能在一月份成为参议院多数党领袖，他在X上的一篇帖子中表示，“唐纳德·特朗普可悲地回归选举否认主义是不可避免的。”

paras.en: "He can whine all he wants, but nothing will stop this inescapable truth: For the last two years of his presidency, Trump will face the largest Democratic congressional majorities in decades, all because he has been an unprecedented failure," Schumer said.
paras.zh: 舒默说：“他可以随心所欲地发牢骚，但没有什么能阻止这个不可避免的事实：在他总统任期的最后两年里，特朗普将面临数十年来最大的民主党国会多数席位，这一切都是因为他是前所未有的失败。”

paras.en: After his electoral loss to former President Joe Biden in 2020, Trump argued, without evidence, that he only lost as a result of widespread ballot fraud.
paras.zh: 在 2020 年选举中输给前总统乔·拜登后，特朗普在没有证据的情况下辩称，他只是因为广泛的选票舞弊而落败。

paras.en: Trump's claims, which were joined by dozens of unsuccessful court cases challenging election procedures, culminated in the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the U.S. Capitol by a mob of his supporters after he spoke at a rally outside the White House.
paras.zh: 特朗普的主张加上数十起挑战选举程序的不成功法庭案件，最终导致 2021 年 1 月 6 日，他的支持者在白宫外的一次集会上发表讲话后袭击美国国会大厦。

paras.en: The riot disrupted a joint session of Congress for hours. Later that day, Congress confirmed Biden's election by the Electoral College.
paras.zh: 骚乱使国会联席会议中断了几个小时。当天晚些时候，国会通过选举人团确认拜登当选。

paras.en: Critics of Trump's conspiracy theories about elections have noted that he lost the 2020 race when he was president, but won the 2024 presidential election, when Biden was in the White House.
paras.zh: 特朗普关于选举的阴谋论的批评者指出，他在担任总统时输掉了 2020 年的竞选，但在拜登入主白宫时赢得了 2024 年总统选举。

paras.en: They also noted that in the past week, Republicans had control of states that saw major Democratic wins that few analysts would have predicted a year ago, including Texas, Kansas, South Carolina, and Iowa.
paras.zh: 他们还指出，过去一周，共和党控制了民主党取得重大胜利的州，包括德克萨斯州、堪萨斯州、南卡罗来纳州和爱荷华州，这些州是一年前很少有分析师预测到的。

articles.title: Jensen Huang affair puts Nvidia's future at risk, with no clear successor to the renowned CEO

paras.en: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's admission of an affair with a purported Chinese spy has raised questions about his future at the company, and what happens if the 63-year-old co-founder, who built the chipmaker into one of the most valuable businesses on the planet, is forced out.
paras.zh: 英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋承认与一名所谓的中国间谍有染，这引发了人们对他在公司的未来的质疑，以及如果这位将这家芯片制造商打造为全球最有价值企业之一的 63 岁联合创始人被迫离职会发生什么。

paras.en: Shares of Nvidia sank more than 4% on Monday, even as the broader market rallied sharply, after Huang acknowledged the affair in a message to staff on Sunday, and said that the board was launching an investigation into whether he was targeted by a foreign intelligence agency. The board said it has "confidence in Jensen," and that it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised."
paras.zh: 黄在周日发给员工的信息中承认了这一事件，并表示董事会正在对他是否成为外国情报机构的攻击目标进行调查，尽管大盘大幅上涨，但英伟达股价周一仍下跌逾 4%。该董事会表示“对 Jensen 充满信心”，并且“没有理由相信国家安全或 Nvidia 的机密受到损害”。

paras.en: The New York Times first reported that the Chinese businesswoman was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security, according to people briefed on the intelligence circulated in a memo among the Trump administration in the spring. China has called the allegation a smear.
paras.zh: 据了解特朗普政府今年春天一份备忘录中流传的情报的人士透露，《纽约时报》首先报道称，这名中国女商人是中国国家安全部的间谍。中国称这一指控是诽谤。

paras.en: While Nvidia says Huang will continue to lead the company during the probe, pressure is rapidly mounting on the chipmaker, whose technology has powered the first four years of the generative artificial intelligence boom. Leaders from both parties are calling for briefings, and Democrats poised to take control of both houses of Congress are calling for investigations and new legislation "to stop advanced AI chips from fueling China's military," Sen. Elizabeth Warren of Massachusetts wrote in a post on X on Monday.
paras.zh: 尽管英伟达表示，黄仁勋将在调查期间继续领导该公司，但这家芯片制造商面临的压力正在迅速加大，该公司的技术为生成式人工智能热潮的前四年提供了动力。马萨诸塞州参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦 (Elizabeth Warren) 周一在 X 上发帖称，两党领导人都在呼吁通报情况，而准备控制国会参众两院的民主党人则呼吁进行调查并制定新立法，“以阻止先进人工智能芯片为中国军队提供动力”。

paras.en: Huang has outsized influence over Nvidia, and is the sole face of the company with no clear second-in-command. He's also among the loudest champions of AI in the country, is critical to the financing of the broader infrastructure buildout and has a close relationship with President Donald Trump, giving Nvidia a front-row seat when it comes to discussions on AI policy, safety and regulation.
paras.zh: 黄仁勋对英伟达有着巨大的影响力，并且是该公司唯一没有明确第二把手的人。他也是美国最响亮的人工智能倡导者之一，对更广泛的基础设施建设融资至关重要，并且与唐纳德·特朗普总统关系密切，这让英伟达在人工智能政策、安全和监管讨论方面占据了前排席位。

paras.en: "The issue at Nvidia is that there is no clear successor to Jensen, and we had expected him to stay in this role for at least 10 more years," analysts at Melius Research said in a Monday research note.
paras.zh: Melius Research 分析师在周一的研究报告中表示：“Nvidia 的问题在于，Jensen 没有明确的继任者，我们原本预计他将继续担任这个职位至少 10 年。”

paras.en: Stacy Rasgon, an analyst at Bernstein, told CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" on Monday that, "Jensen is Nvidia. Nvidia is Jensen." He added that Huang "runs the thing pretty much top down," and "sort of pulls all the strings."
paras.zh: Bernstein 分析师 Stacy Rasgon 周一在 CNBC 的“Squawk on the Street”节目中表示，“Jensen 就是 Nvidia。Nvidia 就是 Jensen。”他补充说，黄“几乎是自上而下地管理这件事”，并且“在某种程度上幕后操纵”。

paras.en: Nvidia didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.
paras.zh: 英伟达没有立即回应置评请求。

paras.en: Nvidia has long maintained a flat, non-hierarchical organizational structure. Huang has deep involvement in the company's day-to-day operations and frequently serves as its spokesperson in front of world leaders and at industry conferences. In addition to being co-founder and CEO, Huang is also Nvidia's president.
paras.zh: 英伟达长期以来一直保持着扁平化、无等级的组织结构。黄先生深入参与公司的日常运营，并经常在世界领导人面前和行业会议上担任公司发言人。除了联合创始人兼首席执行官之外，黄仁勋还是 Nvidia 的总裁。

paras.en: In September of 2025, Huang told CNBC's Becky Quick that he had as many as 60 direct reports. Internal records reviewed by CNBC reveal that, as of this week, he had 33 direct reports, including CFO Colette Kress, influential Chief Scientist Bill Dally, senior vice president of software engineering Dwight Diercks, and Ian Buck, best known as the inventor of Nvidia's CUDA software.
paras.zh: 2025 年 9 月，黄告诉 CNBC 的 Becky Quick，他有多达 60 名直接下属。 CNBC 查阅的内部记录显示，截至本周，他有 33 名直接下属，其中包括首席财务官 Colette Kress、颇具影响力的首席科学家 Bill Dally、软件工程高级副总裁 Dwight Diercks 以及因 Nvidia CUDA 软件发明者而闻名的 Ian Buck。

paras.en: However, relative to some of his founder peers in tech like Meta's Mark Zuckerberg and Elon Musk at SpaceX, Huang has minimal actual control. He owns just over 3% of the outstanding shares and is one of 11 members on a board that has no official chair.
paras.zh: 然而，相对于 Meta 的马克·扎克伯格和 SpaceX 的埃隆·马斯克等科技领域的创始人同行，黄仁勋的实际控制权微乎其微。他拥有略高于 3% 的已发行股份，并且是没有正式主席的董事会的 11 名成员之一。

paras.en: And in the risk factors of Nvidia's financial filings, Huang isn't specifically identified as a key person. Rather, the company says, "we are highly dependent on the services of our longstanding executive team."
paras.zh: 在英伟达财务文件的风险因素中，黄仁勋并没有被明确列为关键人物。相反，该公司表示，“我们高度依赖我们长期管理团队的服务。”

paras.en: "Failure to ensure effective succession planning, transfer of knowledge, and smooth transitions involving executives and key employees could hinder our strategic planning, execution, and long-term success," Nvidia says.
paras.zh: 英伟达表示：“如果无法确保有效的继任计划、知识转移以及高管和关键员工的平稳过渡，可能会阻碍我们的战略规划、执行和长期成功。”

paras.en: Still, Huang's influence is undeniable, so much so that the question of succession is one that's hardly broached among analysts and investors.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，黄的影响力是不可否认的，以至于分析师和投资者几乎没有讨论过继任者的问题。

paras.en: Timm Schulze-Melander, an analyst at Rothschild & Co. Redburn, wrote in a Monday note that Huang could be forced to step back from the CEO role if the board's investigation reveals "something materially more serious" than an undisclosed relationship.
paras.zh: Rothschild & Co. Redburn 分析师蒂姆·舒尔茨-梅兰德 (Timm Schulze-Melander) 在周一的一份报告中写道，如果董事会的调查发现“比未公开的关系更严重的事情”，黄可能会被迫辞去首席执行官职务。

paras.en: But Schulze-Melander said Huang's potential resignation isn't a foregone conclusion of the investigation, pointing to the importance of his leadership at the company.
paras.zh: 但舒尔茨-梅兰德表示，黄的潜在辞职并不是调查的必然结果，并指出了他在公司领导力的重要性。

paras.en: Nvidia's board "needs to demonstrate independence and protect shareholders without destabilizing a company whose success is unusually dependent on its founder," Schulze-Melander wrote. "Its initial statement suggests it is attempting to achieve both."
paras.zh: 舒尔茨-梅兰德写道，英伟达董事会“需要表现出独立性并保护股东，同时又不破坏一家公司的稳定，该公司的成功异常依赖于其创始人”。 “其最初的声明表明它正在努力实现这两点。”

paras.en: Several analysts said the investigation could lead to governance changes at Nvidia, including putting a transition contingency plan in place.
paras.zh: 几位分析师表示，调查可能会导致英伟达的治理发生变化，包括制定过渡应急计划。

paras.en: The Melius analysts wrote that Nvidia has a "strong bench" of executive talent across its networking, hyperscale and high-performance computing businesses, along with "technical expertise" stemming from Chief Technology Officer Michael Kagan as well as Dally, the chief scientist.
paras.zh: Melius 分析师写道，英伟达在网络、超大规模和高性能计算业务方面拥有“强大的管理人才”，以及首席技术官迈克尔·卡根 (Michael Kagan) 和首席科学家达利 (Dally) 的“技术专长”。

paras.en: "While these folks can keep the engine running, Jensen is one of a kind, and his energy will be needed to maintain confidence in the AI trade," the analysts wrote.
paras.zh: 分析师写道：“虽然这些人可以保持引擎运转，但詹森是其中之一，需要他的精力来维持对人工智能行业的信心。”

paras.en: — CNBC's Kif Leswing, Kristina Partsinevelos, Michael Bloom and Lora Kolodny contributed to this report.
paras.zh: — CNBC 的 Kif Leswing、Kristina Partsinevelos、Michael Bloom 和 Lora Kolodny 对本报告做出了贡献。

articles.title: Hegseth impeachment articles introduced by Rep. Massie

paras.en: Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., on Monday introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, triggering a vote in the House of Representatives as early as this week.
paras.zh: 肯塔基州众议员托马斯·马西周一提出了针对国防部长皮特·赫格斯的弹劾条款，最早将于本周在众议院引发投票。

paras.en: The unusual impeachment push against Hegseth by a member of his own party comes after Democrats swept to majorities in both the House and Senate during last week's midterm elections. Many Republicans, including Vice President JD Vance, have cited the Iran war Hegseth has led as a reason for the electoral bludgeoning.
paras.zh: 民主党在上周的中期选举中横扫参众两院多数席位后，本党一名成员对赫格赛斯发起了不同寻常的弹劾行动。包括副总统万斯在内的许多共和党人都将赫格塞斯领导的伊朗战争视为选举中遭受重创的原因。

paras.en: Massie, who lost his reelection bid in a Republican primary in May, introduced eight articles of impeachment against Hegseth. They include waging war in contravention of war powers resolutions Congress passed to limit war, extrajudicial killings tied to boat strikes in the Caribbean that purported to target drug smugglers and suppressing free speech by targeting Sen. Mark Kelly, D-Ariz., a veteran.
paras.zh: 马西在五月份的共和党初选中失去连任，他提出了八项针对赫格斯的弹劾条款。其中包括违反国会通过的限制战争的战争权力决议发动战争、与加勒比海船只袭击有关的法外处决（旨在针对毒品走私者），以及针对退伍军人参议员、亚利桑那州民主党人马克·凯利（Mark Kelly）压制言论自由。

paras.en: "Wherefore, Secretary of Defense Peter Hegseth, by such conduct, has demonstrated that he will remain a threat to the Constitution if allowed to remain in office, and has acted in a manner grossly incompatible with his duties and the rule of law," the articles, which Massie read from the House floor, read. "Peter Brian Hegseth thus warrants impeachment and trial, removal from office, and disqualification to hold and enjoy any office of honor, trust, or profit under the United States."
paras.zh: 马西在众议院宣读的这些文章中写道：“因此，国防部长彼得·赫格斯的这种行为表明，如果允许他继续留任，他将仍然对宪法构成威胁，而且他的行为方式与他的职责和法治严重不相容。” “因此，彼得·布莱恩·赫格斯（Peter Brian Hegseth）应受到弹劾和审判、免职，并取消在美国担任和享有任何荣誉、信任或利润职位的资格。”

paras.en: Massie's resolution will force House Republican leaders to put the measure up for a vote by the end of this week. Impeachment resolutions are privileged, meaning the House must act on them, table them or vote to refer them to committee within two legislative days.
paras.zh: 马西的决议将迫使众议院共和党领导人在本周末之前对该措施进行投票。弹劾决议具有特权，这意味着众议院必须在两个立法日内对这些决议采取行动、将其提交或投票将其提交给委员会。

paras.en: President Donald Trump once again defended Hegseth later Monday, telling reporters at the White House he will stand by the secretary even if he is impeached.
paras.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统周一晚些时候再次为赫格塞斯辩护，他在白宫告诉记者，即使国务卿被弹劾，他也将支持他。

paras.en: "He won two wars. He was in charge," said Trump, who was impeached twice in his first presidential term.
paras.zh: “他赢得了两场战争。他负责，”在第一个总统任期内两次被弹劾的特朗普说道。

paras.en: Trump also credited Hegseth with boosting military recruitment, claiming there are "waiting lists of people trying to get in."
paras.zh: 特朗普还称赞赫格塞斯促进了征兵，称“有一些人在等待入伍”。

paras.en: "He's done a very good job," Trump said.
paras.zh: 特朗普说：“他做得非常好。”

paras.en: Congress has the authority to impeach Cabinet secretaries, though it is a highly unusual move. Republican leadership in the House has not yet laid out how they plan to deal with the Hegseth impeachment, and it is unclear whether they have the votes to dispose of Massie's measure following the election.
paras.zh: 国会有权弹劾内阁部长，尽管这是一个极不寻常的举动。众议院共和党领导层尚未阐明他们计划如何处理赫格斯弹劾案，也不清楚他们是否有票在选举后处理马西的措施。

paras.en: The last Cabinet Secretary to be impeached was Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas in 2024 over his handling of the U.S.-Mexico border. Before Mayorkas, a Cabinet secretary had not been impeached since Secretary of War William Belknap in 1876. Neither was convicted by the Senate.
paras.zh: 上一位因处理美墨边境问题而被弹劾的内阁部长是 2024 年的国土安全部长亚历杭德罗·马约卡斯 (Alejandro Mayorkas)。在马约卡斯之前，自 1876 年陆军部长威廉·贝尔纳普以来，还没有内阁秘书被弹劾过。两人都没有被参议院定罪。

paras.en: If the House votes to impeach Hegseth, the Senate would be tasked with holding a trial and voting on removing the secretary from office. If convicted by a two-thirds majority of the Senate, Hegseth would be removed from office.
paras.zh: 如果众议院投票弹劾赫格塞斯，参议院将负责进行审判并投票罢免这位国务卿。如果参议院三分之二多数票判定赫格塞斯有罪，赫格塞斯将被免职。

paras.en: Republicans hold a razor-thin 218-214 majority in the House, meaning only a handful of Republican defections could result in Hegseth's impeachment.
paras.zh: 共和党在众议院以 218 比 214 的微弱优势占据多数，这意味着只有少数共和党人的叛逃可能导致赫格赛斯被弹劾。

paras.en: House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., reiterated his support for impeaching Hegseth on Monday at his first press conference at the Capitol since last Tuesday's elections. "Pete Hegseth has abused his power, undermined America's national security, and he's the architect of the reckless and costly failed war of choice in Iran," Jeffries said.
paras.zh: 纽约州众议院少数党领袖哈基姆·杰弗里斯周一在国会大厦举行的自上周二选举以来的首次新闻发布会上重申了他对弹劾赫格斯的支持。杰弗里斯说：“皮特·赫格斯滥用权力，破坏了美国的国家安全，他是伊朗这场鲁莽且代价高昂、失败的选择战争的策划者。”

paras.en: Hegseth has appeared to be preparing for an impeachment fight. The secretary put out a video last week defending his actions atop the Pentagon, and the department has led a media campaign to "Stand. Fight. Defend the Republic."
paras.zh: 赫格斯似乎正在为弹劾斗争做准备。国务卿上周发布了一段视频，为他在五角大楼高层的行为辩护，国防部还领导了一场“挺身、战斗、保卫共和国”的媒体运动。

paras.en: Hegseth on Monday announced he would hold a press conference Tuesday morning at the Pentagon. His most recent press conference way May 5, just over two months after the Iran war began.
paras.zh: 赫格斯周一宣布，他将于周二上午在五角大楼举行新闻发布会。他最近一次新闻发布会是在 5 月 5 日，即伊朗战争开始两个多月后。

articles.title: Bursts of ‘pink noise’ during sleep could help your brain clean itself

paras.en: Your brain has a built-in cleansing cycle. While you sleep, the glymphatic system bathes your brain in a liquid called cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) to flush out the waste particles that accumulate throughout the day. But disordered sleep and the natural effects of aging can disrupt this nightly routine, potentially leading to the accumulation of harmful particles that increase your risk for neurodegenerative disease. Now, research published in Science Translational Medicine shows that listening to short bursts of fuzzy-sounding “pink noise” timed with brain waves during sleep can encourage CSF flow.
paras.zh: 你的大脑有一个内置的清洁周期。当您睡觉时，类淋巴系统会将您的大脑浸入一种称为脑脊液 (CSF) 的液体中，以冲洗掉全天积累的废物颗粒。但睡眠紊乱和衰老的自然影响可能会扰乱这种夜间惯例，可能导致有害颗粒的积累，从而增加患神经退行性疾病的风险。现在，发表在《科学转化医学》上的研究表明，在睡眠期间聆听与脑电波同步的短促听起来模糊的“粉红噪音”可以促进脑脊液流动。

paras.en: There have been few promising treatments to improve the glymphatic system’s functioning without major tradeoffs, says University of Rochester glymphatic biologist Lauren Hablitz, who was not involved in the study. “The biggest challenge to the CSF and glymphatic brain-clearance field right now ... is really therapies,” she adds. Compared with drugs and surgeries to increase flow, which are still experimental, using pink noise “could be really powerful in a much less invasive way.”
paras.zh: 罗切斯特大学的类淋巴生物学家劳伦·哈布利茨（Lauren Hablitz）没有参与这项研究，他说，目前几乎没有什么有希望的治疗方法可以在不进行重大权衡的情况下改善类淋巴系统的功能。 “目前脑脊液和类淋巴脑清除领域面临的最大挑战……实际上是治疗，”她补充道。与仍处于实验阶段的药物和增加流量的手术相比，使用粉红噪音“可能以侵入性小得多的方式发挥真正的作用。”

paras.en: Researchers knew that certain waves of brain activity during sleep, called slow waves, precede CSF flow. They also knew that people can enhance their slow waves by listening to bursts of staticky pink noise—a fuzz of sound defined by louder low pitches and quieter high ones—at the same time as the waves’ peaks. The study authors placed electrode caps on participants’ heads while they slept in a magnetic resonance imaging machine, and they used an algorithm to time the pink noise with slow-wave peaks. Brain scans showed that CSF flow was higher when the pink noise played during slow waves than it was during control periods with no noise alongside the waves.
paras.zh: 研究人员知道，睡眠期间大脑活动的某些波（称为慢波）先于脑脊液流动。他们还知道，人们可以通过在波峰达到峰值的同时聆听一阵阵静态粉红噪音（一种由响亮的低音和安静的高音定义的模糊声音）来增强慢波。研究作者在参与者睡在磁共振成像机中时将电极帽戴在他们的头上，并使用一种算法对粉红噪声与慢波峰值进行计时。脑部扫描显示，在慢波期间播放粉红噪音时，脑脊液流量比在波旁没有噪音的对照期间更高。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: The team doesn’t fully know why the timed noises increased CSF flow but suspects the sound may activate a special type of slow wave that helps the brain avoid responding to noises during sleep, such as cars passing by. The brain is less active and draws in less blood during part of the slow wave, so CSF flows in to help maintain pressure in your head.
paras.zh: 研究小组并不完全知道为什么定时噪音会增加脑脊液流量，但怀疑声音可能会激活一种特殊类型的慢波，帮助大脑避免在睡眠期间对噪音做出反应，例如汽车驶过的噪音。在慢波期间，大脑不太活跃，吸入的血液也较少，因此脑脊液流入有助于维持头部压力。

paras.en: Lead author Joshua Levitt, a biomedical engineer who recently completed his Ph.D. at Boston University, says the effect is less about the pink noise itself and more about its timing with brain waves. “You can’t just play pink noise all night and get the same effect,” he says. Sounds with different frequency balances, such as white noise, might also be effective.
paras.zh: 主要作者 Joshua Levitt 是一位生物医学工程师，最近完成了博士学位。波士顿大学的研究人员表示，这种影响与粉红噪音本身无关，而更多地与它与脑电波的时间有关。 “你不可能整晚都播放粉红噪音并获得同样的效果，”他说。具有不同频率平衡的声音（例如白噪声）也可能有效。

paras.en: If validated by future work, selective noise-playing could potentially unlock more restorative sleep in a home environment, the researchers say. They’re particularly interested in testing the method in older individuals and in people with sleep disorders. Study co-author Laura Lewis, a neuroscientist at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, says an important next step is testing whether the increased CSF flow actually helped to clear waste particles from the brain. Confirming that “is very tough to do in a human,” she says, so follow-ups in animals will be key.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，如果未来的工作得到验证，选择性播放噪音可能会在家庭环境中带来更多恢复性睡眠。他们特别有兴趣在老年人和患有睡眠障碍的人身上测试该方法。该研究的合著者、麻省理工学院的神经科学家劳拉·刘易斯表示，下一步重要的是测试增加的脑脊液流量是否真的有助于清除大脑中的废物颗粒。她说，要证实这一点“在人类身上很难做到”，因此在动物身上进行后续研究将是关键。

articles.title: The coin-flipping trick that counts the Internet

paras.en: Let’s say I want to know how many people read one of my articles on Scientific American’s website. Counting how many times it gets opened is easy: the website can maintain a running tally and increment it by one every time anyone loads the page. That tally is a single number and requires only a tiny amount of memory to store. But page loads aren't people. Maybe you started reading over breakfast, got distracted and came back to finish it after lunch. A simple tally would count you twice. To count unique people precisely, a website has to log every reader and check each reader who loads the page against that roster. Counting total views involves a single number, while counting unique viewers seems to need a list of IDs as large as the audience. Now multiply the number of IDs opening an article by every article, every post on a social media platform (perhaps to gauge trends) or every ad on a website (to meet advertisers’ quotas), each with its own roster of potentially millions of IDs. The lists pile up into mountains of data, all to answer a simple question: “How many people saw this?”
paras.zh: 假设我想知道有多少人阅读了我在《科学美国人》网站上的一篇文章。计算它被打开的次数很容易：网站可以维护一个运行计数，并在每次有人加载页面时将其加一。该计数是一个单一的数字，只需要少量的内存来存储。但页面加载的不是人。也许你在早餐时开始阅读，分心了，然后在午餐后回来完成它。一个简单的统计就会算你两次。为了精确地计算独特的人数，网站必须记录每个读者，并根据该名册检查每个加载页面的读者。计算总观看次数涉及一个数字，而计算唯一观看者似乎需要与观众一样大的 ID 列表。现在，将打开一篇文章的 ID 数量乘以每篇文章、社交媒体平台上的每个帖子（也许是为了衡量趋势）或网站上的每个广告（为了满足广告商的配额），每个 ID 都有自己的潜在数百万个 ID 名册。这些列表堆积成海量的数据，所有这些都是为了回答一个简单的问题：“有多少人看到了这个？”

paras.en: Enter the HyperLogLog algorithm. It settles for close estimates instead of exact counts, and in exchange, it uses only a fraction of the memory required by full lists of IDs. The algorithm is worth learning about for at least two reasons. First, it’s everywhere. Google Analytics, which tracks traffic on nearly half of all websites, relies on an augmented version of it to estimate visitor metrics. If you’ve ever checked the visitor count for a personal blog, you’ve probably seen its handiwork. Beyond Google, many fields, including genomics and cybersecurity, also depend on it. Second, HyperLogLog is ridiculously elegant.
paras.zh: 输入 HyperLogLog 算法。它满足于近似估计而不是精确计数，作为交换，它仅使用完整 ID 列表所需内存的一小部分。该算法值得学习至少有两个原因。首先，它无处不在。谷歌分析（Google Analytics）跟踪近一半网站的流量，依靠它的增强版本来估计访问者指标。如果您曾经检查过个人博客的访问者数量，您可能已经看到了它的杰作。除了谷歌之外，包括基因组学和网络安全在内的许多领域也依赖于它。其次，HyperLogLog 非常优雅。

paras.en: To understand the algorithm’s key idea, let’s start with a game. I’ll flip a coin repeatedly until it lands heads up, and then I’ll note how many tails came before it. That counts as one round. I repeat this for many rounds, tracking only one number: the longest streak of tails before the first appearance of heads. Now suppose I tell you that my record after an afternoon of coin flipping was 10 tails in a row. Your task is to guess how many rounds I played.
paras.zh: 为了理解算法的关键思想，让我们从一个游戏开始。我会反复抛一枚硬币，直到它正面朝上，然后我会记下它之前有多少个反面。这算作一轮。我重复了很多轮，只跟踪一个数字：第一次出现正面之前最长的尾巴条纹。现在假设我告诉你，我在一个下午的抛硬币后的记录是连续 10 次反面。你的任务是猜猜我玩了多少轮。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: You can make a decent guess. A streak of 10 tails turns up only about once in every 1,000 rounds. That’s because there is a 50–50 chance for an individual flip to turn up heads. The first flip is tails 1⁄2 of the time; the first two flips are both tails 1⁄4 of the time; the first three are all tails 1⁄8 of the time, and so on with the denominator doubling until 10 consecutive tails occur in one out of every 1,024 rounds. If I had played only a dozen rounds, a streak that long would be a surprising fluke. If I had played a million, I would have almost certainly seen a longer one. My record was a one-in-1,000 event, so a good guess is that it took somewhere around 1,000 rounds.
paras.zh: 你可以做出一个合理的猜测。连续出现 10 条反面的情况大约每 1,000 轮才会出现一次。这是因为单次翻转有 50-50 的机会出现正面。第一次翻转有 1⁄2 出现反面的情况；前两次翻转均为反面的概率均为 1⁄4；前三个都是反面的概率为 1⁄8，以此类推，分母加倍，直到每​​ 1,024 轮中出现 10 次连续反面。如果我只打了十几轮，这么长时间的连续比赛将是一个令人惊讶的侥幸。如果我玩了一百万，我几乎肯定会看到更长的。我的记录是千分之一的事件，所以一个好的猜测是大约需要 1,000 轮。

paras.en: HyperLogLog plays this same game, but every round corresponds to one visitor. At a high level, imagine each visitor flips a bunch of coins, writes down the results and shows them to the site upon every visit. Just as knowing my longest run of tails allowed you to estimate the total number of rounds, the site only needs to track the longest streak of tails among all its visitors to estimate the audience size.
paras.zh: HyperLogLog 玩同样的游戏，但每一轮对应一个访客。在较高的层面上，想象每个访问者都掷一堆硬币，写下结果并在每次访问时将其显示给网站。正如知道我最长的尾巴序列可以让您估计总轮数一样，该网站只需要跟踪所有访问者中最长的尾巴序列即可估计观众规模。

paras.en: Say 10 people visit. Two have coin sequences of tails (T) and heads (H) that begin with TTTH, while the other eight begin with H, TH or TTH. The site just remembers the number three, the longest leading streak it has seen. That’s enough for a rough estimate: 23, or about eight visitors—not far from the true 10. If someone later shows up with a longer streak, the record goes up. And if one of the original 10 comes back, the site doesn’t need to know if they’re a repeat visitor or not: they bring the same sequence of flips, so the estimated count of visitors doesn’t change.
paras.zh: 假设有 10 个人来访。 Two have coin sequences of tails (T) and heads (H) that begin with TTTH, while the other eight begin with H, TH or TTH. The site just remembers the number three, the longest leading streak it has seen. That’s enough for a rough estimate: 23, or about eight visitors—not far from the true 10. If someone later shows up with a longer streak, the record goes up. And if one of the original 10 comes back, the site doesn’t need to know if they’re a repeat visitor or not: they bring the same sequence of flips, so the estimated count of visitors doesn’t change.

paras.en: Notice how little the site must remember. An audience of 1,000 people most likely produces its longest streak after around 10 rounds. A million people should expect to have a record streak at around 20. After a billion, the number grows to 30. Even if every person on Earth visited, the record streak would likely appear somewhere in the low 30s. We went from having to store billions of IDs to precisely count unique visitors to only having to store a two-digit number for an estimate.
paras.zh: 请注意该站点必须记住的内容是多么少。 An audience of 1,000 people most likely produces its longest streak after around 10 rounds.预计 100 万人将创下 20 人左右的连胜记录。超过 10 亿人后，这一数字将增长到 30 人。即使地球上的每个人都访问过，连胜纪录也可能会出现在 30 多岁左右。 We went from having to store billions of IDs to precisely count unique visitors to only having to store a two-digit number for an estimate.

paras.en: Two important questions remain: How exactly do we get every visitor to flip coins and remember them? And what if somebody gets an uncharacteristically long string of tails and skews the estimate?
paras.zh: 仍然存在两个重要问题：我们如何让每个访问者抛硬币并记住它们？如果有人得到一串不寻常的长尾巴并扭曲了估计值，该怎么办？

paras.en: First, of course visitors don’t actually flip coins; instead of tails and heads, the HyperLogLog algorithm tracks 0’s and 1’s. Here’s how it works: when you visit a website, the algorithm takes your unique ID and runs it through a hash function. Hash functions are ubiquitous in computer science. They take an input and transform it into an output that looks random despite being completely deterministic. This means that one can treat the outputs of a hash function as though they’re random numbers, but in fact, the function always yields the same output when it’s given the same input. So a hash function reads some identifier from you, such as the user name user_8675309, and converts it into a string of 1’s and 0’s, such as 01100101000100101000. These bits get treated as random coin flips, with 0 corresponding to tails and 1 to heads. The next time you visit the site using your ID, the same hash function produces the same string of bits to identify you.
paras.zh: 首先，当然，游客实际上并不是在掷硬币；而是在掷硬币。 HyperLogLog 算法跟踪 0 和 1，而不是尾部和头部。它的工作原理如下：当您访问网站时，算法会获取您的唯一 ID 并通过哈希函数运行它。哈希函数在计算机科学中无处不在。他们接受输入并将其转换为看起来随机的输出，尽管输出是完全确定性的。这意味着我们可以将哈希函数的输出视为随机数，但事实上，当给定相同的输入时，该函数总是会产生相同的输出。因此，哈希函数会从您那里读取一些标识符，例如用户名 user_8675309，并将其转换为由 1 和 0 组成的字符串，例如 01100101000100101000。这些位被视为随机硬币翻转，其中 0 对应于反面，1 对应于正面。下次您使用您的 ID 访问该网站时，相同的哈希函数会生成相同的位字符串来识别您的身份。

paras.en: Second, sometimes flukes happen. If somebody’s hash function output is the equivalent of a generational tear of flipping tails, the site will radically overestimate its audience. To guard against this kind of fluke, the algorithm splits the audience into many groups, estimates each group’s size independently, averages those estimates and combines the results.
paras.zh: 其次，有时会出现侥幸心理。如果某人的哈希函数输出相当于一代人翻转尾巴的眼泪，那么该网站就会从根本上高估其受众。为了防止这种侥幸，该算法将观众分成许多组，独立估计每个组的规模，对这些估计进行平均并合并结果。

paras.en: HyperLogLog cleverly uses the first few “flips” of each person’s sequence as a group assignment. Say we want four groups. Visitors whose sequences begin with 11 go in one group, those beginning with 10 go in another, and likewise for 01 and 00. The site then sets aside those first two flips and, within each group, tracks the longest streak of tails at the start of the digits that come after. A visitor whose sequence starts with 10001, for instance, joins the 10 group with a streak of two; if that's the longest streak anyone in the 10 group has shown, the site's record for that group is simply two. Because the first two flips sort people evenly, each group should hold about a quarter of the audience, so each group’s record gives its own estimate of a quarter of the total. Average those four estimates, multiply by four, and you have an estimate of the whole audience. This way a single unlucky visitor can spoil only one of the four records, and the other three pull the average back toward reality. Real implementations use thousands of groups and a special type of averaging called the harmonic mean that lowers the statistical weight of any outliers, so one fluke barely registers. All told, HyperLogLog’s estimates are typically off by less than 1 percent. In exchange for that error, sites can count billions of unique users using roughly the amount of memory it takes to store this article.
paras.zh: HyperLogLog 巧妙地利用每个人序列的前几次“翻转”作为小组作业。假设我们想要四个组。序列以 11 开头的访问者进入一组，以 10 开头的访问者进入另一组，01 和 00 也是如此。然后，该网站将前两次翻转放在一边，并在每组中跟踪后面数字开头的最长的尾巴条纹。例如，序列以 10001 开头的访问者会连续两次加入 10 组；如果这是 10 组中任何人所显示的最长连续记录，则该网站对该组的记录只是两次。因为前两次翻转对人们进行均匀排序，所以每组应该容纳大约四分之一的观众，因此每组的记录给出了自己对总数四分之一的估计。对这四个估计值进行平均，乘以四，您就可以估计整个观众。这样，一个不幸的访客只能破坏四项记录中的一项，而其他三项则将平均值拉回到现实。实际的实现使用数千个组和一种称为调和平均值的特殊平均类型，它可以降低任何异常值的统计权重，因此几乎不会出现侥幸。全部 据了解，HyperLogLog 的估计通常误差不到 1%。作为该错误的交换，网站可以使用大约存储本文所需的内存量来计算数十亿唯一用户。

paras.en: Beyond estimating unique visitors, the algorithm helps both cybersecurity professionals detect anomalous web activity such as swarms of bots and biologists find similarities across genomes. Any time somebody wants to estimate distinct elements in an enormous dataset, HyperLogLog is likely doing the counting.
paras.zh: 除了估计独特的访问者之外，该算法还帮助网络安全专业人员检测异常网络活动（例如机器人群），并帮助生物学家发现基因组之间的相似性。每当有人想要估计庞大数据集中的不同元素时，HyperLogLog 都可能会进行计数。

articles.title: Eli Lilly shows GLP-1 weight-loss pill Foundayo can dramatically improve sleep apnea

paras.en: Foundayo, an oral antiobesity pill, significantly improved obstructive sleep apnea, according to new clinical trial data. The results signal the potential uses of the GLP-1 (glucagonlike peptide 1) drug beyond weight loss.
paras.zh: 根据新的临床试验数据，Foundayo 是一种口服抗肥胖药，可显着改善阻塞性睡眠呼吸暂停。结果表明 GLP-1（胰高血糖素样肽 1）药物除了减肥之外还有潜在用途。

paras.en: Foundayo is the brand name for the drug orforglipron, which is made by Eli Lilly. It was approved for treating obesity by the Food and Drug Administration in April. At the same time, the pharmaceutical company has been probing the drug’s potential to treat other obesity-related conditions, including obstructive sleep apnea. The condition is characterized by pauses in air flow to the lungs during sleep that are longer than 10 seconds; it can cause loud snoring, choking, sleep deprivation, headaches and other symptoms. Globally, as many as 936 million adults are estimated to experience the condition, although most are never formally diagnosed.
paras.zh: Foundayo 是礼来公司生产的药物 orforglipron 的品牌名称。今年四月，美国食品和药物管理局批准其用于治疗肥胖症。与此同时，该制药公司一直在探索该药物治疗其他肥胖相关疾病的潜力，包括阻塞性睡眠呼吸暂停。该病症的特点是睡眠期间流向肺部的气流暂停超过 10 秒；它会导致打鼾、窒息、睡眠不足、头痛和其他症状。在全球范围内，估计有多达 9.36 亿成年人患有这种疾病，尽管大多数人从未被正式诊断过。

paras.en: Because it causes drops in oxygen, obstructive sleep apnea can also increase the risks of heart problems. That suggests treatment with Foundayo may also have cardiovascular health benefits, says Daniel Drucker, an endocrinologist at the Lunenfeld-Tanenbaum Research Institute in Ontario. Drucker was not involved with the new trial but has previously worked as a consultant for Eli Lilly.
paras.zh: 由于阻塞性睡眠呼吸暂停会导致氧气下降，因此也会增加患心脏病的风险。安大略省 Lunenfeld-Tanenbaum 研究所的内分泌学家 Daniel Drucker 表示，这表明 Foundayo 治疗也可能对心血管健康有益。德鲁克没有参与这项新试验，但此前曾担任礼来公司的顾问。

paras.en: “Every time we tinker with the GLP-1 backbone, the question of overall safety and cardiovascular safety resurfaces,” he says.
paras.zh: “每次我们对 GLP-1 主干进行修改时，整体安全性和心血管安全性问题都会重新出现，”他说。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: “We know there’s a two-way relationship between sleep and cardiovascular health, and the repeated drops in oxygen that happen with obstructive sleep apnea can strain blood pressure and the heart over time,” said study co-author Vaishnavi Kundel, an associate professor of medicine at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai, who has also consulted for Eli Lilly, in a statement. “Foundayo significantly reduced breathing interruptions and drops in oxygen during sleep, while also improving blood pressure and inflammation.”
paras.zh: 研究合著者、西奈山伊坎医学院医学副教授、礼来公司顾问瓦什纳维·昆德尔 (Vaishnavi Kundel) 在一份声明中表示：“我们知道睡眠和心血管健康之间存在双向关系，随着时间的推移，阻塞性睡眠呼吸暂停导致的氧气反复下降会使血压和心脏紧张。” “Foundayo 显着减少了睡眠期间的呼吸中断和氧气下降，同时还改善了血压和炎症。”

paras.en: In the new clinical trial results, published today in the Journal of the American Medical Association, after 52 weeks, the drug reduced the severity of sleep apnea by 43.8 percent in participants who were clinically classified as being overweight or having obesity and did not use a positive airway pressure (PAP) machine—such devices are commonly employed to treat sleep apnea. The GLP-1 pill reduced severity of sleep apnea symptoms by 27.5 percent in participants who were overweight or had obesity who did use a PAP machine. Both groups also lost around 28 pounds of weight on average over the course of the study.
paras.zh: 今天发表在《美国医学会杂志》上的新临床试验结果显示，52 周后，临床上被归类为超重或肥胖且未使用气道正压通气 (PAP) 机器（此类设备通常用于治疗睡眠呼吸暂停的设备）的参与者中，该药物将睡眠呼吸暂停的严重程度降低了 43.8%。对于使用 PAP 机的超重或肥胖参与者，GLP-1 药丸将睡眠呼吸暂停症状的严重程度降低了 27.5%。在研究过程中，两组人的体重平均减轻了约 28 磅。

paras.en: The results add to other evidence suggesting that Eli Lilly’s injectable GLP-1 medications may improve obstructive sleep apnea, too, Drucker says. “If approved, orforglipron may represent a new option for individuals preferring once-daily administration of a GLP-1 medicine for treatment of [obstructive sleep apnea],” he adds.
paras.zh: 德鲁克说，这些结果与其他证据相结合，表明礼来公司的注射 GLP-1 药物也可能改善阻塞性睡眠呼吸暂停。 “如果获得批准，orforglipron 可能会为那些喜欢每天服用一次 GLP-1 药物来治疗 [阻塞性睡眠呼吸暂停] 的个人提供一种新的选择，”他补充道。

paras.en: Eli Lilly plans to submit the drug for FDA review for the treatment moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults who are overweight or have obesity by the end of the year, according to a company statement.
paras.zh: 根据礼来公司的一份声明，礼来公司计划在今年年底前将该药物提交 FDA 审查，用于治疗超重或肥胖成人中度至重度阻塞性睡眠呼吸暂停。

articles.title: Record-low temperature created on China’s space station
articles.author: Emily Conover

paras.en: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback?
paras.zh: 这是一个由人工智能配音的人类书写的故事。有反馈吗？

paras.en: Science has reached a new low. Temperature, that is.
paras.zh: 科学已经达到了新的低点。温度，就是。

paras.en: Scientists cooled a collection of atoms to about 10 picokelvins, or 10 trillionths of a kelvin. That’s barely a smidge above absolute zero (−273.15° Celsius). The atoms formed a Bose-Einstein condensate, a quantum state of matter, colder than any before, researchers report November 5 in Science.
paras.zh: 科学家将一组原子冷却至约 10 皮开尔文，即万亿分之一开尔文。这仅比绝对零（-273.15°摄氏度）高一点点。研究人员于 11 月 5 日在《科学》杂志上报道称，这些原子形成了玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚体，这是一种物质的量子态，其温度比以前任何时候都要低。

paras.en: To achieve that record-low chill, scientists took their work to space. The atoms orbited Earth aboard China’s Tiangong space station. There, researchers used laser-based traps to contain 20,000 rubidium atoms and reduce their motion, thereby cooling them. At an atomic level, temperature is tied to motion: Atoms and molecules in the air around us move more slowly when it’s colder. Similarly, in systems of cold atoms, scientists can define an effective temperature based on how slowly the atoms spread apart when they are allowed to expand.
paras.zh: 为了实现创纪录的最低寒冷，科学家们将他们的工作带到了太空。这些原子乘坐中国天宫空间站绕地球运行。在那里，研究人员使用基于激光的陷阱来容纳 20,000 个铷原子并减少它们的运动，从而冷却它们。在原子层面上，温度与运动有关：当温度较低时，我们周围空气中的原子和分子运动得更慢。同样，在冷原子系统中，科学家可以根据原子膨胀时扩散的速度来定义有效温度。

paras.en: On Earth, gravitational forces cause clouds of atoms to sag, reducing the effectiveness of cooling. But on the space station, the atoms experienced microgravity, the apparent weightlessness of an object in free fall.
paras.zh: 在地球上，重力会导致原子云下垂，从而降低冷却效率。但在空间站上，原子经历了微重力，即自由落体物体表面上的失重状态。

paras.en: To make a Bose-Einstein condensate, a disorderly gaggle of atoms is cooled until the atoms all take on the same quantum state, acting as one entity. By experimenting with ultracold atoms, researchers can study exotic states of matter and other mysterious physics. And they can test fundamental concepts, such as the equivalence principle — the idea that explains why objects of different masses fall at the same rate in a vacuum.
paras.zh: 为了制造玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚体，一群无序的原子被冷却，直到所有原子都呈现相同的量子态，充当一个实体。通过对超冷原子进行实验，研究人员可以研究奇异的物质状态和其他神秘的物理现象。他们还可以测试基本概念，例如等效原理——该原理解释了为什么不同质量的物体在真空中以相同的速度下落。

paras.en: Spacefaring Bose-Einstein condensates were previously made on the International Space Station, at effective temperatures as low as 52 picokelvins. And an experiment on Earth, in which atoms were dropped down a tower to induce weightlessness, reached 38 picokelvins. But drop tower experiments are limited by the time their free fall lasts. That’s not an issue for experiments in Earth’s orbit. So cold atoms in space are really taking off.
paras.zh: 太空玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚体之前是在国际空间站上制造的，有效温度低至 52 皮开尔文。在地球上进行的一项实验中，原子从塔上掉落以产生失重状态，温度达到了 38 皮开尔文。但落塔实验受到自由落体持续时间的限制。对于地球轨道上的实验来说，这不是问题。所以太空中的冷原子确实正在起飞。

articles.title: A high-fiber diet may clear away plastic in the gut
articles.author: Meghan Rosen

paras.en: Here’s a new reason to eat your beans and greens.
paras.zh: 这是吃豆类和蔬菜的新理由。

paras.en: A high-fiber diet may help sweep plastic particles from the gut, researchers report October 15 in Nature Communications. In mice that ingested plastic, eating loads of fiber daily kept the particles from piling up in the intestines. The finding hints at fiber’s power to protect the body from environmental garbage, says Eddy Y. Zeng, an environmental scientist at South China University of Technology in Guangzhou.
paras.zh: 研究人员 10 月 15 日在《自然通讯》杂志上报道，高纤维饮食可能有助于清除肠道中的塑料颗粒。在摄入塑料的小鼠中，每天摄入大量纤维可以防止颗粒在肠道内堆积。广州华南理工大学环境科学家 Eddy Y. Zeng 表示，这一发现暗示了纤维具有保护人体免受环境垃圾侵害的能力。

paras.en: Researchers have long known that fiber can improve our health, in part by lowering cholesterol, keeping blood sugar levels in check and easing food through the gut. But now, Zeng says, his team’s results suggest an additional benefit.
paras.zh: 研究人员早就知道纤维可以改善我们的健康，部分原因是降低胆固醇、控制血糖水平和促进食物通过肠道。但现在，曾说，他的团队的结果表明了额外的好处。

paras.en: We live in a world littered with plastic, much of it too small to see. These micro and nanoplastics, shed by disposable water bottles, fast food containers and other worldly junk, can make their way into our bodies. It’s not completely clear what such shards do to our health, but we have some hints. Scientists have linked plastic particles in people’s arteries to increased risk of heart attack and stroke. And mice that ingest tiny bits of plastic can show signs of organ injury.
paras.zh: 我们生活在一个充满塑料的世界，其中大部分太小而看不见。这些由一次性水瓶、快餐盒和其他垃圾排出的微米和纳米塑料可以进入我们的身体。目前还不完全清楚这些碎片对我们的健康有何影响，但我们有一些提示。科学家们发现，人们动脉中的塑料颗粒会增加心脏病和中风的风险。摄入微小塑料碎片的老鼠会表现出器官损伤的迹象。

paras.en: Zeng’s team thought dietary fiber might provide some defense. Fiber forms a complex network of polymers that could trap ingested plastics like flies in a spider web, he says.
paras.zh: 曾的团队认为膳食纤维可能提供一些防御作用。他说，纤维形成了一个复杂的聚合物网络，可以像蜘蛛网上的苍蝇一样捕获摄入的塑料。

paras.en: The researchers put mice on low-, medium-, or high-fiber diets, then fed them plastic particles. Over the next 24 hours, the medium- and high-fiber groups of mice cleared more particles from their bodies than their low-fiber counterparts, the team discovered. That’s important, Zeng says, because these particles can do damage. After a week of daily plastic feedings, his team saw gut tissue damage — but only in the low-fiber group. Experiments in test tubes suggest that fiber physically wraps around and sticks to plastic particles.
paras.zh: 研究人员让小鼠吃低纤维、中纤维或高纤维饮食，然后给它们喂食塑料颗粒。研究小组发现，在接下来的 24 小时内，中纤维和高纤维组的小鼠比低纤维组的小鼠从体内清除了更多的颗粒。曾说，这很重要，因为这些颗粒会造成损害。经过一周的每日塑料喂养后，他的团队发现肠道组织受损——但仅限于低纤维组。试管实验表明，纤维以物理方式包裹并粘附在塑料颗粒上。

paras.en: It’s too soon to say if dietary fiber does the same in humans. Zeng’s study was performed in mice and not tethered to realistic fiber numbers. Though mice in the high-fiber group ate far more fiber than what what’s recommended for people, he thinks the findings are worth pursuing in follow-up studies.
paras.zh: 现在判断膳食纤维是否对人类有同样的作用还为时过早。曾的研究是在小鼠身上进行的，不受实际纤维数量的限制。尽管高纤维组的小鼠摄入的纤维远远多于推荐给人们的纤维，但他认为这些发现值得在后续研究中继续下去。

paras.en: And even if fiber doesn’t end up purging plastic from people’s guts, Zeng says, it probably wouldn’t hurt for us to add a little more to our diets.
paras.zh: 曾说，即使纤维最终不能清除人们肠道中的塑料，我们在饮食中多添加一点可能也不会有什么坏处。

articles.title: Drugs like Ozempic may help reverse chronic kidney disease
articles.author: Rachel Fairbank

paras.en: Ozempic’s key ingredient fixes faulty filters in the kidney.
paras.zh: Ozempic 的关键成分可以修复肾脏中出现故障的过滤器。

paras.en: The well-known weight loss drug repairs and restores blood vessels that power people’s waste disposal systems, researchers report October 1 in Nature Medicine. Those actions mean the ingredient, called semaglutide, can add another notch to its list of health benefits: treating chronic kidney disease.
paras.zh: 研究人员 10 月 1 日在《自然医学》杂志上报道称，这种著名的减肥药可以修复和恢复为人们的废物处理系统提供动力的血管。这些作用意味着这种名为索马鲁肽的成分可以在其健康益处清单上再增加一个档次：治疗慢性肾病。

paras.en: In patients with the condition, semaglutide also increased blood flow and tamped down inflammation, the team found. The study reinforces the GLP-1 drug’s known anti-inflammatory effects, while also suggesting that it may play a direct role in protecting the kidney’s blood vessels, says Susan Quaggin, a nephrologist at Northwestern University Feinberg School of Medicine in Chicago who was not involved in the work.
paras.zh: 研究小组发现，对于患有这种疾病的患者，索马鲁肽还可以增加血流量并抑制炎症。芝加哥西北大学范伯格医学院的肾病学家 Susan Quaggin（未参与这项工作）表示，这项研究强化了 GLP-1 药物已知的抗炎作用，同时也表明它可能在保护肾脏血管方面发挥直接作用。

paras.en: Chronic kidney disease affects an estimated 674 million people worldwide, with some of the most common causes being diabetes and high blood pressure. As the disease progresses, the kidneys slowly lose their ability to filter out waste from blood and excrete it as urine. This causes other health complications, as well as a sharply increased risk of dying from a heart attack or stroke.
paras.zh: 据估计，慢性肾病影响着全球 6.74 亿人，其中一些最常见的原因是糖尿病和高血压。随着疾病的进展，肾脏慢慢失去过滤血液中废物并将其作为尿液排出体外的能力。这会导致其他健康并发症，以及死于心脏病或中风的风险急剧增加。

paras.en: Patients with diabetic chronic kidney disease who took semaglutide were less likely to wind up in kidney failure, or die from a heart attack or stroke, than those taking a placebo, researchers reported in 2024 in the New England Journal of Medicine. That trial was stopped early, as the drug was so effective at preventing death that doctors no longer considered it ethical to keep giving participants the placebo.
paras.zh: 研究人员于 2024 年在《新英格兰医学杂志》上报道，与服用安慰剂的患者相比，服用索马鲁肽的糖尿病慢性肾病患者最终出现肾衰竭、死于心脏病或中风的可能性较小。该试验提前停止，因为该药物在预防死亡方面非常有效，以至于医生不再认为继续给参与者服用安慰剂是合乎道德的。

paras.en: For the new study, some of those same researchers then looked at a subset of 106 participants to find out how the drug worked. The team collected kidney tissue samples before and after the participants took semaglutide, and compared them with samples from participants given the placebo. Semaglutide use led to striking visible changes in the tissues, including increased blood flow, reduced scarring and reduced blood vessel stiffness, a measure of vessel health.
paras.zh: 在这项新研究中，其中一些研究人员对 106 名参与者进行了观察，以了解该药物的作用原理。研究小组收集了参与者服用索马鲁肽前后的肾组织样本，并将其与服用安慰剂的参与者的样本进行了比较。索马鲁肽的使用导致组织发生显着的明显变化，包括血流量增加、疤痕减少和血管硬度降低（衡量血管健康的指标）。

paras.en: Increased blood flow is important because it increases filtration, which is the kidneys’ main job, says Peter Nguyen, a nephrologist at Houston Methodist Hospital who was not involved in the study.
paras.zh: 休斯顿卫理公会医院的肾病专家彼得·阮（Peter Nguyen）没有参与这项研究，他说，增加血流量很重要，因为它可以增加过滤，而过滤是肾脏的主要工作。

paras.en: Researchers also looked at levels of a protein, called albumin, in patients’ urine. High levels can be an early sign that the kidneys’ filters aren’t working well. While those levels didn’t change much in those on the placebo, they dropped in patients taking semaglutide ― a sign the filters weren’t quite as leaky any more.
paras.zh: 研究人员还研究了患者尿液中一种称为白蛋白的蛋白质的水平。高水平可能是肾脏过滤器无法正常工作的早期迹象。虽然服用安慰剂的患者的这些水平没有太大变化，但服用索马鲁肽的患者的这些水平有所下降——这表明过滤器不再那么渗漏了。

paras.en: The team then looked under the hood for genetic clues to how semaglutide appeared to heal the kidneys. Within the glomerulus, the tiny blood vessels responsible for the kidney’s filtering action, genes relating to metabolic stress were turned off, Katherine Tuttle, a nephrologist at the University of Washington’s Providence Medical Research Center in Spokane, and colleagues found. Within these same cells, inflammatory genes were also turned off, while repair genes were switched on.
paras.zh: 然后，研究小组深入寻找索马鲁肽如何治愈肾脏的遗传线索。华盛顿大学斯波坎普罗维登斯医学研究中心的肾病学家凯瑟琳·塔特尔及其同事发现，在肾小球内，负责肾脏过滤作用的微小血管、与代谢压力相关的基因被关闭。在这些相同的细胞内，炎症基因也被关闭，而修复基因被打开。

paras.en: The researchers also looked at a subset of genes responsible for cells “talking” to each other within the glomerulus. Before semaglutide, the blood vessels and immune cells were “chattering” with each other, sending lots of inflammatory signals, Tuttle says. After semaglutide, the immune cells went quiet, silencing the messages that ramp up harmful inflammation. These changes in gene activity point to a healthier kidney that’s less stressed and inflamed, and that has had repair processes flipped on.
paras.zh: 研究人员还研究了负责肾小球内细胞相互“交谈”的基因子集。塔特尔说，在索马鲁肽之前，血管和免疫细胞彼此“喋喋不休”，发送大量炎症信号。服用索马鲁肽后，免疫细胞变得安静，消除了加剧有害炎症的信息。这些基因活性的变化表明肾脏更健康，压力和炎症更少，并且修复过程已启动。

paras.en: With semaglutide treatment, Tuttle says, patients’ damaged kidneys showed clear signs of repair.
paras.zh: 塔特尔说，通过索马鲁肽治疗，患者受损的肾脏显示出明显的修复迹象。

articles.title: Pandemic Stress Linked to Faster Epigenetic Aging, But Only in One Generation
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: Stress is much more than just an emotional reaction.
paras.zh: 压力不仅仅是一种情绪反应。

paras.en: When we experience the feeling of stress, it can do things to our bodies, producing a distinct chemical response.
paras.zh: 当我们感受到压力时，它会对我们的身体产生影响，产生独特的化学反应。

paras.en: What's more, physiological responses to stress exposure can speed up our biological aging, and the extent of the acceleration appears to be different for different people.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，对压力暴露的生理反应会加速我们的生物衰老，而且加速的程度对于不同的人来说似乎是不同的。

paras.en: In a new study in PNAS, scientists found new evidence of this variation in biological aging tied to stress, stemming from one of the most universally stressful events of living memory: the COVID-19 pandemic.
paras.zh: 在《美国国家科学院院刊》的一项新研究中，科学家们发现了这种生物衰老变化与压力有关的新证据，这种变化源于生活记忆中最普遍的压力事件之一：COVID-19 大流行。

paras.en: A growing body of research suggests that the stresses of the pandemic rapidly aged people, with the effects appearing to be the most pronounced in young people, with teenagers in particular showing greater indicators of aging after lockdown.
paras.zh: 越来越多的研究表明，大流行的压力使人们迅速衰老，其影响似乎在年轻人中最为明显，尤其是青少年在封锁后表现出更明显的衰老迹象。

paras.en: Now, in what they claim is a first, researchers have found signs of the stress phenomenon in epigenetic data, based on saliva samples from over 1,000 people in Germany, measuring age-related changes in DNA methylation using four different kinds of epigenetic clocks.
paras.zh: 现在，研究人员声称，他们首次在表观遗传数据中发现了压力现象的迹象，这些数据基于德国 1000 多人的唾液样本，并使用四种不同的表观遗传时钟测量了与年龄相关的 DNA 甲基化变化。

paras.en: In the study, the researchers analyzed data from the TwinLife Epigenetic Change Satellite (TECS) project, which collected saliva samples from children (aged approximately 8–10), adolescents (14–16), and adults (20–29) before the first German lockdown in March 2020, and then again in 2021–2022, after the country emerged from its second national lockdown.
paras.zh: 在这项研究中，研究人员分析了来自 TwinLife 表观遗传变化卫星 (TECS) 项目的数据，该项目在 2020 年 3 月德国第一次封锁之前收集了儿童（约 8-10 岁）、青少年（14-16 岁）和成人（20-29 岁）的唾液样本，然后在德国第二次全国封锁结束后的 2021-2022 年再次收集了唾液样本。

paras.en: "We leveraged this design in which the COVID-19 pandemic constituted a natural experiment occurring between repeated assessments and, thus, were able to test whether a major, globally shared stressor was associated with detectable epigenetic changes," the researchers explain in their paper, led by first author and neuroscientist Alicia Schowe from the Max Planck Institute of Psychiatry in Munich.
paras.zh: 研究人员在由第一作者、慕尼黑马克斯·普朗克精神病学研究所的神经科学家 Alicia Schowe 领导的论文中解释道：“我们利用了这种设计，其中 COVID-19 大流行构成了重复评估之间发生的自然实验，因此能够测试全球共享的主要压力源是否与可检测的表观遗传变化相关。”

paras.en: While the results varied, measurements from three of the four epigenetic clocks found a significant increase in age acceleration or pace of aging from the pre-pandemic baseline in the full sample, with the clocks PedBE, GrimAge2, and DunedinPACE each finding increases in two age groups (PedBE was only used for children and adolescents).
paras.zh: 虽然结果各不相同，但四个表观遗传时钟中的三个的测量结果发现，在整个样本中，年龄加速或衰老速度较大流行前基线显着增加，其中 PedBE、GrimAge2 和 DunedinPACE 时钟均发现两个年龄组的年龄加速或衰老速度增加（PedBE 仅用于儿童和青少年）。

paras.en: Only one of the epigenetic clocks found faster aging in children, which the researchers suggest could be related to sensitivity issues with the other clocks used, as the systems might not be adequately calibrated to children.
paras.zh: 只有其中一种表观遗传时钟发现儿童衰老得更快，研究人员认为这可能与所使用的其他时钟的敏感性问题有关，因为这些系统可能没有针对儿童进行充分校准。

paras.en: Interestingly, however, when the researchers compared the epigenetic results with participants' self-reported experiences of the pandemic, only one age group showed a link between perceived stress and accelerated biological aging: the adolescents.
paras.zh: 然而有趣的是，当研究人员将表观遗传学结果与参与者自我报告的大流行经历进行比较时，只有一个年龄组显示出感知压力和加速生物衰老之间的联系：青少年。

paras.en: "This suggests that adolescence may be a time period that is especially sensitive to the effects of stress," Schowe says.
paras.zh: “这表明青春期可能是对压力影响特别敏感的时期，”绍说。

paras.en: "This could be due to the changes happening in the body during puberty, or because lockdown measures, like restrictions on seeing peers, had a particularly strong impact on this age group."
paras.zh: “这可能是由于青春期身体发生的变化，或者是因为限制与同龄人见面等封锁措施对这个年龄段的影响特别大。”

paras.en: Among adolescents, those who felt more burdened by restrictions on their freedoms and separation from important people in their lives showed stronger signs of accelerated biological aging, although the associations varied depending on which epigenetic clock was used.
paras.zh: 在青少年中，那些因自由受到限制和与生活中重要人物分离而感到负担更重的人表现出更强烈的生物加速加速迹象，尽管这种关联因使用的表观遗传时钟而异。

paras.en: Beyond the stress burden faced by adolescents, the strongest overall links to accelerated epigenetic aging across all age groups were factors related to physical health: higher body mass index (BMI) and smoking exposure.
paras.zh: 除了青少年面临的压力负担之外，与所有年龄段的表观遗传加速衰老最密切的总体联系是与身体健康相关的因素：较高的体重指数（BMI）和吸烟暴露。

paras.en: "Accordingly, observed increases in sedentary lifestyle and weight gain during the pandemic may also partly account for the observed increases in GrimAge2 and DunedinPACE in the overall sample, alongside psychosocial burden in adolescents," the researchers write.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“因此，在大流行期间观察到的久坐生活方式和体重增加的增加也可能部分解释了在整个样本中观察到的 GrimAge2 和 DunedinPACE 的增加，以及青少年的社会心理负担。”

paras.en: "Long-term follow-up will be needed to confirm whether these changes persist and predict adverse health outcomes later in life."
paras.zh: “需要进行长期随访，以确认这些变化是否持续存在，并预测以后生活中的不良健康结果。”

articles.title: Study Identifies The #1 Issue Affecting The Academic Performance of US College Students
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: A college education is a life-changing experience, but nobody said it was easy.
paras.zh: 大学教育是一次改变人生的经历，但没有人说这很容易。

paras.en: On top of all the studying, you need to make sure you get enough sleep, figure out how to block distractions, and find ways to handle academic stress.
paras.zh: 除了学习之外，你还需要确保有足够的睡眠，找出如何排除干扰，并找到应对学业压力的方法。

paras.en: Even if you do all that, let's face it, thinking is hard.
paras.zh: 即使你做到了这一切，让我们面对现实吧，思考是很困难的。

paras.en: But if you ask college students about the challenges they face, one particular problem seems to overshadow all those other issues – and it's an internal struggle that basically anybody can relate to.
paras.zh: 但如果你问大学生他们面临的挑战，一个特定的问题似乎掩盖了所有其他问题——这是一种基本上任何人都可以体会到的内部斗争。

paras.en: In a new study in PLOS One, social scientist Itamar Shatz from the University of Cambridge analyzed survey responses from over 65,000 college students at almost 100 academic institutions across the US.
paras.zh: 在 PLOS One 的一项新研究中，剑桥大学的社会科学家 Itamar Shatz 分析了美国近 100 个学术机构的 65,000 多名大学生的调查回复。

paras.en: Students were asked whether they had experienced problems or challenges with various types of issues in the last 12 months, with the survey specifically questioning them about 36 different kinds of life-related and health-related issues.
paras.zh: 调查询问学生在过去12个月内是否遇到过各类问题或挑战，调查具体询问了他们36种不同的与生活和健康相关的问题。

paras.en: Students indicated the biggest issue causing problems with their academic performance was procrastination, with 45.4 percent of the survey respondents saying procrastination affected their academic results, followed by stress (36.6 percent), anxiety (30.4 percent), sleep difficulties (22 percent), and depression (20 percent).
paras.zh: 学生们表示，导致学业成绩出现问题的最大问题是拖延，45.4%的受访者表示拖延影响了他们的学业成绩，其次是压力（36.6%）、焦虑（30.4%）、睡眠困难（22%）和抑郁（20%）。

paras.en: Procrastination was also identified as the most common cause of significant distress compared to other life issues, with the tendency affecting 45.7 percent of students, which was higher than academic issues (38.9 percent), personal appearance (31.8 percent), finances (30.8 percent), and career (29.6 percent).
paras.zh: 与其他生活问题相比，拖延症也被认为是导致严重困扰的最常见原因，这种倾向影响了 45.7% 的学生，高于学业问题 (38.9%)、个人外表问题 (31.8%)、财务问题 (30.8%) 和职业问题 (29.6%)。

paras.en: Among all the 36 issues raised with students, procrastination was effectively tied with stress as the most prevalent issue overall, reported by 72.3 percent and 73.8 percent of respondents, respectively. Stress was marginally more common, but Shatz says the figures were close enough to be considered a functional tie.
paras.zh: 在学生提出的 36 个问题中，拖延与压力实际上是最普遍的问题，分别有 72.3% 和 73.8% 的受访者表示。压力稍微更常见，但沙茨表示，这些数字足够接近，可以被视为功能性联系。

paras.en: While procrastination had the biggest impact across all students, Shatz notes that its top ranking partly reflects how common it is. When each issue was measured only among the students who had it, procrastination wasn't always the one most likely to affect academic performance.
paras.zh: 沙茨指出，虽然拖延症对所有学生的影响最大，但其排名最高部分反映了拖延症的普遍性。当每个问题都只在有问题的学生中进行衡量时，拖延症并不总是最有可能影响学业成绩的问题。

paras.en: One exception was ADHD, which 12.9 percent of respondents overall reported as affecting their academic performance. Among students who experienced ADHD, 64.1 percent said it affected their academic performance, compared to 62.7 percent of students who experienced procrastination.
paras.zh: 一个例外是注意力缺陷多动症（ADHD），12.9% 的受访者总体报告称其影响了他们的学业成绩。在患有多动症的学生中，64.1% 的学生表示这影响了他们的学习成绩，而有拖延症的学生中这一比例为 62.7%。

paras.en: But ADHD ranked lower overall because far fewer students reported it (20.2 percent, compared with 72.3 percent for procrastination).
paras.zh: 但注意力缺陷多动症总体排名较低，因为报告该问题的学生少得多（20.2%，而拖延症的学生为 72.3%）。

paras.en: It's also worth acknowledging that many of the issues students were asked about overlap with others, and may even feed one another.
paras.zh: 还值得承认的是，学生们被问到的许多问题与其他问题重叠，甚至可能互相影响。

paras.en: "Stress, for instance, was a top issue, but procrastination was a top cause of distress, and procrastination itself can be caused or exacerbated by this and other issues, like anxiety and lack of sleep," Shatz explains.
paras.zh: “例如，压力是一个首要问题，但拖延是造成痛苦的首要原因，拖延本身可能是由这个问题和其他问题引起或加剧的，比如焦虑和睡眠不足，”沙茨解释道。

paras.en: "An example of such a feedback loop is a student procrastinating on a task, which causes them to feel stressed, which interferes with their sleep, which causes them to procrastinate on the task further."
paras.zh: “这种反馈循环的一个例子是学生拖延一项任务，这会让他们感到压力，从而干扰他们的睡眠，从而导致他们进一步拖延任务。”

paras.en: On top of that, a survey like this can only give us a collection of people's self-reported judgments, and it doesn't actually measure or track how each problem affects students' actual grades.
paras.zh: 最重要的是，这样的调查只能为我们提供人们自我报告的判断的集合，而它并不能真正衡量或跟踪每个问题如何影响学生的实际成绩。

paras.en: But despite the limitations of the study, there's a very clear signal here that procrastination is the most widely reported obstacle to academic performance among college students, and that's a signal we ought to pay attention to.
paras.zh: 尽管这项研究存在局限性，但这里有一个非常明显的信号，即拖延是大学生中最广泛报道的学业表现障碍，这是我们应该关注的信号。

paras.en: "It may be insufficient to simply think of procrastination as a big issue among students," Shatz writes.
paras.zh: 沙茨写道：“仅仅将拖延视为学生中的一个大问题可能还不够。”

paras.en: "Rather, it seems plausible that procrastination is the biggest issue on average, at least in terms of its impact on students' academic performance."
paras.zh: “相反，拖延似乎是平均而言最大的问题，至少就其对学生学业成绩的影响而言是这样。”

paras.en: The effects of the problem may extend well after graduation, too, with research suggesting procrastination could ultimately have a marked effect on people's careers and income levels.
paras.zh: 这个问题的影响也可能在毕业后持续很长一段时间，研究表明拖延症最终可能会对人们的职业和收入水平产生显着影响。

paras.en: A 2013 study on procrastination in the workplace found that each one-point increase on a five-point procrastination scale was linked to approximately US$15,000 less income on average, with researchers suggesting that procrastination could be the most important personality trait linked with income (though perhaps second to agreeableness).
paras.zh: 2013 年的一项关于工作场所拖延症的研究发现，拖延症 5 分制中，每增加 1 分，平均收入就会减少约 15,000 美元，研究人员认为，拖延症可能是与收入相关的最重要的人格特质（尽管可能仅次于宜人性）。

paras.en: "This, in turn, suggests that the harmful effects of procrastination persist after students finish their schooling," Shatz explains, "whether because students' academic struggles interfered with their ability to get certain roles in a competitive job market, because procrastination continues to interfere with graduates' ability to advance in the workplace, or because of some other combination of mechanisms."
paras.zh: 沙茨解释说：“这反过来表明，拖延的有害影响在学生完成学业后仍然存在，无论是因为学生的学业困难影响了他们在竞争激烈的就业市场中获得某些角色的能力，还是因为拖延继续影响毕业生在工作场所的晋升能力，或者是因为其他一些机制的组合。”

articles.title: Scientists Find a Way to Grow a Thicker And Fuller Mustache in Just 8 Weeks
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: A popular drug that is commonly used for hair loss may also help someone grow a thicker beard or mustache.
paras.zh: 一种常用于治疗脱发的流行药物也可能有助于人们长出更浓密的胡须或小胡子。

paras.en: Minoxidil was first developed as an oral medication for high blood pressure in the 1970s, yet, unexpectedly, the drug also appeared to stimulate hair growth.
paras.zh: 米诺地尔在 20 世纪 70 年代首次被开发为治疗高血压的口服药物，但出乎意料的是，该药物似乎还可以刺激头发生长。

paras.en: In 1988, a topical version was approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for treating male-pattern hair loss, marketed as Rogaine.
paras.zh: 1988 年，美国食品和药物管理局 (FDA) 批准了一种外用版本用于治疗男性型脱发，商品名为落健 (Rogaine)。

paras.en: A few years later, the treatment was approved for female pattern hair loss, too.
paras.zh: 几年后，这种疗法也被批准用于治疗女性型脱发。

paras.en: For years now, patients and physicians alike have wondered: If Rogaine stimulates hair growth on the scalp, could it also work 'off-label' for facial hair, too?
paras.zh: 多年来，患者和医生都想知道：如果落建能刺激头皮上的毛发生长，那么它是否也能“超出说明书”地治疗面部毛发呢？

paras.en: A recent randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial among transgender men now suggests the answer is yes.
paras.zh: 最近一项针对跨性别男性的随机、双盲、安慰剂对照试验表明答案是肯定的。

paras.en: The findings join a previous study among cisgender men, published in 2016, which was the first to show that topical 3 percent minoxidil can improve beard growth compared to a placebo.
paras.zh: 这一发现与 2016 年发表的一项针对顺性别男性的研究相结合，该研究首次表明，与安慰剂相比，外用 3% 的米诺地尔可以改善胡须生长。

paras.en: The results also support a number of case studies and a growing online community that advocates for minoxidil as a possible way to make facial hair fuller and thicker.
paras.zh: 研究结果还支持了许多案例研究和不断增长的在线社区，该社区主张使用米诺地尔作为使面部毛发更浓密更浓密的一种可能方法。

paras.en: The recent experiments were conducted at Mahidol University in Bangkok, Thailand, and provide some of the best evidence yet that minoxidil works safely on the face in a similar way to the scalp.
paras.zh: 最近的实验是在泰国曼谷玛希隆大学进行的，并提供了一些迄今为止最好的证据，表明米诺地尔在面部的安全作用与头皮类似。

paras.en: The findings are published in The Journal of Dermatological Treatment.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在《皮肤病治疗杂志》上。

paras.en: For the trial, 34 participants receiving gender affirming hormone therapy were randomized to use topical minoxidil (3 percent) twice daily on their faces for 12 weeks, while another 35 participants used a placebo.
paras.zh: 在该试验中，34 名接受性别肯定激素治疗的参与者被随机分配，每天两次在脸上局部使用米诺地尔 (3%)，持续 12 周，而另外 35 名参与者则使用安慰剂。

paras.en: At 8 weeks, those taking minoxidil had denser, thicker facial hair than the placebo group.
paras.zh: 第 8 周时，服用米诺地尔的受试者比安慰剂组的面部毛发更浓密、更浓密。

paras.en: At 12 weeks, the minoxidil group showed a roughly 17 percent increase in mustache density and a 15 percent increase in beard density from baseline.
paras.zh: 第 12 周时，米诺地尔组的胡须密度较基线增加了约 17%，胡须密度增加了 15%。

paras.en: Many participants also reported greater quality of life and higher satisfaction scores.
paras.zh: 许多参与者还表示生活质量更高，满意度更高。

paras.en: Side effects like itching, red skin, and flakiness were minimal, and no serious adverse events were reported.
paras.zh: 瘙痒、皮肤发红和脱皮等副作用很小，并且没有报告严重的不良事件。

paras.en: What's more, the blood pressure of participants remained stable throughout.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，参与者的血压自始至终保持稳定。

paras.en: "Topical 3 percent minoxidil represents an effective, safe, and well-tolerated adjunctive treatment for facial hair enhancement in transgender men receiving gender-affirming hormone therapy," conclude the authors of the study, led by dermatologist Kantarat Wattanawinitchai.
paras.zh: 皮肤科医生 Kantarat Wattanawinitchai 领导的这项研究的作者总结道：“对于接受性别肯定激素治疗的跨性别男性来说，外用 3% 米诺地尔是一种有效、安全且耐受性良好的辅助治疗方法，可以增强面部毛发。”

paras.en: "The excellent safety profile observed is reassuring, particularly given theoretical concerns about systemic absorption."
paras.zh: “观察到的出色的安全性令人放心，特别是考虑到理论上对全身吸收的担忧。”

paras.en: After all, minoxidil is a known blood vessel dilator, and if enough of the drug is absorbed, it could theoretically cause dizziness, low blood pressure, rapid heartbeat, or palpitations.
paras.zh: 毕竟，米诺地尔是一种已知的血管扩张剂，如果吸收足够的药物，理论上它可能会导致头晕、低血压、心跳加快或心悸。

paras.en: The current research is based on transgender men, so it is unclear if the results also apply to other groups.
paras.zh: 目前的研究是基于跨性别男性，因此尚不清楚结果是否也适用于其他群体。

paras.en: It's possible, for instance, that ongoing testosterone therapy produces a synergistic effect with minoxidil, leading to greater hair growth over a shorter time period.
paras.zh: 例如，持续的睾酮疗法可能与米诺地尔产生协同效应，导致头发在更短的时间内生长得更快。

paras.en: But there are several other intriguing case studies that suggest minoxidil could work for the facial hair of cisgender men, too.
paras.zh: 但还有其他几个有趣的案例研究表明米诺地尔也可以治疗顺性别男性的面部毛发。

paras.en: One of the most compelling reports is of two male identical twins, one of whom used topical 5% minoxidil for over a year on the beard and mustache area.
paras.zh: 最引人注目的报告之一是关于两个男性同卵双胞胎，其中一个在胡须区域局部使用 5% 米诺地尔超过一年。

paras.en: Compared to the twin who didn't use the drug, the one who did showed greater hair count and density in both the beard and mustache areas after 16 months.
paras.zh: 与未使用该药物的双胞胎相比，16 个月后，使用该药物的双胞胎胡须区域的毛发数量和密度都更高。

paras.en: Research is still in the early stages, and topical minoxidil is not yet approved by the US FDA for facial hair in any group.
paras.zh: 研究仍处于早期阶段，美国 FDA 尚未批准外用米诺地尔用于任何人群的面部毛发。

paras.en: That said, the drug is sometimes recommended off-label for certain patients.
paras.zh: 也就是说，有时会在标签外推荐该药物给某些患者。

paras.en: Based on these results, researchers in Thailand argue that "minoxidil should be considered as a first-line adjunctive treatment for transgender men who experience incomplete or unsatisfactory facial hair development despite adequate testosterone therapy."
paras.zh: 基于这些结果，泰国的研究人员认为，“对于尽管接受了足够的睾酮治疗，但面部毛发发育不完全或不满意的变性男性，米诺地尔应被视为一线辅助治疗。”

paras.en: "Despite the masculinizing effects of testosterone therapy, facial hair development often remains incomplete or unsatisfactory for many transgender men," the research team explains.
paras.zh: 研究小组解释说：“尽管睾酮疗法具有男性化作用，但对于许多跨性别男性来说，面部毛发的发育通常仍然不完整或不令人满意。”

paras.en: "This discrepancy between expectation and outcome can perpetuate gender dysphoria and negatively impact quality of life.
paras.zh: “期望和结果之间的这种差异可能会导致性别焦虑持续存在，并对生活质量产生负面影响。

paras.en: For others, the benefits are less certain.
paras.zh: 对于其他人来说，好处不太确定。

paras.en: The American Academy of Dermatology warns that before trying minoxidil to enhance facial hair, it is wise to consult a dermatologist.
paras.zh: 美国皮肤病学会警告说，在尝试使用米诺地尔来增强面部毛发之前，明智的做法是咨询皮肤科医生。

paras.en: "When people use minoxidil to help them grow hair on their face, a common side effect is raw, irritated skin," the site explains.
paras.zh: 该网站解释说：“当人们使用米诺地尔帮助脸上长出毛发时，常见的副作用是皮肤粗糙、发炎。”

paras.en: "A dermatologist can offer you treatment options for growing facial hair."
paras.zh: “皮肤科医生可以为您提供面部毛发生长的治疗选择。”

paras.en: The research has been published in The Journal of Dermatological Treatment.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《皮肤病治疗杂志》上。

articles.title: A quantum breakthrough makes light behave like both a solid and a liquid

paras.en: A quantum breakthrough makes light behave like both a solid and a liquid
paras.zh: 量子突破使光表现得既像固体又像液体

paras.en: - University of Warsaw, Faculty of Physics
paras.zh: - 华沙大学物理学院

paras.en: - Scientists have observed a bizarre quantum state of matter that combines the structure of a crystal with the frictionless flow of a liquid, all at room temperature. The breakthrough overturns a major practical limitation of exotic quantum experiments and could help bring powerful new light-based computing and sensing technologies closer to reality.
paras.zh: - 科学家观察到一种奇怪的物质量子态，它在室温下将晶体结构与液体无摩擦流动结合在一起。这一突破推翻了奇异量子实验的主要实际限制，有助于使强大的新型光计算和传感技术更接近现实。

paras.en: Scientists have demonstrated an extraordinary form of quantum matter that combines two properties that seem incompatible. Known as a supersolid, this unusual state has the orderly structure of a crystal while also displaying the frictionless flow associated with a special kind of liquid. Even more remarkably, researchers have now observed this behavior at room temperature, eliminating the need for the extreme cooling traditionally used to investigate such phenomena.
paras.zh: 科学家们展示了一种非凡的量子物质形式，它结合了两种看似不相容的特性。这种不寻常的状态被称为超固体，具有晶体的有序结构，同时还表现出与特殊液体相关的无摩擦流动。更值得注意的是，研究人员现在已经在室温下观察到了这种行为，从而消除了传统上用于研究此类现象的极端冷却的需要。

paras.en: The breakthrough was achieved by an international team from the Faculty of Physics at the University of Warsaw, the Military University of Technology (Poland), IBM Research Zurich, and the French National Centre for Scientific Research (CNRS). Rather than relying on atoms cooled to temperatures near absolute zero, the scientists created a supersolid using particles that combine properties of light and matter.
paras.zh: 这一突破是由来自华沙大学物理系、军事工业大学（波兰）、IBM 苏黎世研究院和法国国家科学研究中心 (CNRS) 的国际团队实现的。科学家们没有依靠冷却到接近绝对零温度的原子，而是利用结合了光和物质特性的粒子创造了一种超固体。

paras.en: Published in Science Advances, the findings introduce a new way to investigate exotic quantum behavior under much more accessible conditions. They could also help advance future technologies ranging from optical computing to highly sensitive sensors.
paras.zh: 该研究结果发表在《科学进展》上，提出了一种在更容易实现的条件下研究奇异量子行为的新方法。它们还可以帮助推进从光学计算到高灵敏度传感器等未来技术。

paras.en: How Can Matter Behave Like Both a Solid and a Liquid?
paras.zh: 物质如何表现得既像固体又像液体？

paras.en: Under ordinary circumstances, solids and liquids behave very differently. Crystals have an organized internal structure, with their particles arranged in repeating patterns. Liquids, by comparison, can flow and change shape.
paras.zh: 在一般情况下，固体和液体的行为非常不同。晶体具有有序的内部结构，其颗粒以重复的图案排列。相比之下，液体可以流动并改变形状。

paras.en: Quantum physics, however, allows matter to behave in ways that would be impossible under the familiar rules of everyday life.
paras.zh: 然而，量子物理学允许物质以日常生活中熟悉的规则不可能的方式表现。

paras.en: One example is superfluidity, a remarkable phenomenon in which a fluid loses its viscosity, or internal resistance to flowing. A superfluid can move through extremely narrow passages without experiencing the usual friction. Imagine placing an oar into such a liquid. You would encounter almost no resistance until the oar reached a certain speed. Beyond that threshold, tiny swirling structures known as quantum vortices would suddenly form.
paras.zh: 一个例子是超流动性，这是一种显着的现象，其中流体失去粘度或流动的内部阻力。超流体可以穿过极其狭窄的通道而不会经历通常的摩擦。想象一下将桨放入这样的液体中。在桨达到一定速度之前，你几乎不会遇到任何阻力。超过这个阈值，被称为量子涡旋的微小漩涡结构就会突然形成。

paras.en: During the 1960s, physicists proposed an even stranger possibility. What if a superfluid could also develop the repeating internal structure normally associated with a crystal?
paras.zh: 20 世纪 60 年代，物理学家提出了一种更奇怪的可能性。如果超流体也能形成通常与晶体相关的重复内部结构呢？

paras.en: This hypothetical combination became known as a supersolid. In such a state, the material exhibits the spatial organization of a solid while retaining the remarkable flow properties of a superfluid.
paras.zh: 这种假设的组合被称为超固体。在这种状态下，材料表现出固体的空间组织，同时保留超流体的显着流动特性。

paras.en: For decades, supersolidity remained a theoretical concept. Experimental confirmation finally arrived in 2017, when researchers observed the phenomenon in ultracold atomic Bose-Einstein condensates. These condensates form when particles enter a collective quantum state and begin behaving as a coordinated system rather than as separate individuals.
paras.zh: 几十年来，超固体仍然是一个理论概念。 2017 年，研究人员在超冷原子玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚体中观察到了这一现象，最终得到了实验证实。当粒子进入集体量子态并开始表现为协调系统而不是单独的个体时，这些凝聚体就会形成。

paras.en: The catch was that producing these conditions generally required sophisticated equipment capable of cooling matter to temperatures extremely close to absolute zero, the lowest possible temperature.
paras.zh: 问题是，产生这些条件通常需要复杂的设备，能够将物质冷却到极其接近绝对零的温度，即可能的最低温度。

paras.en: Creating a Quantum Supersolid Using Light Instead of Cold Atoms
paras.zh: 使用光而不是冷原子创建量子超固体

paras.en: The international TopoLight consortium approached the challenge from a different direction. Instead of using ultracold atoms, the researchers worked with unusual hybrid particles called exciton polaritons.
paras.zh: 国际 TopoLight 联盟从不同的方向应对这一挑战。研究人员没有使用超冷原子，而是使用了称为激子极化激元的不寻常的混合粒子。

paras.en: These quasiparticles arise when light interacts so strongly with matter that the two become coupled inside a tiny optical chamber called a microcavity. The resulting particles display characteristics of both light and matter.
paras.zh: 当光与物质相互作用如此强烈，以致两者在称为微腔的微小光学室内耦合时，就会产生这些准粒子。产生的粒子显示出光和物质的特征。

paras.en: Exciton polaritons are extremely short-lived, typically surviving for only a few picoseconds. A picosecond is one trillionth of a second. Despite their brief existence, these particles can organize into a Bose-Einstein condensate and collectively exhibit the behavior of a quantum superfluid.
paras.zh: 激子极化激元的寿命极短，通常只能存活几皮秒。一皮秒是一万亿分之一秒。尽管存在时间很短，但这些粒子可以组织成玻色-爱因斯坦凝聚体，并共同表现出量子超流体的行为。

paras.en: To create the necessary conditions, the team constructed an optical microcavity containing a specially engineered liquid crystal and covered it with an organic semiconductor. The arrangement allowed light and matter to interact strongly enough to produce the desired quantum effects without the need for extreme cooling.
paras.zh: 为了创造必要的条件，该团队构建了一个包含特殊设计的液晶的光学微腔，并用有机半导体覆盖它。这种布置允许光和物质发生足够强烈的相互作用，以产生所需的量子效应，而不需要极度冷却。

paras.en: "Our liquid-crystal microcavities can operate even at temperatures approaching 60°C," says Professor Wiktor Piecek from the Military University of Technology, whose group developed the liquid-crystal structures.
paras.zh: “我们的液晶微腔甚至可以在接近 60°C 的温度下工作，”军事科技大学的 Wiktor Piecek 教授说，他的团队开发了液晶结构。

paras.en: That temperature is approximately 140°F, far above the freezing conditions normally associated with experiments involving exotic quantum matter.
paras.zh: 该温度约为 140°F，远高于通常与涉及奇异量子物质的实验相关的冰点条件。

paras.en: Strange Patterns of Light Reveal a Supersolid
paras.zh: 奇怪的光图案揭示了超固体

paras.en: How can researchers determine whether a collection of particles has entered such an unusual state?
paras.zh: 研究人员如何确定一组粒子是否已进入如此不寻常的状态？

paras.en: In this experiment, the evidence appeared in the light emitted by the sample. When the system transitioned into the supersolid phase, researchers observed a series of regularly spaced bright fringes.
paras.zh: 在这个实验中，证据出现在样品发出的光中。当系统转变为超固体相时，研究人员观察到一系列规则间隔的明亮条纹。

paras.en: These patterns indicated that the particle condensate had spontaneously developed a repeating variation in its density. This type of spatial organization is a defining feature of crystalline structures and an important sign of supersolidity.
paras.zh: 这些图案表明颗粒凝聚物的密度自发地出现重复变化。这种类型的空间组织是晶体结构的定义特征，也是超固体的重要标志。

paras.en: But the researchers noticed another intriguing effect.
paras.zh: 但研究人员注意到了另一个有趣的效应。

paras.en: Each time a laser pulse excited the sample, the bright fringes appeared in a different position. Rather than following a single fixed arrangement, the quantum system repeatedly selected among several equally possible configurations.
paras.zh: 每次激光脉冲激发样品时，明亮的条纹就会出现在不同的位置。量子系统不是遵循单一的固定排列，而是在几种同等可能的配置中重复选择。

paras.en: "This is a textbook example of spontaneous symmetry breaking," explains Professor Guillaume Malpuech from Institut Pascal (CNRS). "Theory predicted that the supersolid could choose among several equivalent states, and that is exactly what we observed."
paras.zh: “这是自发对称破缺的教科书例子，”帕斯卡研究所（CNRS）的 Guillaume Malpuech 教授解释道。 “理论预测超固体可以在几种等效状态之间进行选择，这正是我们所观察到的。”

paras.en: Spontaneous symmetry breaking occurs when a system that could exist in several equivalent arrangements settles into one particular configuration. In this case, the effect became visible through the changing positions of the light patterns.
paras.zh: 当一个可能存在于几种等效排列中的系统陷入一种特定的配置时，就会发生自发对称性破缺。在这种情况下，通过改变光图案的位置，效果变得可见。

paras.en: The condensate also displayed another unusual characteristic called a persistent spin helix. This refers to a repeating variation in the polarization of the emitted light. Polarization describes the orientation of light's oscillating electric field.
paras.zh: 凝聚物还表现出另一种不寻常的特征，称为持续自旋螺旋。这是指发射光的偏振的重复变化。偏振描述了光振荡电场的方向。

paras.en: Together, these observations revealed two different forms of order occurring at the same time. One appeared in the intensity of the emitted light, while the other appeared in its polarization.
paras.zh: 这些观察结果共同揭示了同时发生的两种不同形式的秩序。一个表现为发射光的强度，而另一个表现为其偏振。

paras.en: A Difficult Experiment With Only Hours to Succeed
paras.zh: 一个艰难的实验，只有几个小时才能成功

paras.en: Achieving these results required overcoming an unexpected practical obstacle.
paras.zh: 实现这些成果需要克服意想不到的实际障碍。
