articles.title: Actually, You Can Go Back to Constantinople. A Landmark Exhibition Reconstructs the Imperial City With 1,600 Years of Treasures From Byzantine and Ottoman Times

paras.en: Napoleon Bonaparte once supposedly declared Constantinople to be “the empire of the world.” From its founding as the capital of the Byzantine Empire under Roman emperor Constantine in the 4th century C.E. until the fall of the Ottoman Empire in the 1920s, the city today known as Istanbul was indeed the epicenter of two successive, world-defining civilizations.

The city’s role in that sweeping, nearly 1,600-year saga is the focus of “Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires,” a major exhibition at London’s Victoria and Albert Museum. Opening November 7, the exhibition unites more than 200 rare objects from Byzantine and Ottoman times.
“Creating this exhibition has been an exciting adventure, bringing together two worlds that are usually kept well apart,” Tim Stanley, the exhibition’s curator, says in a statement.

“The artistic ideas generated there in its double history as an imperial capital still play a major role in the world,” he adds. “By combining the stories of these two empires and the amazing art they both produced, we have been able to release the stories of Constantinople and Istanbul from their separate boxes and let them enjoy the limelight together.”

The exhibition unfolds across four chronological sections: “Roman Beginnings,” charting the city’s imperial origins; “Heaven and Earth,” exploring monumental sacred architecture; “A Capital Reborn,” examining the Ottoman imperial court’s role in artmaking; and “Life in the City,” capturing the vibrant, multi-ethnic metropolis of the 19th century.

The journey begins in 330 C.E., when Constantine selected the former Greek settlement of Byzantium as an eastern counterpart to Rome. Among the early relics is a bronze serpent head from the famous Serpent Column, which Constantine relocated directly from Delphi to furnish the city’s central hippodrome.

At the hippodrome, Romans “thronged in their thousands to cheer on the chariot racers and wolf whistle dancing girls as they performed lascivious burlesques,” Peter Sarris, a historian at the University of Cambridge, writes in the London Times. One such dancer, Sarris points out, was Theodora, the future wife of the Byzantine emperor Justinian.

In the sixth century, Justinian commissioned the Hagia Sophia, a spellbindingly large cathedral that was built in less than six years and served as the religious core of the East Roman world. When envoys sent by Vladimir the Great, the pagan Grand Prince of Kyiv, visited the Hagia Sophia in the 10th century, they were so mesmerized by its grandeur that they “knew not whether [they] were in heaven or earth.”

The exhibition assembles a “rich range of liturgical objects” from the cathedral and beyond, per the statement. One rare object on view is the Lincoln Typikon, an illuminated, 14th-century manuscript from a Constantinople nunnery, on loan from Lincoln College, Oxford, for the first time in six decades, the Art Newspaper’s Gareth Harris reports. The typikon’s delicate illustrations of the convent of the Virgin of Sure Hope offer a vivid window into monastic life just a century before the capital’s fall.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: After the Ottomans conquered Constantinople in 1453, the city’s new rulers both honored and transformed their new domain. Sultan Mehmet II converted Hagia Sophia into a mosque while intentionally retaining its original name, turning the ancient Christian monument into the aesthetic blueprint for grand Islamic architecture across the capital.
- The Byzantine Empire used religious art, such as portable icons and jeweled reliquaries, to bolster geopolitical alliances.

- One standout example is Saint Lawrence’s Pallium, a lavish 13th-century silk depiction of the patron saint of Genoa guiding Byzantine emperor Michael VIII into a strategic pact with the Genoese. Michael gifted the Genoese this cloth to seal the deal.

The transition to Ottoman splendor is heralded by Gentile Bellini’s 1480 portrait of Mehmet II, reflecting a court hungry for Renaissance artistry. The later imperial rooms showcase opulent displays of secular and military authority. Among them are a 30-foot-long, 17th-century processional scroll illustrating the sultan’s elaborate palace retinue, a silk kaftan woven with shimmering gold thread and a pair of gold pistols presented by the Ottoman court to Britain’s King George III, per the Telegraph’s Alastair Sooke.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The exhibition concludes away from royal palaces, diving into the lively social spaces of the 19th-century city of Istanbul through depictions of buzzing coffee houses, literary salons and public bathhouses.
“This is a sumptuous voyage to Byzantium via Istanbul,” Jonathan Jones writes for the Guardian. “Linger in the baths, in your tall wooden shoes and silk towel, and enjoy the artifice of eternity.”
“Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires” is on view at the V&A South Kensington in London from November 7, 2026, to May 9, 2027.

articles.title: It's Not Just You: Some Fast-Flying Birds Also Get Jet Lag

paras.en: Traveling rapidly across multiple time zones often throws our internal clocks out of whack. But new research suggests jet lag is not unique to humans—some birds may also experience it.
paras.zh: 快速穿越多个时区通常会使我们的内部时钟失灵。但新的研究表明，时差并不是人类独有的--一些鸟类也可能会经历时差。

paras.en: A new study published October 29 in the journal Science finds that the internal clocks of Manx shearwaters can get out of sync with local time because the birds fly so fast. These jet lag-like time shifts confuse their sun-based compasses, and cause them to become slightly disoriented and fly a little off course.
paras.zh: 10月29日发表在《科学》杂志上的一项新研究发现，马恩岛剪水河的内部时钟可能与当地时间不同步，因为鸟类飞得太快了。这些时差般的时差混淆了它们基于太阳的罗盘，使它们变得稍微迷失方向，并稍微偏离航线。

paras.en: Black on top and white on bottom, Manx shearwaters are medium-sized seabirds that spend most of their lives flapping over the open ocean. But in late winter and early spring, roughly 80 percent of the world’s population returns to the steep, grassy islands off the western coasts of the United Kingdom to breed. Here, they reunite with their lifelong mates and nest in underground burrows, with females laying one egg that eventually hatches into a fluffy chick.
paras.zh: 黑色在上面，白色在底部，马恩岛剪水是中型海鸟，它们一生中的大部分时间都在公海上飘荡。但在冬末和春初，世界上大约80%的人口返回英国西海岸陡峭的草地岛屿繁殖。在这里，它们与终身伴侣团聚，在地下洞穴中筑巢，雌性产下一个卵，最终孵化成一只毛茸茸的小鸡。

paras.en: Adult birds head out in search of food, bringing back tasty morsels of herring, sardine and sprat to feed their growing chicks. The birds that nest near the U.K. regularly travel more than 600 miles west from their breeding islands to forage in the food-rich waters of the Irish Sea and the northeast Atlantic Ocean. Once they’ve filled their bellies, they make the return eastward journey, navigating back to their colonies with “remarkable efficiency,” the study’s co-authors write in the paper.
paras.zh: 成年鸟类出发寻找食物，带回美味的鲱鱼、沙丁鱼和南瓜，喂养成长中的雏鸟。在英国附近筑巢的鸟类经常从它们的繁殖岛屿向西行驶600多英里，在爱尔兰海和东北大西洋的食物丰富的水域中觅食。研究报告的合著者在论文中写道，一旦他们填饱肚子，他们就会向东返回，以“非凡的效率”回到他们的殖民地。

paras.en: Shearwater chicks are so well-fed by their parents that they become too big to leave the nest. They often need to slim down a bit before fledging.
paras.zh: 剪水雏鸟的父母喂养得非常好，以至于它们变得太大而无法离开巢穴。它们通常需要在成长之前稍微瘦身。

paras.en: Scientists think Manx shearwaters successfully find their way back home by using the sun as a compass, determining which direction to fly based on its position in the sky. But “to use the sun as a compass, you have to know what time of day it is,” lead author Patrick Lewin, an ecologist at the University of Oxford, tells NPR’s Geoff Brumfiel, since the sun’s overhead position changes throughout the day as the Earth rotates on its axis. Manx shearwaters rely on their internal clocks to help make sense of the sun’s movements and stay on track.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: Scientists wondered whether the birds’ speedy east-bound homing journeys might be messing with their internal clocks—similar to jet lag in humans. They theorized that, as the birds zip across the ocean, their internal clocks do not keep pace with the changes to local time, which could affect their sun compasses and, in turn, their overall navigational accuracy.
paras.zh: 科学家们想知道这些鸟类快速向东归航的旅程是否会弄乱它们的内部时钟--类似于人类的时差。他们推测，当鸟类穿越海洋时，它们的内部时钟跟不上当地时间的变化，这可能会影响它们的太阳罗盘，进而影响它们的整体导航精度。

paras.en: To test this idea, researchers analyzed 20 years’ worth of GPS tracking data from 1,045 wild breeding Manx shearwaters. The birds made 3,688 trips between their breeding grounds and foraging grounds, but the scientists were most interested in their homing flights, so they isolated 1,837 of their eastward, home-bound journeys.
paras.zh: 为了验证这一想法，研究人员分析了来自1,045个野生马恩岛牧羊水的20年GPS跟踪数据。这些鸟在它们的繁殖地和觅食地之间进行了3,688次旅行，但科学家们对它们的归巢飞行最感兴趣，因此它们隔离了1,837次向东回家的旅程。

paras.en: The researchers predicted that, as the birds headed east, jet lag would cause them to fly slightly off course in a clockwise direction. Those predictions were borne out by the data, which revealed that the birds veered clockwise by as much as 15 degrees.

To be sure jet lag was responsible for these small orientation errors, the team considered other possible factors, such as the strength of crosswinds and distance from the colony. But “the one thing that best predicted the observed changes in shearwaters’ orientation was always this sun compass effect,” Lewin tells NewScientist’s Michael Le Page.

The birds continued to fly slightly off course even when they were flying alongside coastlines, a surprising finding that suggests Manx shearwaters rely on multiple cues for navigation—and continue using multiple methods even when they give conflicting directions.

That makes sense to Sangeeta Rani, a chronobiologist at the University of Lucknow who was not involved with the research. “After all, if I have marked a path for myself in the woods, my innate ability is not to mindlessly follow the markings,” Rani tells Anirban Mukhopadhyay for ScienceNews. “It is to find out what’s missing and still find my way back.”

Rani adds that the birds’ reliance on multiple navigational methods could serve them well in the future, when climate change and human development could make the landscapes they’re familiar with unrecognizable.

Since Manx shearwaters are covering such long distances, these subtle detours probably don’t make that much of a difference to their overall journeys: The researchers calculated that, for a bird traveling roughly 620 miles, a seven-degree compass error would only add roughly three extra miles to the trip. This is probably why Manx shearwaters haven’t evolved some way of avoiding jet lag, the researchers posit.

The study focused only on Manx shearwaters, but the researchers suspect other creatures that travel long distances—more species of birds, as well as some bats and insects—might also experience jet lag. It probably doesn’t affect birds when they migrate, however, because most migrations follow north-south routes, Ken Cheng, an emeritus comparative cognition scholar at Macquarie University who was not involved with the study, tells NewScientist.
Now that scientists know Manx shearwaters experience jet lag, the next step is to understand whether and how it affects them.

“Do they mistime critical behaviors? Do they experience physiological side effects like we do?” Lewin says in a statement. “Perhaps these birds that routinely travel long distances could help teach us how to cope with and treat jet lag to avoid the really negative effects it can have on our health.”

articles.title: These Moths Use Their Genitals to Fend Off Bats—but Not in the Way You Think. They Emit Ultrasound to Scramble the Predators' Sonar

paras.en: Bats primarily use echolocation to hunt prey, using their sophisticated biological sonar systems to find and capture tasty insects in the dark. But some moths have evolved a clever workaround to these attacks: They use their genitalia to produce high-frequency sound waves that essentially scramble their pursuers’ sonar, causing them to miss their intended target and fly away hungry.
paras.zh: 蝙蝠主要使用回声定位来捕猎猎物，利用其复杂的生物声纳系统在黑暗中寻找和捕获美味的昆虫。但是一些飞蛾已经进化出一种巧妙的方法来应对这些攻击：它们利用生殖器产生高频声波，从本质上扰乱了追捕者的声纳，导致它们错过了预定的目标，饿着肚子飞走了。

paras.en: This is such an effective strategy for staving off bat attacks that it’s arisen in moths independently up to seven times between 5 million and 30 million years ago, researchers report in a study published November 4 in the Proceedings of the Royal Society B.
paras.zh: 研究人员在11月4日发表在《Proceedings of the Royal Society B》杂志上的一项研究中报告说，这是一种抵御蝙蝠攻击的有效策略，在500万至3000万年前，蝙蝠在飞蛾中独立出现了七次。

paras.en: Different lineages of hawkmoths—a group of large, agile pollinators—have separately evolved similar solutions to the same problem, a phenomenon known as convergent evolution. The findings highlight how “interactions between predators and their prey can drive the evolution of complex and sometimes bizarre adaptations,” lead author Paul Masonick, an evolutionary biologist at the Florida Museum of Natural History, tells IFLScience’s Rachael Funnell.
paras.zh: 不同的鹰蛾谱系--一群庞大、敏捷的传粉者--对同一问题分别进化出了相似的解决方案，这种现象被称为趋同进化。佛罗里达自然历史博物馆的进化生物学家保罗·梅森尼克（ Paul Masonick ）告诉IFLScience的雷切尔·芬内尔（ Rachael Funnell ） ，研究结果强调了“捕食者与其猎物之间的相互作用如何推动复杂且有时奇怪的适应性进化”。

paras.en: “Bat predation has been a major driver of insect evolution,” he adds. “It has contributed significantly to the remarkable diversity of bioacoustic defenses among moths that we see today.”
paras.zh: “蝙蝠捕食一直是昆虫进化的主要驱动力，”他补充道。“它为我们今天看到的飞蛾生物声学防御的显着多样性做出了重大贡献。”

paras.en: Hawkmoths, also known as sphinx moths, are sturdy, nocturnal insects known for hovering in mid-air while sipping nectar from flowers, just like hummingbirds. Scientists estimate there are 1,600 species of hawkmoths around the world, with most occupying warm, wet tropical regions.
paras.zh: 鹰蛾，也被称为狮身人面像飞蛾，是坚固的夜间昆虫，以半空中盘旋而闻名，同时从花朵中啜饮花蜜，就像蜂鸟一样。科学家估计，世界各地有1600种鹰蛾，其中大多数生活在温暖潮湿的热带地区。

paras.en: Many species of hawkmoths use ultrasound to fend off bats, often by scraping their sex organs against structures on their abdomens, producing noise via stridulation. Scientists don’t know why moths first evolved these ultrasound-producing systems, but they suspect the behavior initially arose to help males attract mates.
paras.zh: 许多种类的鹰蛾使用超声波来抵御蝙蝠，通常是通过将性器官刮到腹部的结构上，通过大动作产生噪音。科学家们不知道为什么飞蛾首先进化出这些超声波产生系统，但他们怀疑这种行为最初是为了帮助雄性吸引配偶。

paras.en: “In all the species that make the noise, the males have to go to a lot of effort to impress a female,” Ian Kitching, an entomologist at the Natural History Museum in London who provided images of moths for the study, says in a statement. “This may have been the original use for the sounds. It was then co-opted as a means of defense, temporarily confusing the bats when they swoop in for the kill.”
paras.zh: “在所有发出噪音的物种中，雄性必须付出很多努力才能给雌性留下深刻印象，”伦敦自然历史博物馆的昆虫学家伊恩·基钦（ Ian Kitching ）在一份声明中说，他为这项研究提供了飞蛾的图像。“这可能是这些声音的原始用途。然后，它被用作一种防御手段，当蝙蝠扑向杀戮时，它们会暂时混淆视听。”

paras.en: Did you know? Bats’ evolutionary origins
paras.zh: 你知道吗？蝙蝠的进化起源

paras.en: In September, researchers published a massive genetic study on bats hinting that the flying mammals originated 65 million years ago in Europe, rather than Africa, North America or Asia—locations that have previously been suggested. Today, there are some 1,500 species spread across every continent except Antarctica.
paras.zh: 今年9月，研究人员发表了一项关于蝙蝠的大规模遗传研究，暗示这些会飞的哺乳动物起源于6500万年前的欧洲，而不是之前提出的非洲、北美或亚洲。今天，除南极洲外，每个大陆都有大约1,500种物种。

paras.en: In the new work, researchers set out to better understand the diversity of moths’ anti-bat defenses and how their ultrasound-producing systems evolved. They focused on male hawkmoths because scientists have little documentation of female stridulation.
paras.zh: 在这项新工作中，研究人员着手更好地了解飞蛾抗蝙蝠防御的多样性，以及它们的超声波产生系统是如何演变的。他们把重点放在雄性山楂上，因为科学家几乎没有关于雌性大脚怪的记录。

paras.en: The scientists first tested how several hawkmoth species responded when they sensed a potential bat attack. They conducted their behavioral experiments after dark, tethering each moth with a thin strand of fishing line so it could fly in place. Then, they played recordings of bat calls and gently handled each moth to simulate a predator grabbing it, recording any ultrasounds the insects made in response.
paras.zh: 科学家们首先测试了几种鹰蛾在感受到潜在的蝙蝠攻击时的反应。他们在天黑后进行了行为实验，用一条细细的钓鱼线拴住每只飞蛾，以便它们能够飞到位。然后，他们播放蝙蝠呼唤的录音，并轻轻地处理每只飞蛾，以模拟捕食者抓住它，记录昆虫响应的任何超声波。

paras.en: They also dissected moths and used detailed images to investigate the insects’ sound-producing anatomy. Finally, the team looked at an evolutionary family tree showing how different hawkmoth species are related and approximately when they diverged from common ancestors.
paras.zh: 他们还解剖了飞蛾，并使用详细的图像来研究昆虫的发声解剖结构。最后，研究小组观察了一个进化家族树，显示了不同的鹰蛾物种是如何相关的，以及它们大约何时从共同的祖先分化而来。

paras.en: Of the 143 species of hawkmoths the researchers investigated, 77 produced ultrasound. But they did so in different ways.
paras.zh: 在研究人员调查的143种鹰蛾中，有77种产生了超声波。但他们以不同的方式做到了这一点。

paras.en: All rely on special enlarged genital scales that help them hold onto females during sex, the team found, but the moths used three distinct methods to generate sound. Some species scrape their genital scales against another row of scales located near the end of their abdomen, while others rub them against stiff spines along the edge of their abdomen. Another group drags their genital scales across a patch of tiny bumps on the underside of their body, which is a newly identified mechanism.
paras.zh: 研究小组发现，所有这些都依赖于特殊的放大生殖器尺度，帮助它们在性爱过程中抓住雌性，但飞蛾使用三种不同的方法来产生声音。一些物种将生殖器鳞片刮到腹部末端附近的另一排鳞片上，而另一些物种则将生殖器鳞片摩擦到腹部边缘的僵硬脊柱上。另一组将生殖器鳞片拖过身体底部的一小块小肿块，这是一种新发现的机制。

paras.en: These methods produce different types of ultrasound, too, from continuous squeaks to irregular bursts. Species that scrape their genital scales against the bumpy patch on their underside can produce the widest range of sounds, the researchers found. That versatility may give them an evolutionary advantage, allowing them to develop new acoustic defenses against bats as the need arises.
paras.zh: 这些方法也会产生不同类型的超声波，从连续的吱吱声到不规则的爆发。研究人员发现，在底部凹凸不平的斑块上刮擦生殖器鳞片的物种可以产生最广泛的声音。这种多功能性可能会给它们带来进化优势，使它们能够在需要时开发针对蝙蝠的新声学防御。

paras.en: “Clearly the hawkmoths as a whole have more tricks up their sleeve,” Marc Holderied, a biologist at the University of Bristol in England who was not involved with the research, tells Science News’ Elie Dolgin.
paras.zh: 英国布里斯托大学的生物学家马克·霍尔德里德（ Marc Holderied ）没有参与这项研究，他告诉《科学新闻》（ Science News ）的埃利·多尔金（ Elie Dolgin ） ： “显然，鹰蛾作为一个整体有更多的技巧。”

articles.title: A 55-Year-Old Math Problem Was Solved—This Time by Humans
articles.author: Shalma Wegsman

paras.en: The original version of this story appeared in Quanta Magazine.
paras.zh: 这个故事的原始版本出现在广达杂志上。

paras.en: The late Ronald Graham wore two hats. He was a renowned mathematician and, at one time, president of the American Mathematical Society. He was also a serious juggler and president of the International Jugglers’ Association. “He loved tricks,” said Fan Chung, a mathematician at UC San Diego who was married to Graham. “You know, spinning a ball, spinning a coat hanger, spinning several balls together, throwing pens against the wall.”
paras.zh: 已故的罗纳德·格雷厄姆戴着两顶帽子。他是一位著名的数学家，曾任美国数学会主席。他还是一位认真的杂耍演员，也是国际杂耍演员协会的主席。 “他喜欢把戏，”格雷厄姆的妻子、加州大学圣地亚哥分校的数学家范钟 (Fan Chung) 说。 “你知道，旋转一个球，旋转一个衣架，一起旋转几个球，把笔扔到墙上。”

paras.en: Sometimes Graham wore both hats at once. “It’s interesting, in fact, that many mathematicians and computer scientists have an interest in juggling,” he said in a 1980 television interview. “I think it’s the search for patterns and structure that is responsible for this.”
paras.zh: 有时格雷厄姆同时戴上两顶帽子。 “事实上，有趣的是，许多数学家和计算机科学家都对杂耍感兴趣，”他在 1980 年的一次电视采访中说道。 “我认为这是对模式和结构的探索造成的。”

paras.en: He would go on to write numerous papers, some with Chung, on the mathematics of juggling. But back in 1971, decades before he made that connection explicit, he posed a question that some mathematicians now say might have been inspired by juggling, too.
paras.zh: 他继续写了许多关于杂耍数学的论文，其中一些是与钟一起写的。但早在 1971 年，也就是他明确表达这种联系的几十年前，他就提出了一个问题，一些数学家现在说这个问题也可能是受到杂耍的启发。

paras.en: Start with a random set of different integers, not including zero. Can you always rearrange them so that if you add up the first two numbers, then the first three, then the first four, and so on, every “partial sum” turns out different? In the language of juggling, this would mean that if each ball stays in the air for a different amount of time, you can always find an order to throw them in such that two balls won’t come crashing down on the same beat—which would ruin the act.
paras.zh: 从一组随机的不同整数开始，不包括零。你是否可以重新排列它们，以便如果你将前两个数字相加，然后将前三个数字相加，然后是前四个数字，依此类推，每个“部分和”的结果都会不同？用杂耍的语言来说，这意味着如果每个球在空中停留的时间不同，你总是可以找到一个将它们扔进去的命令，这样两个球就不会在同一节拍上坠落——这会破坏表演。

paras.en: If the numbers are all positive, then the answer to Graham’s question is obviously yes: The sums will always grow larger as you add more numbers. Similarly, if there are both positive and negative numbers in the mix, the answer is also known to be yes. But what if the numbers live in a finite world—like numbers wrapped around a clock, which repeat after a certain count?
paras.zh: 如果这些数字都是正数，那么格雷厄姆的问题的答案显然是肯定的：随着你增加更多的数字，总和总是会变得更大。同样，如果组合中有正数和负数，答案也已知是肯定的。但是，如果这些数字生活在一个有限的世界里，就像环绕在一个时钟上的数字一样，在一定数量之后重复出现，会怎么样？

paras.en: That’s what Graham wanted to know. He conjectured that the answer should still be yes. It often happens, he figured, that even when dealing with rigid constraints, you can still find enough flexibility to construct special patterns or structures—just as it’s usually possible to find a valid sudoku board or Latin square (another kind of puzzle) despite their many rules. “It fits nicely in all these questions about designs and about very symmetric structures,” said Noga Alon, a mathematician at Princeton University. But for decades, no one could prove Graham’s intuition to be true.
paras.zh: 这就是格雷厄姆想知道的。他猜想，答案应该还是肯定的。他认为，这种情况经常发生，即使在处理严格的约束时，你仍然可以找到足够的灵活性来构建特殊的模式或结构，就像通常可以找到有效的数独板或拉丁方（另一种拼图），尽管它们有很多规则。普林斯顿大学数学家诺加·阿隆 (Noga Alon) 表示：“它非常适合所有这些有关设计和非常对称结构的问题。”但几十年来，没有人能够证明格雷厄姆的直觉是正确的。

paras.en: That changed recently, when several young mathematicians picked up the balls. In a proof that spanned four papers and various fields of mathematics, they finally resolved Graham’s rearrangement conjecture. The final paper, by Lisa Sauermann of the University of Bonn and Huy Tuan Pham of the University of Chicago, appeared in February 2026, officially closing the problem.
paras.zh: 最近，当几位年轻的数学家拿起球时，情况发生了变化。在跨越四篇论文和数学各个领域的证明中，他们最终解决了格雷厄姆的重排猜想。最终论文由波恩大学的 Lisa Sauermann 和芝加哥大学的 Huy Tuan Pham 于 2026 年 2 月发表，正式解决了该问题。

paras.en: Across the papers, one theme prevailed: the power of randomness to draw out patterns. As Alon put it, “It’s the power of collaboration, the power of the young generation, the power of probabilistic methods” that solved the problem.
paras.zh: 在所有论文中，一个主题盛行：随机性绘制模式的力量。正如阿隆所说，“正是协作的力量、年轻一代的力量、概率方法的力量”解决了这个问题。

paras.en: Alp Müyesser, a mathematician at the University of Oxford, often finds himself drawn to problems whose solutions need two ingredients: a random process and something extra as well. After solving one such problem in 2022 while he was still a graduate student, he encountered Graham’s conjecture and realized that his just-finished proof could help there, too.
paras.zh: 牛津大学数学家 Alp Müyesser 经常发现自己被一些问题所吸引，这些问题的解决方案需要两个要素：随机过程和额外的东西。 2022 年，当他还是一名研究生时，他解决了一个这样的问题，之后遇到了格雷厄姆猜想，并意识到他刚刚完成的证明也能对此有所帮助。

paras.en: The conjecture is set in the world of clock arithmetic. You start by placing the whole numbers on a number line, then you wrap the line around the face of a clock so that the numbers repeat after some prime number, p. Say p is 7, for instance. In this setting, 0, 7, 14, and all other multiples of 7 are equivalent—meaning that you can add two positive numbers (like 3 and 4) and get zero.
paras.zh: 猜想设定在时钟算术的世界中。您首先将整数放在一条数字线上，然后将线绕在时钟的表面上，使数字在某个素数之后重复， p.例如，假设p是7。在此设置中， 0、7、14和所有其他7的倍数是等价的，这意味着您可以添加两个正数（如3和4 ）并得到零。

paras.en: Graham asked the following: If you pick any set of nonzero numbers off this number line (for any p), can you always rearrange them so that the partial sums you get are all different?
paras.zh: 格雷厄姆问道：如果你从这条数字线上选择任何一组非零数字（对于任何p ） ，你能总是重新排列它们，使你得到的部分总和都不一样吗？

paras.en: The challenge depends on how big your set is compared to p. The more numbers you pick, the more sums there are to manage. But if you choose fewer numbers, there will be fewer ways to rearrange them. These different cases inspire different approaches.
paras.zh: 挑战取决于您的套餐与p相比有多大。您选择的数字越多，要管理的金额就越多。但是，如果您选择较少的数字，重新排列它们的方法就会较少。这些不同的案例激发了不同的方法。

paras.en: Müyesser, along with his former adviser, Alexey Pokrovskiy of University College London, tackled the case where your set includes almost every possible number up to p. With sets this large, it can be extremely hard to construct a valid ordering. But it turned out that starting with a random ordering can bring you most of the way there.
paras.zh: Müyesser和他的前顾问，伦敦大学学院的Alexey Pokrovskiy一起解决了这样一个案例，即您的数据集几乎包含了所有可能的数字，最高可达p。集合如此之大，构建有效的排序可能非常困难。但事实证明，从随机排序开始可以为您带来大部分便利。

paras.en: “Computer scientists often call this a ‘finding the hay in the haystack’ problem,” Müyesser said. You might know that lots of good orderings are out there, but actually finding one is hard. “If you do it randomly, it’s likely going to work, but it’s hard to explicitly describe what the solution is supposed to look like.”
paras.zh: Müyesser说： “计算机科学家经常称之为‘在干草堆中找到干草’问题。”您可能知道有很多好的订单，但实际上很难找到一个。“如果你随机这样做，它可能会奏效，但很难明确地描述解决方案应该是什么样子。”

paras.en: Müyesser and Pokrovskiy needed to ensure that no sequence of numbers anywhere in the ordering added up to zero. Otherwise, adding those numbers to the previous partial sum would repeat that sum.
paras.zh: Müyesser和Pokrovskiy需要确保排序中的任何数字序列都不会加到零。否则，将这些数字加到上一个部分和将重复该和。

paras.en: A completely random ordering might have a few of these troublesome sequences. So Müyesser and Pokrovskiy first set aside a few specially chosen numbers from the set, then randomly scrambled the rest. They scanned their random ordering for any problems; if they came across an interval that added up to zero, they could insert one of the spare numbers to change it. In 2022, they posted their solution, though it was hidden in a paper that focused on applying the same technique to a more general problem.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: A couple of years later, Noah Kravitz of Oxford, unaware of Müyesser and Pokrovskiy’s solution, stumbled on Graham’s conjecture in an online archive of unsolved problems. “I saw there was an open problem, and I was like, it’s embarrassing for humanity that we don’t know this,” Kravitz said. “This situation just had to be rectified.”
paras.zh: 几年后，牛津大学的Noah Kravitz不知道Müyesser和Pokrovskiy的解决方案，在未解决问题的在线档案中偶然发现了Graham的猜想。Kravitz说： “我看到一个悬而未决的问题，我觉得，我们不知道这一点，这对人类来说很尴尬。” “这种情况必须得到纠正。”

paras.en: He decided to approach the conjecture from the opposite end. Together with Benjamin Bedert of Oxford, he considered the case where the set of numbers is tiny compared to p—for instance, Alon said, if you have a set of 100 numbers where p is 1 billion.
paras.zh: 他决定从另一端接近这个猜想。阿隆说，他与牛津大学的本杰明·贝德特（ Benjamin Bedert ）一起考虑了一组数字与p相比很小的情况，例如，如果你有一组100个数字，其中p是10亿。

paras.en: Kravitz and Bedert solved Graham’s conjecture for those cases and posted their proof in September 2024. Müyesser saw it and reached out, sharing his own work; the three of them (plus two other colleagues) then teamed up to extend Müyesser’s original approach.
paras.zh: Kravitz和Bedert解决了Graham对这些案件的猜测，并于2024年9月发布了他们的证据。Müyesser看到了这一点并伸出援手，分享了他自己的工作；他们三人（加上另外两位同事）随后联手扩展了Müyesser的原始方法。

paras.en: “It was a pretty unlikely combination of people,” Kravitz said. He and Müyesser come from two areas of combinatorics that don’t typically collaborate. “Different sections have completely different techniques,” he said.
paras.zh: “这是一个相当不可能的人群组合，” Kravitz说。他和Müyesser来自两个通常不合作的组合学领域。“不同的部分有完全不同的技术，”他说。

paras.en: Their paper, which they posted in August 2025, handled more cases where the set of numbers is relatively large compared to p. But between those cases and the small-set cases that Kravitz and Bedert had covered, a gap remained. No one could figure out what to do about medium-size sets, such as those that include roughly half as many numbers as p. “Our methods didn’t work there, and there were clear reasons that they would not have worked,” Müyesser said.
paras.zh: 他们在2025年8月发表的论文处理了更多的案例，这些案例的数字与p相比相对较大。但是，在这些病例和Kravitz和Bedert所涵盖的小病例之间，仍然存在差距。没有人能弄清楚如何处理中等大小的集合，例如那些包含大约一半数量的数字的集合。Müyesser说： “我们的方法在那里不起作用，而且有明确的理由表明它们不会奏效。”

paras.en: It seemed as though research on the problem might enter another long hiatus. Then, in February 2026, a surprise appeared online.
paras.zh: 似乎对这个问题的研究可能会进入另一个漫长的间歇期。然后，在2026年2月，一个惊喜出现在网上。

paras.en: Lisa Sauermann and Huy Tuan Pham were old friends. The two mathematicians had met in 2015 at Stanford University, where Sauermann was a graduate student and Pham an undergraduate. Today they live on different continents—Sauermann in Bonn, Germany, and Pham in Chicago. But a conference in Germany in September 2025 provided a rare chance for them to share a chalkboard again, and afterward Pham followed Sauermann to Bonn for a short visit. All they needed was a problem to work on.
paras.zh: Lisa Sauermann和Huy Tuan Pham是老朋友。这两位数学家于2015年在斯坦福大学相遇，索尔曼是斯坦福大学的研究生，范是斯坦福大学的本科生。如今，他们生活在不同的大陆上--德国波恩的绍尔曼和芝加哥的PHAM。但2025年9月在德国举行的一次会议为他们提供了一个难得的机会，让他们再次分享黑板，之后范跟随索尔曼到波恩进行了短暂的访问。他们所需要的只是一个需要解决的问题。

paras.en: At the conference, they heard two talks on Graham’s conjecture by mathematicians who had attempted but failed to bridge the gap. They were intrigued. And as it later turned out, Sauermann had encountered a closely related problem in the International Mathematical Olympiad as a high school student. She solved it correctly, and by the time she finished high school, she’d won a gold medal in the prestigious competition four times. (Most likely, it was Chung who placed the problem on that year’s exam, as she was on the committee that wrote the questions, and she frequently took inspiration from Graham’s many puzzles.)
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: By the end of their three-day visit, Sauermann and Pham had a plan for how to crack the case.
paras.zh: 在为期三天的访问结束时， Sauermann和Pham制定了一个如何破案的计划。

paras.en: It hinged on a technically demanding method called anti-concentration. Here, an anti-concentration statement asserts that some event has a particularly low chance of happening. But the mechanics of proving these kinds of statements are so intricate that, though Kravitz and others were aware that such an anti-concentration approach might succeed, “we just hadn’t had the guts to actually try it,” he said.
paras.zh: 它依赖于一种技术要求苛刻的方法，称为反浓缩。在这里，反集中声明断言某些事件发生的可能性特别低。但是，证明这类陈述的机制是如此复杂，以至于尽管Kravitz和其他人意识到这种反集中方法可能会成功，但“我们只是没有勇气真正尝试它，”他说。

paras.en: First, though, Sauermann and Pham began the way their predecessors had. They randomly reordered their set of numbers and came up with a procedure to fix any problems—that is, any sequences that add up to zero. Any time they found a zero-sum sequence, they swapped out the last number in the sequence with another one.
paras.zh: 首先， Sauermann和Pham开始了他们的前辈的方式。他们随机重新排序他们的数字集，并提出一个程序来解决任何问题-即任何加起来为零的序列。每当他们发现零和序列时，他们都会将序列中的最后一个数字换成另一个数字。

paras.en: This procedure often went without a hitch. But three types of “bad events” would cause it to fail. One: A zero-sum sequence might occur toward the end of the entire arrangement; then there would be no other numbers to swap in. Two: Many zero-sum sequences might appear too close together, making it impossible to fix them all. And three: Fixing one bad sequence might create another zero-sum sequence down the line.
paras.zh: 这个过程通常顺利进行。但三种类型的“不良事件”会导致其失败。第一：零和序列可能会出现在整个安排的末尾；然后就没有其他数字可以交换了。第二：许多零和序列可能看起来太接近了，因此不可能全部解决。第三：修复一个错误序列可能会产生另一个零和序列。

paras.en: Sauermann and Pham hoped to prove, using anti-concentration, that each of these bad events was sufficiently unlikely. Then there would have to be a way to rearrange the set of numbers to satisfy the conjecture.
paras.zh: Sauermann和Pham希望用反集中来证明，这些不良事件都不太可能发生。然后，必须有一种方法来重新排列数字集以满足猜想。

paras.en: To do this, the duo used Fourier analysis—an area of math that lets you rewrite functions as sums of simple waves—to show that in general, when you add up random sets of numbers, no one sum is especially likely to appear. They then used this insight to carefully estimate the probability that each bad event would occur, ultimately showing that the total chance of getting a bad event was less than 100 percent. That was enough to settle the conjecture.
paras.zh: 为此，两人使用傅里叶分析（一个数学领域，允许您将函数重写为简单波的总和）来表明，一般来说，当您将随机数字集合相加时，没有一个总和特别可能出现。然后，他们利用这一见解仔细估计每个不良事件发生的概率，最终表明发生不良事件的总概率低于100%。这足以解决这个猜测。

paras.en: A few months after their stint in Germany, Sauermann and Pham posted their 27-page proof online. They had shown not only that a satisfactory rearrangement was always possible, but that a random ordering could be rearranged to eliminate bad events at least 90% of the time—a massive success rate.
paras.zh: 在德国工作几个月后， Sauermann和Pham在网上发布了他们27页的证明。他们不仅证明了令人满意的重排始终是可能的，而且可以重新安排随机排序以至少在90 ％的时间内消除不良事件-这是一个巨大的成功率。

paras.en: The mathematicians who had previously worked on the problem were surprised to see the remaining case closed so quickly. “Their approach is just completely different,” Müyesser said.
paras.zh: 以前研究过这个问题的数学家们惊讶地发现，剩下的问题这么快就解决了。“他们的方法完全不同，” Müyesser说。

paras.en: Together, the four papers prove Graham’s conjecture for sets of all sizes. But they all assume that p is very large; though no one has calculated its exact value, think along the lines of 10 raised to the 100th power. To mathematicians, that’s fine—the salient point is that you’re working in the setting of clock arithmetic. But another aspect of the problem technically remains unsolved—you might still try to resolve the conjecture for all p. And if you want to use the result to choreograph a real juggling routine, you’re out of luck: To correspond to such a large p, the routine would have to be much too long.
paras.zh: QUERY LENGTH LIMIT EXCEEDED. MAX ALLOWED QUERY : 500 CHARS

paras.en: The proof confirms that even within these strange, limited number settings, “there are some nice structures that always exist,” Alon said. You can always achieve some degree of flexibility, shuffling the numbers in your set around to avoid revisiting the same partial sums.
paras.zh: 阿隆说，证据证实，即使在这些奇怪的、数量有限的设置中， “也有一些漂亮的结构一直存在。”您始终可以实现一定程度的灵活性，对集合中的数字进行洗牌，以避免重新审视相同的部分金额。

paras.en: “To pose a good problem is really an art,” Chung said. “I think Ron would be extremely happy to see the problem solved.”
paras.zh: “提出一个好的问题真的是一门艺术，” Chung说。“我认为Ron会非常高兴看到问题得到解决。”

articles.title: How to Remind Your Boss of Your PTO Without Pissing Them Off
articles.author: Jill Duffy

paras.en: You're about to slam that laptop shut for two weeks when the boss messages, “See you Monday!”
paras.zh: 当你准备将笔记本电脑关上两周时，老板发消息说：“周一见！”

paras.en: We've all been there, staring down a manager who has forgotten about our paid time off—even though we told them!
paras.zh: 我们都经历过这样的情况，盯着一位忘记了我们带薪休假的经理——尽管我们告诉了他们！

paras.en: When we communicate something that's important to us, we can forget that it's not necessarily as meaningful to the recipient. Surely you've been on the flip side, too, annoyed at a coworker who hasn't replied to your messages, until someone mentions that they're on holiday.
paras.zh: 当我们传达对我们来说很重要的事情时，我们可能会忘记它对接收者来说不一定有意义。当然，您也曾有过相反的经历，对没有回复您的消息的同事感到恼火，直到有人提到他们正在度假。

paras.en: A key to efficient communication in the workplace is to repeat yourself. It sounds counterintuitive, but it's true. We're all better off when we overcommunicate by saying the same thing two or three times.
paras.zh: 工作场所高效沟通的关键是重复自己的话。这听起来违反直觉，但却是事实。当我们通过将同一件事说两三遍来进行过度沟通时，我们的情况都会更好。

paras.en: The trick is how and when you do it. Think of all the avenues you have for requesting, recording, and reminding people of your PTO. Use all the channels, and spread out the messaging so that each instance has relevant context and timing.
paras.zh: 诀窍在于如何以及何时进行。想想您用于请求、记录和提醒人们您的 PTO 的所有途径。使用所有渠道并分散消息传递，以便每个实例都有相关的上下文和时间安排。

paras.en: 6 Weeks to 6 Months Out: Get It on the Books
paras.zh: 6 周到 6 个月后：将其记录在案

paras.en: If you like to plan in advance, you might request time off four to six months out. Not all managers appreciate this much notice, however, because they might not know what the workload will be when your vacation rolls around, making it hard for them to approve your dates.
paras.zh: 如果您想提前计划，您可以请求四到六个月的休假。然而，并不是所有的经理都喜欢这么多的通知，因为他们可能不知道当你的假期到来时工作量会是多少，这使得他们很难批准你的日期。

paras.en: How far in advance you should request time off is a conversation to have with your direct boss. It depends on them as a person, the type of work you do, the size of your team, and other factors. If this conversation doesn't give you much clarity, four to six weeks before your time off is probably about right. Start there and adjust as necessary.
paras.zh: 您应该提前多长时间请假，具体取决于您与直接上司的沟通。这取决于他们个人、你所做的工作类型、你的团队规模以及其他因素。如果这次谈话没有给你带来太多清晰的信息，那么在你休假前四到六周可能是合适的。从这里开始并根据需要进行调整。

paras.en: Occasionally, you need approval well in advance for an event that cannot move and will cost you a lot of money to cancel, like your own wedding or a nonrefundable trip. In those cases, six months or more is not unreasonable, but bring it up from time to time so no one forgets.
paras.zh: 有时，您需要提前获得某些无法移动且需要花费大量费用才能取消的活动的批准，例如您自己的婚礼或不可退款的旅行。在这种情况下，六个月或更长时间并不是不合理的，但要时不时地提出来，这样就不会有人忘记。

paras.en: Whenever you put in your initial request, it must be recorded. Log it into a time-off system if your organization uses one (human resources software, a shared calendar) or write it in an email with a clear subject line, and make sure your boss replies saying it's approved.
paras.zh: 每当您提出初始请求时，都必须记录下来。如果您的组织使用休假系统（人力资源软件、共享日历），请将其记录到休假系统中，或者将其写在主题行明确的电子邮件中，并确保您的老板回复说已批准。

paras.en: About two weeks before your time off, remind your boss and colleagues verbally in meetings. The ideal settings are in a weekly one-on-one meeting with your direct manager and in a team meeting.
paras.zh: 休假前大约两周，在会议上口头提醒你的老板和同事。理想的设置是每周与直接经理举行一对一会议以及团队会议。

paras.en: Save your info for the end of the meeting after all pressing business has been discussed. If you need to make sure your responsibilities are covered while you're out, raise that point privately with your manager rather than in a team meeting so the boss has time to decide how to handle it.
paras.zh: 在讨论完所有紧迫事务后，保存您的信息以供会议结束时使用。如果您需要确保在外出期间履行自己的职责，请私下向您的经理提出这一点，而不是在团队会议上提出，以便老板有时间决定如何处理。

paras.en: 1 Week Out: Email or Message Your Contacts
paras.zh: 1 周后：向您的联系人发送电子邮件或消息

paras.en: If you need to tell someone beyond your team—such as clients or another department—about your planned time off, do so in writing a week before you leave. This gives them plenty of opportunity to reach out while you’re still available.
paras.zh: 如果您需要告诉团队之外的人（例如客户或其他部门）您的计划休假时间，请在离开前一周以书面形式告知。这让他们有足够的机会在您还有空的时候与您联系。

paras.en: Email is fine, though if you usually communicate with these people through Slack or Microsoft Teams, that may be a better option. How you format the message matters—see the next step for tips.
paras.zh: 电子邮件很好，但如果您通常通过 Slack 或 Microsoft Teams 与这些人沟通，那可能是更好的选择。消息的格式很重要 - 请参阅下一步以获取提示。

paras.en: 2 Business Days Out: Send Formatted Messages
paras.zh: 2 个工作日后：发送格式化消息

paras.en: Two business days before your time off begins, send a short, clear message to everyone who needs to know that you will be out. If the norm is to use Slack or Microsoft Teams, use that.
paras.zh: 在休假开始前的两个工作日，向所有需要知道您将休假的人发送一条简短而明确的信息。如果标准是使用 Slack 或 Microsoft Teams，请使用它。

paras.en: How you format this message makes a huge difference. The first sentence should say something like, "Just a reminder, I will be out beginning DATE. I will be back on DATE." This sentence can be in bold. The second DATE is the day you return to work, not the last day of your PTO. What's relevant to your colleagues is the day you are available.
paras.zh: 您如何格式化此消息会产生巨大的差异。第一句话应该是这样的：“只是提醒一下，我将在 DATE 开始外出。我将在 DATE 回来。”这句话可以加粗。第二个日期是您返回工作的日期，而不是 PTO 的最后一天。与您的同事相关的是您有空的日期。

paras.en: If you need to give more information, such as who is covering for you, put that in a new paragraph. Do not go overboard with detail. It will make people crazy. Should you need to leave detailed instructions, put them in a shared document and link to it.
paras.zh: 如果您需要提供更多信息，例如谁为您提供服务，请将其放在新的段落中。不要过度关注细节。它会让人们疯狂。如果您需要留下详细说明，请将其放入共享文档中并链接到该文档。

paras.en: Why send this message two business days out? Simple: If your first PTO day is Monday, you send this message on Thursday so that anybody who takes off or calls in sick on Friday still sees it in time.
paras.zh: 为什么要在两个工作日后发送此消息？很简单：如果您的第一个 PTO 日是星期一，您可以在星期四发送此消息，以便任何在星期五请假或请病假的人仍然可以及时看到它。

paras.en: My favorite PTO reminder is the status indicator in a team messaging platform. Set it to show you're out and add an appropriate emoji, like a palm tree or airplane.
paras.zh: 我最喜欢的 PTO 提醒是团队消息平台中的状态指示器。将其设置为显示您外出并添加适当的表情符号，例如棕榈树或飞机。

paras.en: Even if you dislike emoji, they are extremely efficient and effective communicators here. At a glance, everyone who sees it is reminded that you're out.
paras.zh: 即使你不喜欢表情符号，它们在这里也是非常高效和有效的沟通者。一眼望去，每个看到它的人都会想起你出去了。

paras.en: You can typically set a status message too; use this to tell everyone the date you’ll be available again.
paras.zh: 您通常也可以设置状态消息；用它来告诉大家您再次有空的日期。

paras.en: Your First Day Off: A Final Reminder for the Extra Forgetful
paras.zh: 你的第一天休息：对特别健忘的人的最后提醒

paras.en: For those supremely forgetful bosses and coworkers, you might set up an automated message that appears at 8:30 am the first day you're out. Slack, Teams, email, or even a text message will do the trick. Be concise. Be kind. And have a sense of humor. The point of the message is to be helpful—not make someone else feel like a forgetful jerk.
paras.zh: 对于那些极其健忘的老板和同事，您可以设置一条自动消息，该消息会在您外出的第一天上午 8:30 出现。 Slack、Teams、电子邮件，甚至短信都可以解决问题。保持简洁。友善一点。并且有幽默感。这条信息的重点是提供帮助——而不是让别人觉得自己是个健忘的混蛋。

articles.title: Welcome to Weed Island
articles.author: Orlando Crowcroft

paras.en: Steven Tan walks along a narrow concourse in the Northern Leaf greenhouse in St Lawrence, Jersey, reading aloud the strains of his cannabis plants: Pink Gasoline, Moon Beam Gelato, Carbon Fibre, Gorilla Kush. Rows of plants stretch off into the distance. To the untrained eye, they look largely the same, with their distinctive jagged-edged, multi-fingered leaf shape and sticky buds like tiny pinecones.
paras.zh: 史蒂文·谭（Steven Tan）沿着泽西岛圣劳伦斯北叶温室的狭窄大厅行走，大声朗读他的大麻植物品种：粉红汽油、月光冰淇淋、碳纤维、大猩猩库什。一排排植物一直延伸到远方。对于未经训练的人来说，它们看起来基本上是一样的，都有独特的锯齿状边缘、多指的叶子形状和像小松果一样的粘芽。

paras.en: But Tan, the CEO and director of medical cannabis manufacturer Northern Leaf, knows them intimately. “These plants are all different,” he says, stopping next to a mature Carbon Fibre specimen. “Just like humans.”
paras.zh: 但医用大麻制造商 Northern Leaf 的首席执行官兼董事 Tan 非常了解他们。 “这些植物都是不同的，”他在一个成熟的碳纤维标本旁边停下来说道。 “就像人类一样。”

paras.en: Northern Leaf is one of the largest licensed medical marijuana producers in Europe. Its 100,000-square-foot growing facility is based in Jersey, the largest of the Channel Islands, located between England and France. Previously, this greenhouse was home to Jersey tomatoes, once a famed crop on the island that came close to extinction, thanks to growing fuel costs and cheaper competition from overseas. Now, it is fitted out with all of the technology required for cultivating cannabis that meets strict regulations for medical use, which include: automated irrigation, environmental monitoring, and air purification.
paras.zh: Northern Leaf 是欧洲最大的获得许可的医用大麻生产商之一。其种植基地占地 100,000 平方英尺，位于英国和法国之间海峡群岛中最大的岛屿泽西岛。此前，这个温室是泽西西红柿的家园，泽西西红柿曾经是岛上著名的作物，由于燃料成本不断上涨和来自海外的廉价竞争而濒临灭绝。现在，它配备了种植大麻所需的所有技术，符合严格的医疗用途法规，其中包括：自动灌溉、环境监测和空气净化。

paras.en: Despite being just 45 square miles in size, with a population of 100,000, Jersey—which lies 14 miles off the coast of the French mainland but is a British Crown Dependency—has emerged as an unlikely player in the medical cannabis industry. Although its total exports (over 9,200 kilograms in 2025) are small compared to UK growers, this represents an enormous amount per capita, and cannabis is fast becoming one of the island’s important new industries. Jersey’s chief minister, Lyndon Farnham, has previously said that he wants Jersey to be a “centre of excellence” for medical cannabis, and for cannabis production to become a mainstay of the island’s economy.
paras.zh: 尽管面积只有 45 平方英里，人口只有 10 万，泽西岛距法国大陆海岸 14 英里，但属于英国皇家属地，但它已成为医用大麻行业中一个不太可能的参与者。尽管与英国种植者相比，其出口总量（2025 年超过 9,200 公斤）很小，但这代表了人均出口量巨大，而且大麻正迅速成为该岛重要的新兴产业之一。泽西岛首席部长林登·法纳姆此前曾表示，他希望泽西岛成为医用大麻的“卓越中心”，并使大麻生产成为该岛经济的支柱。

paras.en: Currently, 90 percent of Jersey’s cannabis production comes from Northern Leaf. In 2025, the company exported £8.4 million ($11.3 million) worth of medical marijuana to markets including the UK and Germany (regulations mean it is only permitted to grow for export and cannot sell to customers in Jersey). Tan has much greater ambitions. He points to another famous Jersey export, Jersey Royal potatoes. “Jersey’s potato industry did £40 million in 2025,” he said. “I am already doing a quarter of the potato industry on 5 percent of the land. On 20 percent of the land, I could create an industry worth more than the potato industry. That is where it will get interesting.”
paras.zh: 目前，泽西岛 90% 的大麻产量来自 Northern Leaf。 2025 年，该公司向英国和德国等市场出口了价值 840 万英镑（1130 万美元）的医用大麻（法规规定大麻只能用于出口，不能出售给泽西岛的客户）。谭有更大的野心。他提到了另一个著名的泽西出口产品——泽西皇家土豆。 “到 2025 年，泽西岛的马铃薯产业创造了 4000 万英镑的收入，”他说。 “我已经在 5% 的土地上开展了四分之一的马铃薯产业。在 20% 的土地上，我可以创建一个比马铃薯产业更有价值的产业。这就是它会变得有趣的地方。”

paras.en: Born in Malaysia to a Chinese dad and Irish mother, Tan, 50, wanted to become a vet, but after graduating from university in 1998, ended up developing software for Citibank. He was making good money, but his heart wasn’t in finance. What really interested him was growing weed. “I loved the science of it, the genetics, the seeds, the smells,” Tan says.
paras.zh: 50 岁的 Tan 出生于马来西亚，父亲是中国人，母亲是爱尔兰人，他想成为一名兽医，但 1998 年大学毕业后，最终为花旗银行开发软件。他赚了很多钱，但他的心不在金融上。他真正感兴趣的是种植杂草。 “我喜欢它的科学、遗传学、种子、气味，”谭说。

paras.en: The early 2000s were the perfect time for an inquisitive young business grad to get into the cannabis business. Across the world, governments were legalizing medical marijuana and moving towards decriminalization over draconian sentencing.
paras.zh: 2000 年代初期是充满好奇心的年轻商业毕业生进入大麻行业的最佳时机。世界各地的政府都在将医用大麻合法化，并朝着严厉量刑的非刑事化迈进。

paras.en: Tan began bouncing around jurisdictions that were relaxing laws on cannabis, working as a consultant in California, the Netherlands, and Canada. “I started to see these legal frameworks opening up. The minute they existed, I went there,” he says.
paras.zh: 谭开始在放宽大麻法律的司法管辖区工作，在加利福尼亚州、荷兰和加拿大担任顾问。 “我开始看到这些法律框架正在开放。它们一存在，我就去了那里，”他说。

paras.en: Jersey has a somewhat unique regulatory environment. As a Crown Dependency, it has close ties to Britain, but is not a part of the UK. Crucially, it is self-governing: It can make its own laws. Jersey’s main reputation today is as a tax haven, attracting some of the world’s wealthiest individuals and companies, thanks to its lack of capital gains tax and 0 percent corporation tax for most companies. Along its coastline, next to twee beachside cafes and Nazi bunkers (the Channel Islands were the only part of the British Isles to be occupied by Hitler’s forces in World War II), you can find offices of international banks and wealth management firms catering to the super rich.
paras.zh: 泽西岛的监管环境有些独特。作为皇家属地，它与英国有着密切的联系，但不属于英国的一部分。至关重要的是，它是自治的：它可以制定自己的法律。泽西岛如今的主要声誉是作为避税天堂，吸引了一些世界上最富有的个人和公司，因为它不征收资本利得税，并且对大多数公司实行零公司税。沿着海岸线，在特威海滨咖啡馆和纳粹碉堡旁边（海峡群岛是不列颠群岛中唯一在第二次世界大战中被希特勒军队占领的部分），您可以找到为超级富豪提供服务的国际银行和财富管理公司的办事处。

paras.en: Although traditionally culturally conservative, Jersey has become something of a trailblazer on cannabis. The island legalized medical cannabis in 2019. Today, five private clinics operate on the island. The latest figures suggest that 6 percent of the population is prescribed cannabis, compared to an estimated 0.4 percent in Germany and 0.1 percent in the UK. Upon legalization, the island’s chief minister, Lyndon Farnham, laid out ambitious plans for the island to become a hub of the medical cannabis trade, repurposing the horticultural facilities and know-how from its tomato-growing glory days for this new endeavor.
paras.zh: 尽管传统上文化保守，泽西岛已成为大麻的开拓者。该岛于 2019 年实现医用大麻合法化。如今，岛上有五家私人诊所。最新数据显示，6% 的人口服用大麻，而德国和英国的这一比例分别为 0.4% 和 0.1%。合法化后，该岛首席部长林登·法纳姆 (Lyndon Farnham) 制定了雄心勃勃的计划，使该岛成为医用大麻贸易中心，并重新利用其番茄种植辉煌时期的园艺设施和技术来实现这一新目标。

paras.en: Tan joined Northern Leaf as CEO in 2024, when the company was in dire straits after a failed IPO. That year, it was valued at just £3.7 million, despite having spent as much as £30 million on its weed-growing facility.
paras.zh: 谭于 2024 年加入 Northern Leaf 担任首席执行官，当时该公司因 IPO 失败而陷入困境。那一年，尽管在杂草种植设施上花费了 3000 万英镑，但它的价值仅为 370 万英镑。

paras.en: Tan nevertheless saw a lot of potential, and over the last two years has seen capacity at the site increase from 25 percent to 75 percent. He believes the £8.4 million of product the company exported last year is just the beginning.
paras.zh: 尽管如此，Tan 还是看到了巨大的潜力，在过去两年中，该站点的容量从 25% 增加到了 75%。他认为公司去年出口的 840 万英镑产品仅仅是一个开始。

paras.en: Sarah Clover, a barrister at Kings Chambers who works on cannabis licensing in Jersey, told WIRED the island’s advantage is hard to replicate. Growers are inspected by the UK Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), which is known for enforcing rigorous standards on quality. “Anybody buying from Jersey knows that the stuff coming out of it is absolutely gold standard, because the MHRA says it is,” she says. Permits, however, are handled by a small team on the island: “You can make an application for a permit on a Monday and get it on a Tuesday.”
paras.zh: 国王钱伯斯 (Kings Chambers) 的律师莎拉·克洛弗 (Sarah Clover) 在泽西岛从事大麻许可工作，她告诉《连线》杂志，该岛的优势很难复制。种植者接受英国药品和保健品监管机构 (MHRA) 的检查，该机构以执行严格的质量标准而闻名。 “任何从泽西岛购买产品的人都知道，这里生产的产品绝对是黄金标准，因为 MHRA 就是这么说的，”她说。然而，许可证是由岛上的一个小团队处理的：“您可以在周一申请许可证，并在周二获得许可证。”

paras.en: Many within the Jersey medicinal cannabis industry now want to go beyond growing the raw ingredient and package it for export as a final product on the island. Northern Leaf already has the facilities to do so, but Jersey law dictates it can only export bulk amounts of raw cannabis for other companies to process and pack for distribution and sale. The company is waiting to see if Jersey will change its law. “At the minute we’re kind of on this seesaw—which way will the island go?” Clover says. “It could really take off here. Jersey could be a life sciences hub, not just for cannabis but for all sorts of pharmaceuticals.”
paras.zh: 泽西岛药用大麻行业的许多人现在希望不仅仅种植原材料，并将其包装作为岛上的最终产品出口。 Northern Leaf 已经拥有这样做的设施，但泽西岛法律规定它只能出口大量原料大麻供其他公司加工和包装以供分销和销售。该公司正在等待泽西岛是否会改变其法律。 “此刻我们就像坐在跷跷板上一样——岛屿会朝哪个方向发展？”四叶草说。 “它真的可以在这里起飞。泽西岛可以成为生命科学中心，不仅是大麻，而且是各种药品。”

paras.en: But running a cannabis business on a small island poses challenges, and not everyone is enthused about the idea of expansion. Tan has faced off against residents every time that the facility has expanded production. Some locals have complained that they can smell cannabis from their balconies. Others have linked the growing industry to concerns over misuse of cannabis on the island, despite the fact that all of its product is exported. Cannabis is a “contributory factor” in 22 percent of admissions to the island’s acute mental health ward, according to Jersey’s health minister.
paras.zh: 但在一个小岛上经营大麻业务带来了挑战，并不是每个人都对扩张的想法感到热衷。每当工厂扩大生产时，谭都会与居民发生冲突。一些当地人抱怨说，他们可以从阳台上闻到大麻的味道。其他人则将不断增长的行业与岛上滥用大麻的担忧联系起来，尽管该岛所有产品均用于出口。泽西岛卫生部长表示，岛上 22% 的急性精神健康病房入院患者中，吸食大麻是一个“促成因素”。

paras.en: One patient, Michael, told WIRED that he was prescribed medical cannabis for 18 months after having tried two other prescribed medications for insomnia and anxiety. “The initial assessment was simple. I had a meeting with the cannabis doctor who was pretty evangelical about its medicinal properties. They check your medical history with your GP, and within 10 days you’re good to go,” he says.
paras.zh: 一位名叫迈克尔的患者告诉《连线》杂志，他在尝试了另外两种治疗失眠和焦虑的处方药物后，开始服用医用大麻 18 个月。 “最初的评估很简单。我和大麻医生会面了，他对大麻的药用特性非常了解。他们会和你的全科医生一起检查你的病史，10 天内你就可以走了，”他说。

paras.en: Michael was prescribed 30 grams a month of “unbelievably good” cannabis and told that if he ran out he could back and ask for more. “I stopped because it was seriously affecting my mental health [and] I have since seen a psychiatric professional who said I should never have been prescribed it given my documented mental health history,” he says.
paras.zh: 迈克尔每月被开出 30 克“令人难以置信的好”大麻，并被告知如果他用完，他可以回来索取更多。 “我停药了，因为它严重影响了我的心理健康，[而且]我见过一位精神科专业人士，他说，鉴于我有记录的心理健康史，我不应该开这种药，”他说。

paras.en: Illegal resale of medical cannabis is also an issue, with a rise in so-called “user-dealers,” who sell their excess medical marijuana to others. Jersey Police told WIRED this “undermines the legal framework and creates opportunities for criminal supply.”
paras.zh: 非法转售医用大麻也是一个问题，所谓的“用户经销商”不断增加，他们将多余的医用大麻出售给其他人。泽西岛警方告诉《连线》杂志，这“破坏了法律框架，并为犯罪活动创造了机会”。

paras.en: Overall, however, cannabis-related offenses have dropped since Jersey legalized medical cannabis in 2019—from 216 in 2016 to just 12, as of July 2026.
paras.zh: 然而，总体而言，自泽西岛于 2019 年将医用大麻合法化以来，与大麻相关的犯罪有所下降，从 2016 年的 216 起减少到截至 2026 年 7 月的仅 12 起。

paras.en: Tan is circumspect about the challenges of operating on Jersey. “Culturally, the people here are harder to convince about cannabis,” he says. “It’s an older society.” But after 25 years working in the industry, he’s used to the pushback.
paras.zh: 谭对在泽西岛运营的挑战持谨慎态度。 “从文化上来说，这里的人们更难相信大麻，”他说。 “这是一个古老的社会。”但在这个行业工作了 25 年之后，他已经习惯了这种阻力。

paras.en: “It’s a normal challenge,” he says. “And I think when anyone sits down and meets me, they understand. This isn’t a bunch of stoners growing a bit of weed in a plastic greenhouse.”
paras.zh: “这是一个正常的挑战，”他说。 “我认为，当任何人坐下来见到我时，他们都会理解。这不是一群在塑料温室里种植杂草的瘾君子。”

paras.en: While Jersey’s medical cannabis industry grows, some people on the island want to go further. In 2024, a vote to decriminalize recreational cannabis was defeated by a single vote in the island’s parliament. When it was brought back for another vote by the island’s then health minister, it was withdrawn before it could be debated. It is expected to be brought back before the parliament in the coming months.
paras.zh: 虽然泽西岛的医用大麻产业不断发展，但岛上的一些人希望走得更远。 2024年，岛上议会以一票之差否决了休闲大麻合法化的投票。当该岛当时的卫生部长将其带回再次投票时，它在辩论之前就被撤回了。预计该法案将在未来几个月内重新提交议会审议。

paras.en: Some individuals on the island have decided not to wait. By exploiting a loophole in current laws, they have made Jersey one of the only places in Europe outside of Amsterdam where THC products can be purchased and consumed legally.
paras.zh: 岛上的一些人决定不再等待。通过利用现行法律的漏洞，他们使泽西岛成为欧洲除阿姆斯特丹之外唯一可以合法购买和消费 THC 产品的地方之一。

paras.en: One morning in February 2024, Gary Tucker arrived at work, his weed shop in St Helier, Jersey, to find a dozen customs officers and the local media waiting outside. It was a raid—and not his first. The officers emptied shelves and boxes into bin bags. “They were literally running their arms down the shelves and putting everything into bags. They took everything,” Tucker, a California native and former analyst in the US Army, told WIRED.
paras.zh: 2024 年 2 月的一天早上，加里·塔克 (Gary Tucker) 来到他位于泽西岛圣赫利尔的杂草店上班，发现十几名海关官员和当地媒体在外面等候。这是一次突袭——而且不是他的第一次。警察将架子和盒子清空到垃圾袋中。 “他们真的把手臂伸到货架上，把所有东西都放进袋子里。他们拿走了所有东西，”加州人、前美国陆军分析师塔克告诉《连线》杂志。

paras.en: Tucker operates outside of Jersey’s medical cannabis industry. His shop, Bailiwick Botanicals, sells products that are clearly recreational: hash cakes, gummies, and other snacks, all infused with tetrahydrocannabinol (THC), the psychoactive ingredient in cannabis that gets you high and is heavily controlled.
paras.zh: 塔克在泽西岛的医用大麻行业之外开展业务。他的 Bailiwick Botanicals 商店销售的产品显然是休闲性的：哈希蛋糕、软糖和其他零食，全部都添加了四氢大麻酚 (THC)，这是大麻中的一种精神活性成分，可以让人兴奋，并且受到严格控制。

paras.en: He’s able to do this owing to a loophole in Jersey law which allows the sale of products containing CBD—another critical ingredient in cannabis, but one that doesn’t get you high. Jersey’s law says that the amount of THC in CBD products cannot exceed 3 percent of the weight of the CBD. So, if you want to sell products with high levels of THC, you just have to boost the CBD. “It’s just a math equation,” Tucker says.
paras.zh: 他之所以能够做到这一点，是因为泽西岛法律存在一个漏洞，该法律允许销售含有 CBD 的产品，CBD 是大麻的另一种关键成分，但不会让人兴奋。泽西岛法律规定 CBD 产品中 THC 的含量不能超过 CBD 重量的 3%。因此，如果你想销售 THC 含量高的产品，你只需要提高 CBD 的含量即可。 “这只是一个数学方程，”塔克说。

paras.en: Tucker admits it isn’t an ideal situation: studies suggest that ingesting high levels of CBD can cause liver damage. But he sees that as an issue with the regulation, not his solution. “I’m just following consumer demand,” he says.
paras.zh: 塔克承认这不是一个理想的情况：研究表明摄入高浓度的 CBD 会导致肝脏损伤。但他认为这是监管的问题，而不是他的解决方案。 “我只是在关注消费者的需求，”他说。

paras.en: Tucker is somewhat evangelical about the properties of cannabis. In his time as a weapons trainer for the military, he struggled with the mental health impacts of hearing that recruits he had trained had been killed in action. “I needed to step back from it. It started to really affect my mind,” Tucker says.
paras.zh: 塔克对大麻的特性有些乐观。在担任军队武器训练师期间，当他听说自己训练的新兵在行动中阵亡时，他的心理健康受到了影响。 “我需要退出它。它开始真正影响我的思想，”塔克说。

paras.en: Veterans he knew were turning to cannabis, and Tucker began buying it on the black market. “It was the only thing that helped me,” he says. ”Cannabis gave me my life back.”
paras.zh: 他认识的退伍军人正在转向大麻，塔克开始在黑市上购买大麻。 “这是唯一对我有帮助的事情，”他说。 “大麻让我重获新生。”

paras.en: Tucker currently manufactures most of his products in the US before shipping them to Sark—a smaller Channel Island best known for having no cars and also its own government—and then to Jersey. New regulations in the US, however, mean Tucker may need to change his approach.
paras.zh: 塔克目前在美国生产大部分产品，然后将其运往萨克岛（一个较小的海峡岛屿，以没有汽车和自己的政府而闻名），然后运往泽西岛。然而，美国的新规定意味着塔克可能需要改变他的做法。

paras.en: Tucker sees Jersey as a potential export hub for THC products to Europe. He believes Jersey’s budding weed industry should push beyond medical cannabis and into the recreational market. “This isn’t just a bunch of guys in a cellar somewhere. Not only does cannabis help people, but getting it to the shelf creates jobs. From the grower to the retailer. It permeates across all industries. We’re making cosmetics. We’re making gummies. We’re making drinks,” he says.
paras.zh: 塔克将泽西岛视为 THC 产品向欧洲的潜在出口中心。他认为泽西岛新兴的杂草产业应该超越医用大麻并进入娱乐市场。 “这不仅仅是地窖里的一群人。大麻不仅能帮助人们，而且把它放在货架上还能创造就业机会。从种植者到零售商。它渗透到所有行业。我们在生产化妆品。我们在生产软糖。我们在生产饮料，”他说。

paras.en: After the 2024 raid, Bailiwick Botanicals shut its doors for two weeks, and its full stock wasn’t returned until six months later. As of June 2026, Tucker and his team are selling THC-infused fudge, chocolate, and other sweets. His newest product, THC-infused coffee beans, is selling well. The police have stayed away.
paras.zh: 2024 年突袭后，Bailiwick Botanicals 关门两周，直到六个月后才归还全部库存。截至 2026 年 6 月，塔克和他的团队正在销售添加 THC 的软糖、巧克力和其他糖果。他的最新产品，添加 THC 的咖啡豆，卖得很好。警察已经远离了。

paras.en: In a written statement to WIRED, Jersey’s government said that the “possibility of abuse of our limits to get round the law in other jurisdictions is a matter of concern to the Government of Jersey and we are looking at ways to address it. Work is underway to consider whether Jersey’s existing legal exemptions for CBD products require amendment.”
paras.zh: 在给《连线》杂志的一份书面声明中，泽西岛政府表示，“泽西岛政府担心滥用我们的限制来规避其他司法管辖区法律的可能性，我们正在寻找解决方案。目前正在考虑泽西岛对 CBD 产品的现有法律豁免是否需要修改。”

paras.en: For his part, Tan is reluctant to be drawn on his views on the so-called “rec” (recreational) market. For now, Jersey still has harsh sentencing rules on recreational cannabis use, with the penalties for possession and possession with intent to supply remaining up to five years and 14 years in jail, respectively. The proposed (and withdrawn) law to decriminalize cannabis notes that, the way the law is currently written, someone who rolled three joints and gave one to a friend would be guilty of supply and receive a criminal record. “Without change, people will continue receiving serious criminal records for small amounts … punishments [that] can result in additional harms greater than the drug itself,” it said.
paras.zh: 就谭而言，他不愿透露自己对所谓“休闲”市场的看法。目前，泽西岛对娱乐性大麻的使用仍然有严厉的量刑规则，持有和意图供应大麻的处罚分别最高可达 5 年和 14 年监禁。拟议的（已撤回的）大麻非刑罪化法律指出，根据目前法律的编写方式，如果某人卷了三个大麻并将一根送给朋友，则将犯有供应罪并获得犯罪记录。 “如果不做出改变，人们将继续因少量的犯罪记录而受到严重的犯罪记录……惩罚可能会导致比毒品本身更大的额外伤害，”报告称。

paras.en: While Jersey makes its own laws, however, it may not be able to completely legalize cannabis. Jersey is a signatory to the UN Convention on drugs control via the UK, and the UK Home Office would undoubtedly have a view if the island were to set itself up as an “Amsterdam on the Sea.” In 2022, an effort by the government of Bermuda (a British Overseas Territory) to legalize recreational cannabis was blocked after the UK withheld Royal Assent from the bill.
paras.zh: 然而，虽然泽西岛制定了自己的法律，但它可能无法完全使大麻合法化。泽西岛是通过英国签署的《联合国毒品管制公约》的签署国，如果将该岛打造成“海上阿姆斯特丹”，英国内政部无疑会有意见。 2022 年，百慕大（英国海外领土）政府在英国拒绝批准该法案后，休闲大麻合法化的努力遭到阻碍。

paras.en: Back at the Northern Leaf warehouse in the Jersey parish of St Lawrence, Tan is flipping the lids off large boxes and rifling through clear plastic bags packed full of cannabis.
paras.zh: 回到泽西岛圣劳伦斯教区的北叶仓库，谭正在打开大箱子的盖子，翻阅装满大麻的透明塑料袋。

paras.en: This is all weed that will not be sold, either because there were issues with production or the THC levels were too low. Instead, it is taken to a secure area of the facility where it is locked away in a reinforced armored vault. Specialist staff with bodycams take the bags to the island’s incinerator, where it is unceremoniously burned, as required by law.
paras.zh: 这些都是不会出售的杂草，要么是因为生产出现问题，要么是 THC 含量太低。相反，它被带到设施的安全区域，锁在加固的装甲库中。配备随身摄像机的专业工作人员将这些袋子送到岛上的焚化炉，并按照法律要求将其毫不客气地焚烧。

paras.en: Tan regularly makes a case to the government for changes to the law and support for the cannabis industry, such as an industrial energy tariff to help with spiraling energy costs.
paras.zh: 谭定期向政府提出修改法律和支持大麻产业的理由，例如工业能源关税，以帮助应对不断上升的能源成本。

paras.en: He has claimed that Jersey could be home to “the Monsanto of cannabis,” alluding to the agricultural giant that was acquired by pharmaceutical company Bayer in 2018 for $66 billion. He’d like to get deeper into the genetics of cannabis, form a tissue-culture lab, and “bring out strains that nobody has ever seen.”
paras.zh: 他声称泽西岛可能是“大麻界孟山都”的所在地，指的是这家农业巨头，该公司于 2018 年被制药公司拜耳以 660 亿美元收购。他想更深入地研究大麻的遗传学，建立一个组织培养实验室，并“培育出从未见过的菌株”。

paras.en: But speaking of himself, he references a different genre of business: He’s Willy Wonka, but for weed. Thirty years ago, when Tan quit corporate finance, his father warned him that he could make a lot more money if he stayed in banking. “And you know what, he was right,” he says. “But I would not have had nearly as much fun.”
paras.zh: 但说到他自己，他提到了一种不同的商业类型：他是威利·旺卡，但他是大麻。三十年前，当谭退出公司财务时，他的父亲警告他，如果他留在银行业，他可以赚更多的钱。 “你知道吗，他是对的，”他说。 “但我不会有那么多乐趣。”

articles.title: Nvidia launches probe into reported Chinese spy effort targeting CEO

paras.en: Nov. 8 (UPI) -- Semiconductor behemoth Nvidia announced Sunday that it has launched an independent investigation into reports that its high-profile co-founder was targeted by "a foreign intelligence effort."
paras.zh: 11 月 8 日（UPI）——半导体巨头英伟达周日宣布，已对其知名联合创始人成为“外国情报机构”目标的报道展开独立调查。

paras.en: "While the Board has no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, the Board's inquiry will examine all available information," Nvidia said in a statement.
paras.zh: 英伟达在一份声明中表示：“虽然董事会没有理由相信国家安全或英伟达的机密遭到泄露，但董事会的调查将检查所有可用信息。”

paras.en: Nvidia's co-founder and CEO Jensen Huang "fully supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it," it said.
paras.zh: 英伟达联合创始人兼首席执行官黄仁勋“完全支持此次审查，并承诺与其合作”。

paras.en: The investigation follows reports that Jensen Huang, a Taiwan-born American executive, was in an intimate relationship with Alice Huang, a top executive with Singapore-based Megaspeed, whom the Trump administration alleges was recruited to spy on the Nvidia head for China.
paras.zh: 此前有报道称，台湾出生的美国高管黄仁勋与新加坡 Megaspeed 高管 Alice Huang 关系密切，特朗普政府称后者被招募来监视英伟达中国区负责人。

paras.en: U.S.-based Nvidia manufactures some of the world's most advanced artificial intelligence chips. Megaspeed purchases these sought-after electronics components that the United States has placed export controls on to prevent them from being exported to China, where they could be used for surveillance, military and artificial intelligence advancements.
paras.zh: 总部位于美国的英伟达生产一些世界上最先进的人工智能芯片。 Megaspeed 购买了这些广受欢迎的电子元件，美国对其实施了出口管制，以防止它们出口到中国，这些元件可用于监视、军事和人工智能进步。

paras.en: Jensen Huang, a close adviser to President Donald Trump, has been a vocal critic of U.S. restrictions on exporting advanced AI chips to China.
paras.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统的亲密顾问黄仁勋一直直言不讳地批评美国限制向中国出口先进人工智能芯片。

paras.en: On Oct. 29, The New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence officials believed Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset who developed a close relationship with Jensen Huang. In a follow-up report on Friday, The Times reported that an intelligence memo circulated among senior Trump administraiton policymakers last spring alleged that she had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to spy on Jensen Huang. The Financial Times on Friday was the first to report that their relationship was romantic.
paras.zh: 10月29日，《纽约时报》报道称，美国情报官员认为黄爱丽是中国情报人员，与黄仁勋关系密切。在周五的后续报道中，《泰晤士报》报道称，去年春天在特朗普政府高级政策制定者中流传的一份情报备忘录称，她被中国国家安全部招募来监视黄仁勋。周五，英国《金融时报》率先报道了他们的恋情。

paras.en: Jensen Huang, who is married and has two children with Lori Huang, acknowledged being unfaithful in a letter to Nvidia employees, a copy of which was sent to UPI.
paras.zh: 已婚并与 Lori Huang 育有两个孩子的黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 在给 Nvidia 员工的一封信中承认自己不忠，该信的副本已发送给 UPI。

paras.en: "I owe my family and all of you an apology. I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did," he said in the letter, which does not identify the person he had the affair with.
paras.zh: 他在信中说：“我欠我的家人和你们所有人一个道歉。我对我的妻子不忠。我的行为伤害了她和我们的孩子。我的所作所为没有任何借口。”信中没有透露与他有染的人是谁。

paras.en: "Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, Nvidia's Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security."
paras.zh: “对于新闻报道中提出的国家安全担忧，英伟达董事会已启动独立调查。我支持调查并将全力配合。我爱我们的国家和我们的公司。我致力于保护英伟达并支持美国的国家安全。”

paras.en: Nvidia said the investigation will be overseen by a committee of independent directors and assisted by outside counsel.
paras.zh: 英伟达表示，调查将由独立董事委员会监督，并由外部律师协助。

paras.en: Concerning Jensen Huang's position at Nvidia's helm, the board said it has "confidence" in his leadership team and will "provide further updates as appropriate."
paras.zh: 关于黄仁勋在英伟达掌舵人的职位，董事会表示对他的领导团队“有信心”，并将“酌情提供进一步的更新”。

paras.en: An Nvidia spokesperson told UPI in an emailed statement that news of the affair and investigation will not affect the company.
paras.zh: Nvidia 发言人在一份电子邮件声明中告诉 UPI，该事件和调查的消息不会影响该公司。

paras.en: "Today's news will not slow Nvidia down. Jensen is committed to continuing to lead Nvidia as CEO without interruption," the spokesperson said.
paras.zh: “今天的消息不会让英伟达放慢脚步。詹森致力于继续以首席执行官的身份不间断地领导英伟达，”该发言人表示。

articles.title: Iran warns U.S. to accept war-ending proposal or risk renewed fighting

paras.en: Nov. 9 (UPI) -- Iran on Sunday warned the United States to accept its proposal for ending the war and opening the Strait of Hormuz or risk renewed fighting.
paras.zh: 11月9日（合众社）——伊朗周日警告美国接受其结束战争和开放霍尔木兹海峡的提议，否则将面临重新爆发战斗的风险。

paras.en: "Our 2-day proposal stands: meet the requirements, including end to war on all fronts, and you will see results. Or choose war, and see our alert and battle-hardened Warriors rain down hell," Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi said in a social media statement.
paras.zh: 伊朗外交部长赛义德·阿巴斯·阿拉格奇在社交媒体声明中表示：“我们为期两天的建议是：满足要求，包括在所有方面结束战争，你们就会看到结果。或者选择战争，然后看到我们警觉的、身经百战的战士如雨点般落入地狱。”

paras.en: The warning came amid a stalemate in the war, now in its ninth month, and ongoing negotiations that have yet to produce a diplomatic breakthrough.
paras.zh: 这一警告是在战争陷入僵局之际发出的，目前已进入第九个月，谈判仍在进行，但尚未取得外交突破。

paras.en: Speaking to reporters Sunday before heading to Paris for the G7 foreign ministers meeting, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said he didn't have much progress to report concerning a diplomatic agreement on ending the war.
paras.zh: 周日，在前往巴黎参加七国集团外长会议之前，国务卿马可·卢比奥对记者表示，关于结束战争的外交协议，他没有太多进展需要报告。

paras.en: "I wouldn't say we're on a verge of a breakthrough," he said.
paras.zh: “我不会说我们正处于突破的边缘，”他说。

paras.en: "The president would always prefer to solve this and every problem diplomatically. Sometimes that's not possible, unfortunately. But if there's a chance to do it, we'll explore it. Right now it hasn't been very productive, because the Iranian demands are simply not just unacceptable, but in some cases, outrageous and ridiculous and really not realistic."
paras.zh: “总统总是更愿意通过外交方式解决这个问题和所有问题。不幸的是，有时这是不可能的。但如果有机会这样做，我们会探索它。目前效果不是很好，因为伊朗的要求不仅不可接受，而且在某些情况下是令人愤慨和荒谬的，而且真的不现实。”

paras.en: In an interview with CNN on Sunday, Trump said whether U.S. strikes would resume depended on "whether or not they sign a very strong agreement." However, he said a return to open hostilities was "highly unlikely."
paras.zh: 特朗普周日在接受美国有线电视新闻网采访时表示，美国是否会恢复打击取决于“他们是否签署了一项非常强有力的协议”。不过，他表示，重新爆发公开敌对行动“极不可能”。

paras.en: "I would if necessary, but we hit them really hard. I hit them so hard. You don't know how hard I hit them," he told CNN's Jim Sciutto in the telephone interview.
paras.zh: 他在电话采访中对美国有线电视新闻网（CNN）的吉姆·休托（Jim Sciutto）表示：“如果有必要的话，我会的，但我们对他们的打击真的很大。我对他们的打击非常大。你不知道我对他们的打击有多大。”

paras.en: "So, it's highly unlikely I'll have to. They're withering away financially. We've hit them militarily. We could finish them off."
paras.zh: “所以，我不太可能不得不这样做。他们在经济上正在萎缩。我们已经在军事上打击了他们。我们可以消灭他们。”

paras.en: The negotiations center in part on the vital Strait of Hormuz energy route, through which Iran has militarily restricted transit through following the initial U.S.-Israeli attack on Feb. 28.
paras.zh: 谈判的部分重点是重要的霍尔木兹海峡能源路线，在2月28日美国和以色列发动首次袭击后，伊朗已对通过该海峡的过境进行了军事限制。

paras.en: Specifics of the proposal have not been entirely made public, but Araghchi said it would see the United States first meet several conditions on the first day of its implementation, including lifting sanctions, reducing its military presence in the region and unfreezing Iranian assets, while Tehran would, on the second day, reopen shipping lanes through the Strait of Hormuz.
paras.zh: 该提案的具体细节尚未完全公开，但阿拉格奇表示，美国将在实施第一天首先满足几个条件，包括解除制裁、减少在该地区的军事存在以及解冻伊朗资产，而德黑兰将在第二天重新开放穿过霍尔木兹海峡的航道。

paras.en: Negotiations have been ongoing since at least Sept. 22, when U.S. and Iranian representatives held indirect talks through mediators on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly. Early this month, Araghchi said negotiations on a proposed two-day plan were being conducted through Qatari mediators, Iran state-run Press TV reported.
paras.zh: 谈判至少从 9 月 22 日起就一直在进行，当时美国和伊朗代表在联合国大会期间通过调解人进行了间接会谈。据伊朗国营新闻电视台报道，本月初，阿拉格奇表示正在通过卡塔尔调解人就拟议的为期两天的计划进行谈判。

paras.en: What began as a joint U.S.-Israeli military operation targeting Iran's nuclear and military capabilities, accompanied by calls for regime change, has morphed into a protracted war.
paras.zh: 最初的美国和以色列针对伊朗核和军事能力的联合军事行动，伴随着要求政权更迭的呼吁，已经演变成一场旷日持久的战争。

articles.title: Ben Barnes: Tim and the kids are hunted after challenging 'Institute'

paras.en: NEW YORK, Nov. 9 (UPI) -- Season 1 of The Institute ended with the shocking revelation that psychically gifted children were being drained of their energy in an effort to prevent global disasters.
paras.zh: 纽约，11 月 9 日（合众国际社）——《研究所》第一季以令人震惊的揭露结束：为了防止全球性灾难，有天赋的儿童正在耗尽他们的能量。

paras.en: The big questions that followed then are, is this true? and, even if it is, is it worth torturing and killing kids for a "greater good" determined by a shadowy government agency?
paras.zh: 接下来的大问题是，这是真的吗？即使是这样，为了一个影子政府机构所决定的“更大的利益”而折磨和杀害孩子是否值得？

paras.en: Deciding the human cost is too high, former police detective Tim (Ben Barnes) rescues several teens held captive at the show's titular Maine facility.
paras.zh: 前警探蒂姆（本·巴恩斯饰）认为人员伤亡太高，于是营救了几名被关押在剧中缅因州设施中的青少年。

paras.en: Season 2 of MGM+'s Stephen King book adaptation kicked off Sunday with Tim and the kids on the run, but trying to find a journalist who will believe their story and help them free others being experimented on.
paras.zh: 米高梅+改编自斯蒂芬·金小说的第二季于周日拉开帷幕，蒂姆和孩子们在逃亡，但他们试图找到一位愿意相信他们的故事并帮助他们释放其他被实验者的记者。

paras.en: "What you're looking for in the protagonists in a series like this are characters who will always question the tactics of those in power and, I think, in this instance, obviously, the kids represent the next generation. They represent innocence," Barnes, 45, told UPI in a recent Zoom interview.
paras.zh: 45 岁的巴恩斯在最近的 Zoom 采访中告诉合众国际社：“在这样的连续剧中，你要寻找的主角是那些总是质疑当权者策略的人物，我认为，在这种情况下，孩子们显然代表了下一代。他们代表着纯真。”

paras.en: "It fields interesting questions through the series that the characters kind of dig into of doing the right thing for the greatest number of people, versus protecting the people that you care about and the people that you love," he said. "It's kind of an age-old story. There's always a president with a daughter who's been kidnapped. He's got to make that kind of decision."
paras.zh: 他说：“这部剧提出了一些有趣的问题，角色们深入探讨了为最大多数人做正确的事情，而不是保护你关心的人和你爱的人。” “这是一个古老的故事。总有一位总统的女儿被绑架了。他必须做出这样的决定。”

paras.en: The group forms a found family as they try to gather evidence about what is going on, while staying off the grid so the authorities can't find them.
paras.zh: 该小组组建了一个被发现的家庭，试图收集有关正在发生的事情的证据，同时远离网络，以免当局找不到他们。

paras.en: "Season 2 is very physical and exciting and they're also being hunted. So, it's a question of are they evading and hiding, or are they going to strike back against the powers that be?" Barnes said.
paras.zh: “第二季非常激烈、刺激，而且他们也遭到追捕。所以，问题是他们是在逃避和躲藏，还是会反击现有的力量？”巴恩斯说。

paras.en: "The more interesting story is always going to be finding a way to use what they've got to fight back."
paras.zh: “更有趣的故事总是会找到一种方法来利用他们所拥有的东西来反击。”

paras.en: Joe Freeman, 19, plays Luke, a teen with the gifts of telepathy and pre-cognition.
paras.zh: 19 岁的乔·弗里曼 (Joe Freeman) 饰演卢克 (Luke)，一名具有心灵感应和预知能力的青少年。

paras.en: "We are the next ones up and we'll have to fix the problems that were caused," he said.
paras.zh: “我们是下一个，我们必须解决由此造成的问题，”他说。

paras.en: Even though Luke and Tim are very close, they aren't always on the same page, particularly when Luke is reading Tim's thoughts without permission.
paras.zh: 尽管卢克和蒂姆关系非常亲密，但他们并不总是意见一致，尤其是当卢克未经许可阅读蒂姆的想法时。

paras.en: "There's a bit of a rift that divides us, unfortunately," Freeman said.
paras.zh: “不幸的是，我们之间存在一些裂痕，”弗里曼说。

paras.en: Barnes added: "There was one line a couple of episodes into the season where the kids are using telepathy to speak to each other and Tim is still not about that. Tim is like, 'Hey, if you're going to speak,[do it] out loud!'"
paras.zh: 巴恩斯补充道：“在这一季的几集里，有一句台词是孩子们使用心灵感应互相交谈，而蒂姆仍然不这么认为。蒂姆就像是，‘嘿，如果你要说话，就大声说出来！’”

paras.en: This season also sees the addition of Game of Thrones alum Alfie Allen as tech giant Nolan Reeves.
paras.zh: 本季还邀请了《权力的游戏》演员阿尔菲·艾伦饰演科技巨头诺兰·里维斯。

paras.en: "I was very excited that Alfie Allen was joining the cast. Having known him for a long time, I am a big fan of his acting and I thought he was a great choice to represent the man behind the man behind the man behind the money," Barnes said.
paras.zh: “我很高兴阿尔菲·艾伦加入演员阵容。认识他很长时间了，我是他表演的忠实粉丝，我认为他是代表金钱背后的人的绝佳选择，”巴恩斯说。

paras.en: "He was very safe. He, obviously, knew what to do and that made my job a lot easier and he is a good laugh," Freeman added. "I like him a lot. Great guy."
paras.zh: “他非常安全。显然，他知道该做什么，这让我的工作轻松多了，而且他很开朗，”弗里曼补充道。 “我非常喜欢他。很棒的人。”

articles.title: Druski’s Best ‘SNL’ Sketches Had Him Singing Through a Proposal Gone Wrong & In a Hip-Hop Parody
articles.author: Ashley Iasimone

paras.en: Druski made his SNL hosting debut on an episode that had The Strokes as musical guest, but it was Druski crooning “she said yes” at the just the right comedic moment that was the real earworm of the show.
paras.zh: 德鲁斯基在《周六夜现场》节目中首次主持，The Strokes 担任音乐嘉宾，但德鲁斯基在恰到好处的喜剧时刻低声低吟“她说是”才是该节目真正的耳目一新。

paras.en: “Proposal” and “Golden Age of Hip-Hop,” two of the funniest sketches to make it to air Saturday night (Nov. 7), had the SNL host showing he’s got a knack for musical comedy — and some vocal talent.
paras.zh: 《求婚》和《嘻哈黄金时代》是周六晚（11 月 7 日）播出的两部最有趣的短剧，这位《周六夜现场》主持人展示了他在音乐喜剧方面的天赋以及一些声乐天赋。

paras.en: In “Proposal,” SNL‘s Jeremy Culhane plays a man asking his girlfriend (Sarah Sherman) to marry him, and things don’t quite go as planned. But since he assumed she’d say yes and went all-out on making the proposal an unforgettable moment, the show goes on for his hired entertainment — Druski, expertly leading an awkward musical finale that was meant to celebrate the engagement.
paras.zh: 在《求婚》中，《周六夜现场》的杰里米·卡尔哈恩饰演一名男子向女友（莎拉·谢尔曼饰）求婚，但事情并没有按计划进行。但由于他以为她会答应，并全力以赴地让求婚成为一个难忘的时刻，演出继续进行，他聘请了娱乐节目——德鲁斯基，熟练地主持了一场尴尬的音乐结局，旨在庆祝订婚。

paras.en: “I don’t really know how to tell you this, but the next four minutes are about to be really tough,” Culhane says when Sherman turns him down.
paras.zh: “我真的不知道如何告诉你这一点，但接下来的四分钟将非常艰难，”当谢尔曼拒绝他时，卡尔哈恩说道。

paras.en: And then all eyes (and ears) are on Druski and an ensemble that keeps growing around him as he belts with soul: “She said yes, oh, she said yes/ Can’t wait to see her wearing that dress/ Got down on one knee and she said yes.”
paras.zh: 然后所有的眼睛（和耳朵）都集中在德鲁斯基身上，当他充满灵魂时，他周围的整体不断壮大：“她说是的，哦，她说是的/迫不及待地想看到她穿那件衣服/单膝跪下，她说是的。”

paras.en: One of the other highlights of the episode was the final sketch, “Golden Age of Hip-Hop,” a TV documentary-style parody telling the story of a “socially conscious hip-hop” group called Lenny & The Street Smart Crew (Druski, James Austin Johnson, Ben Marshall, Kam Patterson and Tommy Brennan). The bit has the Druski-led crew performing songs like “Gangs Ain’t Good (Free Yo Mind)” and “You Can Be My Brother, Friend.”
paras.zh: 这一集的另一个亮点是最后的小品《嘻哈黄金时代》，这是一部电视纪录片风格的戏仿作品，讲述了一个名为 Lenny & The Street Smart Crew（Druski、James Austin Johnson、Ben Marshall、Kam Patterson 和 Tommy Brennan）的“具有社会意识的嘻哈”团体的故事。由 Druski 领导的团队表演了《Gangs Ain’t Good (Free Yo Mind)》和《You Can Be My Brother, Friend》等歌曲。

paras.en: When Druski was announced as a season 52 host for Saturday Night Live, he got plenty of support from his hip-hop friends. Among those sending him congratulatory comments were Drake, Travis Scott, Quavo and Wheezy.
paras.zh: 当 Druski 被宣布担任《周六夜现场》第 52 季主持人时，他得到了嘻哈朋友们的大力支持。 Drake、Travis Scott、Quavo 和 Wheezy 等人向他发送了祝贺。

paras.en: Watch Druski in Saturday night’s “Proposal” and “Golden Age of Hip-Hop” sketches below.
paras.zh: 观看周六晚上德鲁斯基的“求婚”和“嘻哈黄金时代”草图。

articles.title: Morgan Wallen, Garth Brooks, Taylor Swift & More Artists With Most Weeks at No. 1 on Top Country Albums Chart: Full List
articles.author: Paul Grein

paras.en: Morgan Wallen’s I’m the Problem leads Billboard‘s Top Country Albums chart (dated Nov. 14) for the 52nd nonconsecutive week. This ups Wallen’s career tally of weeks at No. 1 to 238, allowing him to extend his lead as the artist with the most weeks at No. 1 in the chart’s 62-year history.
paras.zh: 摩根·沃伦 (Morgan Wallen) 的《I'm the Problem》连续第 52 周在 Billboard 乡村专辑排行榜（日期为 11 月 14 日）上名列前茅。这使得 Wallen 在职业生涯中排名第一的周数上升至 238 周，从而扩大了他作为该排行榜 62 年历史上排名第一周数最多的艺人的领先地位。

paras.en: Wallen’s achievement is especially impressive because he has amassed this hefty total of weeks at No. 1 in such a short amount of time. He first topped the chart a little more than six years ago — on Aug. 15, 2020.
paras.zh: 沃伦的成就尤其令人印象深刻，因为他在如此短的时间内积累了如此多的周时间排名第一。他首次登顶排行榜是在六年多前，即 2020 年 8 月 15 日。
