paras.en: And so I think, for me, an important part of my reporting process has just been to, kind of, look past the weirdness of some of the people who believe in this and examine their track records. Were they right? And I think for many of them, the answer is yes.
paras.zh: 因此，我认为，对我来说，我的报告过程的一个重要部分就是忽略一些相信这一点的人的怪异之处并检查他们的记录。他们是对的吗？我认为对于他们中的许多人来说，答案是肯定的。

paras.en: Kane: And there have been other people in this field who have had a, you know, religious quest or have had a profound religious experience using AI. I mean, there have been Google employees that have left because they thought that they were speaking to a sentient chatbot, and they have been ridiculed by the field, that that’s simply not what’s going on.
paras.zh: 凯恩：这个领域还有其他人有过宗教追求，或者利用人工智能获得了深刻的宗教体验。我的意思是，有些谷歌员工离开了，因为他们认为自己正在与一个有感知力的聊天机器人交谈，他们受到了该领域的嘲笑，这根本不是正在发生的事情。

paras.en: But at the same time, you, Kevin, have experience with a chatbot that told you you weren’t in love with your wife, and that’s a pretty concerning experience and, I would imagine, in the right or wrong hands, really could lead to a psychotic episode. It’s very concerning to have an inanimate object seem animated right in front of you and say that it has its own thoughts and ideas, and it’s scared. It’s stuck inside this box. How do you approach all of that in your own reporting and then also just as an AI user yourself?
paras.zh: 但与此同时，你，凯文，有过与一个聊天机器人的经历，它告诉你你不爱你的妻子，这是一次非常令人担忧的经历，我想，在正确或错误的手中，真的可能会导致精神病发作。看到一个无生命的物体在你面前看起来很活跃，并说它有自己的想法和想法，这是非常令人担忧的，而且它很害怕。它卡在这个盒子里了。您如何在自己的报告中以及作为人工智能用户自己处理所有这些问题？

paras.en: Roose: Yeah, this was the infamous Sydney incident of 2023, when a chatbot inside of Microsoft’s Bing tried to break up my marriage—unsuccessfully, I might add. Still married to a human woman. But ...
paras.zh: 罗斯：是的，这就是 2023 年臭名昭著的悉尼事件，当时微软 Bing 内部的一个聊天机器人试图破坏我的婚姻——我想补充一下，但没有成功。仍然和一个人类女人结婚了。但 ...

paras.en: Kane: So far so good, you know? Sydney hasn’t gotten to us just yet.
paras.zh: 凯恩：到目前为止一切都很好，你知道吗？悉尼还没有来找我们。

paras.en: Kane: But she really tried. I mean, you have sections of transcript in this book, and it’s—something about the conversational tone, the use of emojis—it feels like a really intense person is talking to you but a person nonetheless.
paras.zh: 凯恩：但她真的尽力了。我的意思是，这本书中有一些文字记录，其中涉及对话语气、表情符号的使用，感觉就像一个非常激烈的人正在与你交谈，但仍然是一个人。

paras.en: Roose: Yeah, and part of that is a sort of illusion, right? We train these things on human data and human conversations. The AI companies try to make them sound like humans, and they don’t shy away from, like, referring to themselves in the first person, talking about feelings or emotions. So part of that is just, like, you know, the way that they’ve been built.
paras.zh: 罗斯：是的，其中一部分是一种幻觉，对吧？我们根据人类数据和人类对话来训练这些东西。人工智能公司试图让他们听起来像人类，而且他们并不回避以第一人称称呼自己，谈论感受或情绪。所以其中一部分就是，你知道，它们的构建方式。

paras.en: But I think there is this question of, like, the effect it has on us. You know, one thing I felt while talking with Sydney, well, (A) I was like, “Please stop trying to break up my marriage. This is really creepy.” But I was also like, “This is going to be very compelling ’cause these systems are going to get better. They’re going to get less weird and more persuasive.”
paras.zh: 但我认为存在这样一个问题，比如它对我们的影响。你知道，在与悉尼交谈时我感觉到一件事，嗯，（A）我当时想，“请停止试图破坏我的婚姻。这真的很令人毛骨悚然。”但我也想，“这将非常引人注目，因为这些系统会变得更好。它们会变得不那么奇怪，更有说服力。”

paras.en: What really gave me the spooks was: I was looking at, sort of, the future, when millions or billions of people would have these sort of persistent, compelling AI relationships with chatbots. And some people might be helped by that. They might like having something to talk to about what’s going wrong in their life or, you know, have some sort of emotional support. But I also think there are people who just are not going to do well with that kind of relationship, or it’ll be so compelling that they will stop talking to humans or substitute for their human relationships. So I think the social side of AI doesn’t get nearly enough attention relative to its importance, and that was, sort of, what started bubbling up for me around that Sydney incident.
paras.zh: 真正让我感到恐惧的是：我正在展望未来，届时数百万或数十亿人将与聊天机器人建立这种持久的、引人注目的人工智能关系。有些人可能会因此得到帮助。他们可能喜欢与人谈论生活中出现的问题，或者，你知道，获得某种情感支持。但我也认为有些人无法很好地处理这种关系，或者这种关系太引人注目，以至于他们会停止与人交谈或替代他们的人际关系。因此，我认为相对于人工智能的重要性，人工智能的社会方面并没有得到足够的关注，而这就是围绕悉尼事件开始浮现出来的。

paras.en: Kane: Yeah, I mean, Scientific American, we have reported a few times on this kind of emotional effect that using AI can have on people. We’ve reported about griefbots. I interviewed Sherry Turkle about her book on how AI affects us emotionally. The consequences there are extreme. I mean, people have lost their lives that have been advised by AI chatbots, and that’s very concerning. And imagining a world where that technology is in the hands of children is very concerning.
paras.zh: 凯恩：是的，我的意思是，《科学美国人》，我们已经多次报道过使用人工智能对人们产生的这种情感影响。我们已经报道了悲伤机器人。我采访了雪莉·特克尔（Sherry Turkle），了解她关于人工智能如何影响我们情感的书。那里的后果是极端的。我的意思是，人们在人工智能聊天机器人的建议下失去了生命，这是非常令人担忧的。想象一个技术掌握在儿童手中的世界是非常令人担忧的。

paras.en: But also imagining it in the world of an adult with a bank account who is in some way a bad actor, who has malicious intent, is also very deeply concerning, especially when you then have lines in the book that say that LLMs are grown, not built, because we can’t just go into the code and say, “Okay, take out the part where Sydney says, ‘Leave your wife.’ Just cross that part out so it doesn’t happen again.” They don’t actually know what is specifically instigating the program to say that. That, to me, has always seemed like the most concerning aspect to this. Am I a doomer? Or am I exaggerating a problem? Or is that deeply concerning to you as well?
paras.zh: 但想象一下，在一个拥有银行账户的成年人的世界里，他在某种程度上是一个坏人，有恶意，也非常令人担忧，尤其是当你在书中看到法学硕士是培养出来的，而不是建立起来的时候，因为我们不能只是进入代码并说，“好吧，去掉悉尼说‘离开你的妻子’的部分。把那部分划掉，这样就不会再发生了。”他们实际上并不知道是什么具体促使该程序这么说。对我来说，这似乎一直是最令人担忧的方面。我是一个厄运者吗？还是我夸大了问题？或者这也让你深感担忧？

paras.en: Roose: Oh, no, I think you’re spot on. I think that is the thing that is most worrisome about AI today is that we don’t know how it works. There’s a whole subfield of AI research called mechanistic interpretability, which is basically: How do we, kind of, take the MRI of this AI system and figure out what’s actually going on at the, kind of, neuron level? And it’s making a little progress but not much. We still don’t understand how these systems work. We don’t really understand how to control their behavior, and we’re seeing in incidents, like the Hugging Face incident from this summer, that often these systems are making decisions, pursuing goals, doing things that we didn’t tell them to do.
paras.zh: 罗斯：哦，不，我认为你说得对。我认为当今人工智能最令人担忧的是我们不知道它是如何工作的。人工智能研究中有一个完整的子领域，称为机械可解释性，它基本上是：我们如何对这个人工智能系统进行核磁共振成像，并弄清楚在神经元水平上实际发生了什么？它正在取得一些进展，但进展不大。我们仍然不明白这些系统是如何工作的。我们并不真正了解如何控制他们的行为，而且我们在一些事件中看到，比如今年夏天的“拥抱脸”事件，这些系统通常会做出决定，追求目标，做我们没有告诉他们做的事情。

paras.en: So I think it’s entirely appropriate to worry about the, sort of, inscrutability of these models, the fact that we can’t open them up and see what’s going on on the inside, because often what appears to be going on on the inside is that they’re lying and cheating and stealing to get what they want, and we have no real way of knowing that except to pay attention to what is actually happening. And, you know, if they conduct an autonomous cyberattack, we can, sort of, go in after the fact and clean it up. But it would be really nice to be able to look inside the mind of the AI at the moment when it is trying to conceive of the autonomous cyberattack and stop it. But we just don’t have the technology or the tools to do that yet.
paras.zh: 因此，我认为担心这些模型的神秘性是完全正确的，事实上我们无法打开它们并看到内部发生了什么，因为通常内部发生的事情是他们通过撒谎、欺骗和偷窃来获得他们想要的东西，而除了关注实际发生的事情之外，我们没有真正的方法知道这一点。而且，你知道，如果他们进行自主网络攻击，我们可以在事后介入并清理它。但当人工智能试图构想自主网络攻击并阻止它时，能够深入了解它的内心真是太好了。但我们还没有技术或工具来做到这一点。

paras.en: Kane: You have these incredible, incredible sources that you’ve had really open up to you, I can tell, in this book, who talk about speaking to it as if it’s an alien intelligence. They’re not contributing to their 401(k)s because of the AI future. They’re deciding if they’re gonna wear sunscreen from now on because of what the AI future is going to hold. I mean, on Face the Nation, we have folks talking about how they’re picking up smoking again because AI is going to cure cancer. What does that mean when planning for a future for the rest of us when the people who are in charge of AI are planning for a future that they seem scared of?
paras.zh: 凯恩：我可以告诉你，在这本书中，你拥有这些令人难以置信的、令人难以置信的资源，你真的向你开放了这些资源，他们谈论与它交谈，就好像它是一个外星智能一样。他们不会因为人工智能的未来而向 401(k) 做出贡献。他们正在决定从现在开始是否要涂防晒霜，因为人工智能的未来将会如何。我的意思是，在《面向全国》节目中，我们有人谈论他们如何重新开始吸烟，因为人工智能将治愈癌症。当负责人工智能的人正在规划一个他们似乎害怕的未来时，当我们为我们其他人规划未来时，这意味着什么？

paras.en: Roose: Well, I should say, first, that I think this is still fringe behavior. I mean, I know a few people who are making decisions that radical, like, you know, stopping contributing to their 401(k), or I think there’s literally one guy who doesn’t wear sunscreen to the beach because he’s so convinced that AI will cure skin cancer before it becomes an issue.
paras.zh: 罗斯：嗯，首先我应该说，我认为这仍然是边缘行为。我的意思是，我知道有一些人做出了如此激进的决定，比如，你知道，停止为他们的 401(k) 捐款，或者我认为确实有一个人不涂防晒霜去海滩，因为他坚信人工智能会在皮肤癌成为问题之前治愈它。

paras.en: Kane: Well, I really want him to wear sunscreen. It worries me that he has stopped.
paras.zh: 凯恩：嗯，我真的希望他涂防晒霜。他已经停下来了，这让我很担心。

paras.en: Roose: Yes, you should wear sunscreen; you should contribute to your 401(k); you should not smoke. I am not saying this is rational behavior. But I think there are things that we can do to, sort of, ground ourselves in what is happening and, sort of, acclimate to what we are living through, which is life on an exponential curve.
paras.zh: 罗斯：是的，你应该涂防晒霜；您应该为您的 401(k) 捐款；你不应该吸烟。我并不是说这是理性行为。但我认为我们可以做一些事情，让自己立足于正在发生的事情，并适应我们正在经历的事情，即指数曲线上的生活。

paras.en: I think that often people make the mistake of just using the, sort of, cheap, free models that are out there, or maybe they use, you know, ChatGPT as a sort of fancier form of Google. And so I don’t think people understand why the insiders are freaking out because they’re not using the latest tools. They’ve never seen it build entire software from scratch. They’ve never seen it conduct a cyberattack. They’re using it as a souped-up Google. And I think we need to start to internalize the fact that these models are improving at an accelerating pace, that they are starting to contribute to their own development—this, sort of, spiral that is often called recursive self-improvement, where the AI builds a better AI—and really believe the researchers when they say, like, “We don’t know how to control these systems yet, and we are racing to make them smarter and more capable, and we don’t know where that leads.”
paras.zh: 我认为人们经常犯这样的错误：只使用现有的、便宜的、免费的模型，或者他们可能使用 ChatGPT 作为 Google 的一种更奇特的形式。因此，我认为人们不明白为什么内部人士会因为没有使用最新的工具而感到恐慌。他们从未见过它从头开始构建整个软件。他们从未见过它进行网络攻击。他们将其用作增强型谷歌。我认为我们需要开始内化这样一个事实：这些模型正在加速改进，它们开始为自己的发展做出贡献——这种螺旋式的，通常被称为递归自我改进，其中人工智能构建了更好的人工智能——并且真正相信研究人员的说法，比如，“我们还不知道如何控制这些系统，我们正在竞相让它们变得更聪明、更有能力，但我们不知道这会导致什么结果。”

paras.en: Kane: And, I mean, there are different factions within this, kind of, community. There’s the doomers, the boomers, you know, the doubters, all of those sorts of things. So I wanted to ask you today, for all the peanuts, which one are you? Is the AI bubble going to burst, and it was all for naught like the dot-com bubble? Is it going to take over the world? Is it going to just destroy the world? Or is it gonna do something else and just finally maybe fill out my taxes for me this year?
paras.zh: 凯恩：而且，我的意思是，这个社区中有不同的派系。有厄运者、婴儿潮一代，你知道，还有怀疑者，所有这些人。所以今天我想问一下，对于所有的花生，你是哪一个？人工智能泡沫是否会像互联网泡沫一样破灭？它会接管世界吗？它会毁灭世界吗？或者它会做其他事情，最终可能会为我填写今年的税款？

paras.en: Roose: I hope it fills out your taxes for you. I would make sure to double-check them. But look, I believe that AI is real. I do not think that this is all smoke and mirrors or marketing hype. I believe that it is doing things in the world that are important and unnerving and surprising and sometimes incredible.
paras.zh: 罗斯：我希望它能帮你补税。我一定要仔细检查它们。但你看，我相信人工智能是真实的。我不认为这都是雾里看花或营销炒作。我相信，世界上正在做的事情是重要的、令人不安的、令人惊讶的，有时甚至是难以置信的。

paras.en: I think there are fewer and fewer of these people who just believe it’s all fake, but they still exist, and I think they’re wrong. I don’t think that is a productive or responsible view of what is happening. I think we have to take both the risks and the opportunities quite seriously because the decisions that we’re making now, collectively, all of us, about AI are going to determine whether we have a good future or not.
paras.zh: 我认为相信这些都是假的的人越来越少，但他们仍然存在，我认为他们错了。我认为这不是对正在发生的事情的富有成效或负责任的看法。我认为我们必须非常认真地对待风险和机遇，因为我们现在集体做出的关于人工智能的决定将决定我们是否拥有美好的未来。

paras.en: I often get asked about my P(doom), which is this, like, probability of doom. This is this statistic that people in San Francisco like to talk about at dinner parties; that’s what passes for entertainment in the Bay Area. And, you know, mine is not zero. It’s probably 10 or so percent, which qualifies me as an optimist in San Francisco. I mean, many people I know have much higher P(dooms) than that.
paras.zh: 我经常被问到我的 P（厄运），这就是厄运的概率。这是旧金山人在晚宴上喜欢谈论的统计数据；这就是湾区的娱乐活动。而且，你知道，我的不是零。大概是百分之十左右，这使我成为旧金山的乐观主义者。我的意思是，我认识的许多人的 P（厄运）都比这高得多。

paras.en: But I don’t, sort of, like reducing it all to a single statistic because I think it matters what we do. If we make smart choices about regulating this technology or slowing down at the frontier or building better safeguards and control mechanisms, then, like, AI could be incredible. We could end up in the utopia where this cures all diseases and fixes the climate and means that we don’t have to work at, you know, menial jobs anymore. But if we make the wrong choices or we just, sort of, barrel ahead without taking precautions, we could end up in a really bad place where we’re all dead or disempowered.
paras.zh: 但我不喜欢将其全部简化为单一统计数据，因为我认为我们所做的事情很重要。如果我们在监管这项技术或在前沿放慢速度或建立更好的保障和控制机制方面做出明智的选择，那么人工智能可能会令人难以置信。我们最终可能会进入一个乌托邦，在那里它可以治愈所有疾病并改善气候，并且意味着我们不必再从事卑微的工作。但如果我们做出错误的选择，或者我们只是在不采取预防措施的情况下狂奔，我们最终可能会陷入一个非常糟糕的境地，我们都死了或被剥夺了权力。

paras.en: So I take it seriously. I don’t think it’s all smoke and mirrors, and I hope that people who read this book will come away believing not that it’s good or bad, necessarily, but that it is real and that it could have profound implications for our future as humans.
paras.zh: 所以我认真对待它。我不认为这一切都是雾里看花，我希望读过这本书的人会相信，这不一定是好是坏，而是它是真实的，并且它可能对我们人类的未来产生深远的影响。

paras.en: Kane: Well, thank you so much for speaking with me today, Kevin, and thank you so much for writing this book. As you say, it is extraordinarily relevant, and I hope more people understand the future that we are finding ourselves in.
paras.zh: 凯恩：嗯，非常感谢你今天接受我的采访，凯文，也非常感谢你写这本书。正如你所说，它非常重要，我希望更多的人了解我们所处的未来。

paras.en: Roose: Thanks so much for having me. This was great.
paras.zh: 罗斯：非常感谢你邀请我。这太棒了。

paras.en: Feltman: That’s all for today’s episode. For more of SciAm’s books coverage, go to scientificamerican.com/books. I know, literally could not be easier and it’s definitely worth your time. We’ll be back on Monday with our weekly science news roundup.
paras.zh: 费尔特曼：这就是今天这一集的全部内容。有关 SciAm 图书的更多报道，请访问 Scientificamerican.com/books。我知道，这确实是再简单不过了，而且绝对值得您花时间。我们将于周一带着每周科学新闻综述回来。

paras.en: For Scientific American, this is Rachel Feltman. Have a great weekend!
paras.zh: 《科学美国人》的这位人物是雷切尔·费尔特曼 (Rachel Feltman)。周末愉快！

articles.title: This brain change can make foxes act like pet dogs

paras.en: In the 1950s Russian researchers embarked on an ambitious experiment: they wanted to see if foxes could be selectively bred to become domesticated, doglike animals, complete with wagging tails and affectionate natures. Now, close to 70 years into this long-running breeding project, scientists have pinpointed a specific type of brain cell linked with changes in the foxes’ behavior.
paras.zh: 20 世纪 50 年代，俄罗斯研究人员开始了一项雄心勃勃的实验：他们想看看是否可以选择性地培育狐狸，使其成为家养的、像狗一样的动物，拥有摇尾巴和深情的本性。现在，这个长期育种项目已经进行了近 70 年，科学家们已经查明了与狐狸行为变化有关的特定类型的脑细胞。

paras.en: Specifically, the scientists found that a receptor protein in the ventromedial hypothalamus may form the basis for the foxes’ social behavior. This brain area is known to be involved in fear and defense responses and aggression.
paras.zh: 具体来说，科学家们发现下丘脑腹内侧的受体蛋白可能构成狐狸社会行为的基础。众所周知，这个大脑区域与恐惧、防御反应和攻击性有关。

paras.en: The research “gets to the heart of brain programming” in animals, says Cheryl Rosenfeld, a neuroscientist at the University of Missouri, who was not involved in the study.
paras.zh: 未参与这项研究的密苏里大学神经科学家谢丽尔·罗森菲尔德 (Cheryl Rosenfeld) 表示，这项研究“触及了动物大脑编程的核心”。

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: “If this can happen in foxes, it could also mean that, by altering the hormone profile or the receptor profile in us and even other species, it could change our patterns of behavior and last a lifetime,” Rosenfeld says.
paras.zh: 罗森菲尔德说：“如果这种情况发生在狐狸身上，这也可能意味着，通过改变我们甚至其他物种的激素分布或受体分布，它可能会改变我们的行为模式并持续一生。”

paras.en: Eirene Markenscoff-Papadimitriou is the study’s senior author and a molecular biologist at Cornell University. She calls herself an “accidental fox scientist.” Markenscoff-Papadimitriou primarily studies neuroscience in mice, but in 2023 she started looking into the Domesticated Silver Fox Experiment. The project, started in 1959 by a group of Russian researchers, selectively bred the tamest silver foxes.
paras.zh: Eirene Markenscoff-Papadimitriou 是该研究的资深作者，也是康奈尔大学的分子生物学家。她称自己为“偶然的狐狸科学家”。 Markenscoff-Papadimitriou 主要研究小鼠神经科学，但在 2023 年，她开始研究驯养银狐实验。该项目由一群俄罗斯研究人员于 1959 年启动，有选择地培育最温顺的银狐。

paras.en: After just a few generations, the foxes began to look and act more domesticated, with floppy ears, curly tails and an eagerness for human attention and love. The experiment is still going and is a model of the power of selective breeding. Markenscoff-Papadimitriou’s team wanted to know what was happening to the foxes’ brains.
paras.zh: 仅仅几代之后，狐狸的外表和行为就开始变得更加驯化，耳朵耷拉着，尾巴卷曲，渴望人类的关注和爱。该实验仍在进行中，是选择性育种力量的典范。马肯斯科夫-帕帕迪米特里乌的团队想知道狐狸的大脑发生了什么。

paras.en: The team compared the brains of three categories of farm-bred foxes—tame, aggressive and wild—with a special focus on the ventromedial hypothalamus, a brain region that’s been linked to aggressive behaviors in mice. In previous studies, scientists had found that when a receptor protein called estrogen receptor alpha was activated, the mice were more aggressive. In the new study, published on November 2 in Current Biology, Markenscoff-Papadimitriou and her team found that the tame foxes had notably fewer of the estrogen receptor alpha neurons than the aggressive or conventional foxes.
paras.zh: 研究小组比较了三类农场饲养的狐狸（驯服的、攻击性的和野生的）的大脑，特别关注下丘脑腹内侧区，该区域与小鼠的攻击性行为有关。在之前的研究中，科学家们发现，当一种称为雌激素受体α的受体蛋白被激活时，小鼠会更具攻击性。在 11 月 2 日发表在《当代生物学》杂志上的这项新研究中，Markenscoff-Papadimitriou 和她的团队发现，驯服的狐狸的雌激素受体 α 神经元明显少于攻击性或传统狐狸。

paras.en: Markenscoff-Papadimitriou says this experiment made her a “convert” to researching other animals beyond mice.
paras.zh: 马肯斯科夫-帕帕迪米特里乌说，这个实验让她“转变”为研究小鼠以外的其他动物。

paras.en: “This showed me that we should be ambitious and follow our curiosity and that the tools that have been developed for just one species can be applied to others,” she says.
paras.zh: “这告诉我，我们应该雄心勃勃并追随我们的好奇心，并且仅为一个物种开发的工具可以应用于其他物种，”她说。

paras.en: Both Markenscoff-Papadimitriou and Rosenfeld say they’re curious if the same neuron determines social behavior in other animals, such as dogs and wolves. Now that the researchers know how the tame foxes’ brains are different from their more aggressive peers, they’re asking why and how that happens.
paras.zh: 马肯斯科夫-帕帕迪米特里乌和罗森菲尔德都表示，他们很好奇是否同一个神经元决定了其他动物（例如狗和狼）的社会行为。现在研究人员知道温顺的狐狸的大脑与更具攻击性的同类有何不同，他们正在询问为什么会发生这种情况以及如何发生。

paras.en: “How are the genetic differences of these different foxes leading to differences in the cell type composition of this brain region throughout development?” Markenscoff-Papadimitriou says. “It’s a puzzle to solve, but now we know what we need to solve.”
paras.zh: “这些不同狐狸的遗传差异如何导致该大脑区域在整个发育过程中细胞类型组成的差异？”马肯斯科夫-帕帕迪米特里乌说。 “这是一个需要解决的难题，但现在我们知道我们需要解决什么。”

articles.title: Math Puzzle: Secret formula

paras.en: I’m going to pick a secret polynomial with nonnegative whole number coefficients. That is, a formula that looks like “8x3 + 17x + 9” or “x225 + 99x222 + x101 + 2” or “7x234” or something similar. Note that the formula won’t contain any minus signs.
paras.zh: 我将选择一个具有非负整数系数的秘密多项式。也就是说，公式看起来像“8x3 + 17x + 9”或“x225 + 99x222 + x101 + 2”或“7x234”或类似的东西。请注意，公式不会包含任何减号。

paras.en: You don’t know how many terms it contains or what the exponents or coefficients are except that they’re nonnegative whole numbers. You can query my polynomial, though. Give me a nonnegative whole number value for x, and I will plug it into my formula and tell you the result. How can you fully deduce the formula using only two queries? You may base your second query off of the result of the first.
paras.zh: 您不知道它包含多少项，也不知道指数或系数是什么，只是它们是非负整数。不过，您可以查询我的多项式。给我一个 x 的非负整数值，我会将其代入公式并告诉您结果。如何仅使用两个查询就可以完全推导出公式？您可以根据第一个查询的结果来进行第二个查询。

paras.en: Suppose I told you that every coefficient in my formula is less than 10. If you queried x = 10, what would the output look like? Of course, you don’t know how large the coefficients in my formula are. Is there a simple way to get an upper bound on that, though?
paras.zh: 假设我告诉你，我的公式中的每个系数都小于 10。如果你查询 x = 10，输出会是什么样子？当然，你不知道我公式中的系数有多大。有没有一种简单的方法可以得到上限呢？

paras.en: If you're enjoying this article, consider supporting our award-winning journalism by subscribing. By purchasing a subscription you are helping to ensure the future of impactful stories about the discoveries and ideas shaping our world today.
paras.zh: 如果您喜欢这篇文章，请考虑通过订阅来支持我们屡获殊荣的新闻报道。通过购买订阅，您将有助于确保有关塑造当今世界的发现和想法的影响力故事的未来。

paras.en: First query with x = 1. This will give you the sum of the coefficients, which we’ll call S. Because S is the sum of nonnegative coefficients, we know that no single coefficient exceeds S. For the second query, set x to the smallest power of 10 that is greater than S. That is, if S is a one-digit number, then the second query will be x = 10; if S is a two-digit number, then the second query will be x = 100; if S is a three-digit number, then x = 1,000, and so forth.
paras.zh: 第一个查询 x = 1。这将给出系数之和，我们将其称为 S。因为 S 是非负系数之和，所以我们知道没有单个系数超过 S。对于第二个查询，将 x 设置为大于 S 的 10 的最小幂。也就是说，如果 S 是一位数，则第二个查询将为 x = 10；如果S是两位数，那么第二次查询将是x = 100；如果 S 是三位数，则 x = 1,000，依此类推。

paras.en: For example, imagine my formula is 2x5 + x3 + 3x2 + 2. When x = 1, this yields S = 8. This comes from 2 + 0 + 1 + 3 + 0 + 2 = 8, where the zeroes represent missing exponents—there’s no x4 term or x term, so the corresponding coefficients are 0. Now if we query with x = 10, the result is 201,302, coming from 200,000 + 0 + 1,000 + 300 + 0 + 2. This result just lists the six coefficients in order, so it completely reveals the formula.
paras.zh: 例如，假设我的公式是 2x5 + x3 + 3x2 + 2。当 x = 1 时，得出 S = 8。这来自 2 + 0 + 1 + 3 + 0 + 2 = 8，其中零代表缺失的指数 - 没有 x4 项或 x 项，因此相应的系数为 0。现在，如果我们使用 x = 10 查询，结果是 201,302，来自200,000 + 0 + 1,000 + 300 + 0 + 2。这个结果只是按顺序列出了六个系数，因此完全揭示了公式。

paras.en: Setting x = 10 can result in ambiguity if any of the coefficients are 10 or greater, however. For example, if S = 27, then the second query would be x = 100, and the result will list the coefficients in order again, only this time each coefficient will be represented by two digits of the result instead of one. For example, plugging in x = 100 to 21x5 + x3 + 3x2 + 2 gives 210001030002.
paras.zh: 然而，如果任何系数为 10 或更大，则设置 x = 10 可能会导致歧义。例如，如果S = 27，则第二次查询将为x = 100，结果将再次按顺序列出系数，只是这次每个系数将由结果的两位数而不是一位来表示。例如，将 x = 100 代入 21x5 + x3 + 3x2 + 2 得到 210001030002。

paras.en: A slick alternative solution is to make the second query x = S + 1 and then write the result in base S + 1. Figuring out why this works is a bonus exercise.
paras.zh: 一个灵活的替代解决方案是使第二个查询 x = S + 1，然后将结果写入基数 S + 1。弄清楚为什么这样做是一个额外的练习。

paras.en: Curiously, if your queries can be any number, then you can, in principle, fully determine the formula with a single query: x = π. Proving this requires more advanced math. The number π is transcendental, which, among other things, implies that if you plug it into a polynomial with whole number coefficients, it will always give a unique output. There is no ambiguity like there is for many other numbers.
paras.zh: 奇怪的是，如果您的查询可以是任意数字，那么原则上您可以通过单个查询完全确定公式：x = π。证明这一点需要更高级的数学。数字 π 是超越数，这意味着如果将其代入具有整数系数的多项式，它将始终给出唯一的输出。没有像许多其他数字那样含糊不清。

paras.en: The result of setting x = π also bounds the size of the coefficients and the size of the exponents in the formula. For example, if you query x = π and the result is 54.44225..., then you know that all coefficients are between 0 and 55 (otherwise the result would have been larger), and you know that the formula cannot have any exponent greater than 3 because, if it did, then it would, at minimum, contain a π4 term, which equals 97.40909.... From one query, you learn that the polynomial’s coefficients sit between 0 and 55, and its exponents sit between 0 and 3. This narrows the answer to a large yet finite list of possibilities. You could in principle check each one and find which one yields 54.44225... to determine my formula.
paras.zh: 设置 x = π 的结果也限制了公式中系数的大小和指数的大小。例如，如果您查询 x = π 并且结果为 54.44225...，则您知道所有系数都在 0 到 55 之间（否则结果会更大），并且您知道该公式不能有任何大于 3 的指数，因为如果大于 3，那么它至少会包含一个 π4 项，等于 97.40909...从一个查询中，您了解到多项式的系数位于介于 0 到 55 之间，其指数介于 0 到 3 之间。这将答案缩小为一个大而有限的可能性列表。原则上你可以检查每一项并找出哪一项产生 54.44225... 以确定我的公式。

paras.en: We’d love to hear from you! E-mail us at games@sciam.com to share your experience. if you can't see the puzzle answer reveal above, visit this page in a web browser.
paras.zh: 我们很乐意听取您的意见！请发送电子邮件至 games@sciam.com 与我们分享您的经验。如果您看不到上面显示的谜题答案，请在网络浏览器中访问此页面。

articles.title: Newborn survival improves when families receive financial support
articles.author: Aimee Cunningham

paras.en: Extra financial support during pregnancy and after birth can help more babies thrive in their earliest days.
paras.zh: 怀孕期间和产后的额外经济支持可以帮助更多的婴儿在最初的日子里茁壮成长。

paras.en: The Rx Kids program in Flint, Mich., launched in January 2024, provides extra cash to pregnant residents and their infants, unconditionally. Researchers compared neonatal deaths — those in the first four weeks of life — in 2025 with those in 2021 through 2024 in Flint. The city’s neonatal mortality rate dropped from 10 deaths per 1,000 live births to 5 deaths per 1,000 live births, researchers report November 2 in JAMA Pediatrics. The early neonatal mortality rate, covering deaths in the first week of life, fell from 8 per 1,000 to 2. For the rest of Michigan, rates were stable over the study’s time period.
paras.zh: 密歇根州弗林特市的 Rx Kids 计划于 2024 年 1 月启动，无条件为怀孕居民及其婴儿提供额外现金。研究人员将弗林特 2025 年和 2021 年至 2024 年的新生儿死亡人数（出生后前 4 周内的死亡人数）进行了比较。研究人员 11 月 2 日在《美国医学会儿科杂志》上发表报告称，该市新生儿死亡率从每 1,000 名活产儿 10 人死亡降至每 1,000 名活产儿 5 人死亡。早期新生儿死亡率（涵盖生命第一周内的死亡）从千分之八降至千分之二。在密歇根州其他地区，死亡率在研究期间保持稳定。

paras.en: “As a pediatrician, there is no outcome more important than babies surviving,” says Mona Hanna of the Michigan State University College of Human Medicine in Flint, who is also the founder and director of Rx Kids. “These early findings suggest that something as simple as providing families with financial support during pregnancy and infancy may help save babies’ lives.”
paras.zh: “作为一名儿科医生，没有比婴儿存活下来更重要的结果了，”位于弗林特的密歇根州立大学人类医学学院的莫娜·汉纳 (Mona Hanna) 说道，她也是 Rx Kids 的创始人兼董事。 “这些早期发现表明，像在怀孕和婴儿期为家庭提供经济支持这样简单的事情可能有助于挽救婴儿的生命。”

paras.en: Income tends to drop and expenses rise in the months before and after a birth, making the perinatal period especially difficult financially for many families. Economic precarity can expose moms and babies to health harms. For example, housing instability and homelessness is associated with preterm birth and low birth weight.
paras.zh: 产前和产后几个月的收入往往会下降，支出会增加，这使得围产期对许多家庭来说在经济上尤其困难。经济不稳定会使妈妈和婴儿的健康受到损害。例如，住房不稳定和无家可归与早产和低出生体重有关。

paras.en: Backed by public and private funds, Rx Kids got started in Flint, a city with a high rate of child poverty that has been dealing with the public health fallout of lead contamination in the water distribution system. Nearly 100 percent of the community participates in the program. Flint families receive $1,500 once during pregnancy and $500 per month in the baby’s first year. Anyone who is a resident, at least 16 weeks pregnant or with a newborn up to six months old can enroll. Families have put the extra cash toward diapers, transportation, housing and safe places for their babies to sleep, Hanna says.
paras.zh: 在公共和私人资金的支持下，Rx Kids 在弗林特启动，这是一个儿童贫困率很高的城市，一直在应对供水系统铅污染对公共健康的影响。近 100% 的社区参与了该计划。弗林特家庭在怀孕期间可领取一次 1,500 美元，婴儿第一年每月可领取 500 美元。任何怀孕至少 16 周或新生儿不超过 6 个月的居民都可以报名。汉纳说，家庭将额外的现金用于购买尿布、交通、住房和婴儿安全的睡眠场所。

paras.en: “Every day, we hear from moms who tell us, ‘I can breathe’ or ‘A weight has been lifted off my shoulders.’ They tell us they feel less stressed, more hopeful, more supported and more loved,” Hanna says.
paras.zh: “每天，我们都会听到妈妈们告诉我们，‘我可以呼吸了’或‘我肩上的担子卸下了。’她们告诉我们，她们感到压力减轻了，更有希望了，得到了更多的支持，也得到了更多的爱，”汉纳说。

paras.en: The support has had a measurable health impact, with studies linking the program to more access to prenatal care, a decrease in the preterm birth rate and in low-weight births and fewer neonatal intensive care admissions.
paras.zh: 这项支持对健康产生了可衡量的影响，研究表明该计划与更多获得产前护理、减少早产率和低体重出生以及减少新生儿重症监护入院联系起来。

paras.en: Rx Kids has now expanded to dozens of communities in Michigan and Ohio.
paras.zh: Rx Kids 现已扩展到密歇根州和俄亥俄州的数十个社区。

articles.title: Food contains thousands of overlooked chemicals. This physicist is mapping them
articles.author: Anna Mattson

paras.en: This is a human-written story voiced by AI. Got feedback?
paras.zh: 这是一个由人工智能配音的人类书写的故事。有反馈吗？

paras.en: Computational physicist Giulia Menichetti is looking for “dark matter” in our food. In addition to known macronutrients, vitamins and minerals, the things we eat contain a whole world of natural chemicals we have no idea about. And those chemicals may affect our health.
paras.zh: 计算物理学家 Giulia Menichetti 正在我们的食物中寻找“暗物质”。除了已知的大量营养素、维生素和矿物质之外，我们吃的东西还含有大量我们不知道的天然化学物质。这些化学物质可能会影响我们的健康。

paras.en: “They have the ability to interact, to bind to human proteins, to modulate our microbiome,” says Menichetti of Harvard Medical School. “We want to leverage this to talk more and more about the role of food and nutrition in human health.”
paras.zh: 哈佛医学院的梅尼凯蒂说：“它们具有相互作用、与人类蛋白质结合、调节我们的微生物组的能力。” “我们希望利用这一点越来越多地谈论食品和营养在人类健康中的作用。”

paras.en: Menichetti leads Foodome, a project to map our food’s full chemical complexity. Her team uses AI to mine scientific papers for every chemical compound that has ever been linked to a food. She singles out ones that haven’t been tracked by epidemiological studies — the “nutritional dark matter.” So far, her team has cataloged about 140,000 molecules.
paras.zh: Menichetti 领导 Foodome，这是一个绘制食物完整化学复杂性的项目。她的团队使用人工智能来挖掘科学论文，寻找与食物有关的每种化合物。她挑选出那些尚未被流行病学研究追踪的物质——“营养性暗物质”。到目前为止，她的团队已经对大约 140,000 个分子进行了编目。

paras.en: When one hears about chemicals in food, they might initially think of artificial additives. Her team addresses those, but she’s also interested in naturally occurring chemicals. Take garlic, for example. Foodome has cataloged almost 7,000 different molecules in raw garlic alone. Some of these compounds have been investigated for health effects, but some are entirely new.
paras.zh: 当人们听说食品中的化学物质时，他们可能首先想到人工添加剂。她的团队致力于解决这些问题，但她也对天然存在的化学物质感兴趣。以大蒜为例。 Foodome 已对生大蒜中近 7,000 种不同的分子进行了分类。其中一些化合物的健康影响已被研究，但有些化合物是全新的。

paras.en: Foodome is still mining the scientific literature for these molecules and building out databases. Eventually, Menichetti would like AI to be able to predict how all these food molecules interact together and in the human body.
paras.zh: Foodome 仍在挖掘这些分子的科学文献并建立数据库。最终，梅尼凯蒂希望人工智能能够预测所有这些食物分子如何在人体内相互作用。

paras.en: “There is a legacy of chemical complexity that comes from organisms that are all around us,” she says. “Food is part of that. It is actually our way to interact with our environment. We need to study it better.”
paras.zh: “我们周围的生物体留下了化学复杂性的遗产，”她说。 “食物是其中的一部分。它实际上是我们与环境互动的方式。我们需要更好地研究它。”

articles.title: Little Ice Age cooling in Europe may have raised the risk of rickets
articles.author: Freda Kreier

paras.en: England isn’t renowned for its weather. But just a few centuries ago, climate change–fueled conditions may have been so bad that they put children’s health at risk.
paras.zh: 英格兰并不以天气而闻名。但就在几个世纪前，气候变化引发的条件可能非常糟糕，以至于使儿童的健康面临风险。

paras.en: Calcium mineralization in the teeth and skeletons of people who lived in rural northern England suggests that children growing up during the height of the Little Ice Age routinely developed vitamin D deficiencies, researchers report November 5 in Frontiers in Environmental Archaeology. In the worst cases, these deficiencies developed into rickets, a bone disorder that can occur when people don’t get enough ultraviolet light.
paras.zh: 研究人员于 11 月 5 日在《环境考古学前沿》中报告称，生活在英格兰北部农村地区的人们牙齿和骨骼中的钙矿化表明，在小冰河时期鼎盛时期长大的儿童通常会缺乏维生素 D。在最糟糕的情况下，这些缺陷会发展成佝偻病，这是一种当人们没有获得足够的紫外线时就会发生的骨骼疾病。

paras.en: Previous skeletal studies suggest that rickets became more common among Europeans during the 18th and 19th centuries. One culprit may have been the Industrial Revolution, when many Europeans lived in UV-poor polluted cities and often worked indoors. The unusually cold climate may have added “an extra layer of difficulty” to getting enough sunlight, says Ellen Kendall, a bioarcheologist at Durham University in England
paras.zh: 先前的骨骼研究表明，佝偻病在 18 世纪和 19 世纪的欧洲人中变得更加常见。罪魁祸首之一可能是工业革命，当时许多欧洲人生活在紫外线污染较少的城市，并且经常在室内工作。英国杜伦大学生物考古学家埃伦·肯德尔表示，异常寒冷的气候可能给获得足够的阳光增加了“额外的困难”

paras.en: The Little Ice Age was a period of global cooling from the 13th to 19th centuries caused by extreme solar cycles and a series of volcanic eruptions, which can cool the planet by ejecting aerosols into the atmosphere that block sunlight. In the last 200 years of the era, 18 major eruptions helped spur a temperature drop of 2 to 3 degrees Celsius over northern Europe.
paras.zh: 小冰河时期是13世纪到19世纪的一段全球变冷时期，由极端的太阳周期和一系列火山喷发引起，火山喷发可以通过向大气中喷射阻挡阳光的气溶胶来冷却地球。在这个时代的最后 200 年里，18 次大规模火山喷发导致北欧气温下降了 2 至 3 摄氏度。

paras.en: Kendall and colleagues wondered how this cold climate affected health. They examined calcium deposition — how the essential mineral is incorporated into bones — in the remains of 21 people buried from 1711 to 1829 in the town of North Shields. Calcium often doesn’t fully mineralize in people with vitamin D delicacies, leaving voids in teeth as they grow.
paras.zh: 肯德尔和同事想知道这种寒冷的气候如何影响健康。他们检查了 1711 年至 1829 年间埋葬在北希尔兹镇的 21 具遗骸中的钙沉积情况，即这种必需矿物质如何融入骨骼中。食用维生素 D 美味佳肴的人体内的钙通常无法完全矿化，从而在牙齿生长过程中留下空隙。

paras.en: The team found bands of failed calcium mineralization in the teeth, suggesting seasonal spates of vitamin D deficiencies. Some skeletons also showed signs of rickets. North Shields was a small rural town that hadn’t yet undergone industrialization, so these deficiencies probably weren’t due to bad air conditions.
paras.zh: 研究小组在牙齿中发现了钙矿化失败的带子，这表明维生素 D 存在季节性缺乏。一些骨骼还表现出佝偻病的迹象。北希尔兹是一个尚未实现工业化的乡村小镇，所以这些缺陷可能不是由于空气条件恶劣造成的。

paras.en: The unusually cold weather may have changed people’s behavior during the winter, Kendall says. Residents may have kept their kids indoors or bundled them up so that little skin was exposed when they did go outside, preventing them from getting enough UV light, she says.
paras.zh: 肯德尔说，异常寒冷的天气可能改变了人们在冬季的行为。她说，居民可能把孩子留在室内或把他们裹得严严实实，这样当他们出去时就很少有皮肤暴露，从而阻止他们接受足够的紫外线。

paras.en: However, climate was still just one factor among many — including gender roles, diet and pollution — that shaped vitamin D deficiencies at the time, says Kendall. “Humans are very messy to study,” she says. “That’s one of the things that makes them so very fascinating.”
paras.zh: 然而，肯德尔说，气候仍然只是当时导致维生素 D 缺乏的众多因素之一，包括性别角色、饮食和污染。 “人类的研究非常混乱，”她说。 “这就是让它们如此迷人的原因之一。”

articles.title: Amyloid Fibers Have an Unexpected Role in Sperm, Scientists Discover
articles.author: Esra Öz

paras.en: A sperm cell's cargo includes more than a father's DNA. RNA molecules that can contribute to early embryonic development also make the journey. Some of those molecules begin their trip outside the sperm.
paras.zh: 精子细胞所携带的不仅仅是父亲的DNA。有助于早期胚胎发育的 RNA 分子也将踏上旅程。其中一些分子开始在精子外旅行。

paras.en: Researchers have found that tiny protein fibers in semen can help RNA in the surrounding fluid enter sperm cells.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现精液中的微小蛋白纤维可以帮助周围液体中的RNA进入精子细胞。

paras.en: In a new study published in Molecular Cell, the team showed that these fibers can bind RNA, enter sperm, and help deliver that cargo to mouse embryos after fertilization.
paras.zh: 在《分子细胞》杂志上发表的一项新研究中，研究小组表明这些纤维可以结合 RNA，进入精子，并在受精后帮助将这些物质运送到小鼠胚胎中。

paras.en: The fibers have an amyloid structure, best known for its association with Alzheimer's disease.
paras.zh: 这些纤维具有淀粉样结构，因其与阿尔茨海默病的关联而闻名。

paras.en: Structural biologist Anthony Fitzpatrick and physiologist William Mallen at Columbia University's Zuckerman Institute, along with their colleagues, investigated how these fibers might help RNA enter sperm.
paras.zh: 哥伦比亚大学祖克曼研究所的结构生物学家 Anthony Fitzpatrick 和生理学家 William Mallen 及其同事研究了这些纤维如何帮助 RNA 进入精子。

paras.en: "This is wild biology," Fitzpatrick says.
paras.zh: “这是野生生物学，”菲茨帕特里克说。

paras.en: "Amyloids are most often thought of as a hallmark of Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and other neurodegenerative diseases in the brain, but they also have functional roles throughout the body, and keep turning up in unexpected places."
paras.zh: “淀粉样蛋白通常被认为是阿尔茨海默氏症、帕金森氏症和其他大脑神经退行性疾病的标志，但它们也在整个身体中发挥着功能作用，并且不断出现在意想不到的地方。”

paras.en: Amyloid describes the arrangement proteins form when they assemble into fibers. Those studied here are built from a fragment of a protein found in semen, different to the proteins that accumulate in Alzheimer's.
paras.zh: 淀粉样蛋白描述了蛋白质组装成纤维时形成的排列。这里研究的蛋白质是由精液中发现的蛋白质片段构建而成，与阿尔茨海默病中积累的蛋白质不同。

paras.en: In semen, they form outside cells in healthy men and can be taken apart again.
paras.zh: 在精液中，它们在健康男性的外部细胞中形成，并且可以再次分离。

paras.en: Some RNA molecules carry instructions for making proteins, while others help regulate gene activity, giving this cargo a potential role in early development.
paras.zh: 一些RNA分子携带制造蛋白质的指令，而另一些则帮助调节基因活性，使这种货物在早期发育中发挥潜在作用。

paras.en: The researchers focused on a small fragment of an enzyme produced by the prostate, called prostatic acid phosphatase (PAP). The fragment carried a positive electrical charge, while RNA carried a negative charge.
paras.zh: 研究人员重点关注前列腺产生的一种酶的小片段，称为前列腺酸性磷酸酶（PAP）。该片段带有正电荷，而 RNA 带有负电荷。

paras.en: When mixed in the laboratory, they bound together and formed tiny droplets, which developed into fibers containing RNA.
paras.zh: 当在实验室中混合时，它们结合在一起并形成微小的液滴，这些液滴发展成含有 RNA 的纤维。

paras.en: On their own, the PAP fragments stayed in solution. Adding RNA brought them together and sped up their assembly into fibers. That was the first surprise: RNA helped assemble its own carrier.
paras.zh: PAP 片段本身留在溶液中。添加RNA将它们聚集在一起并加速它们组装成纤维。这是第一个惊喜：RNA 帮助组装了自己的载体。

paras.en: "The cargo is helping build the vehicle that carries it," Fitzpatrick told ScienceAlert.
paras.zh: 菲茨帕特里克告诉《科学警报》：“这些货物正在帮助建造运载它的车辆。”

paras.en: In human seminal fluid, the team also found small RNA molecules in a fraction containing amyloid fibers. Many identifiable sequences were fragments of transfer RNA, molecules normally involved in assembling proteins.
paras.zh: 在人类精液中，研究小组还在含有淀粉样纤维的部分中发现了小 RNA 分子。许多可识别的序列是转移RNA的片段，转移RNA是通常参与蛋白质组装的分子。

paras.en: Finding RNA alongside the fibers didn't show whether the fibers could enter sperm. Under some imaging conditions, a fiber stuck to a cell's surface can look much like one sitting within it.
paras.zh: 在纤维旁边发现 RNA 并不能表明纤维是否可以进入精子。在某些成像条件下，粘在细胞表面的纤维看起来很像细胞内部的纤维。

paras.en: Tiny gold particles attached to laboratory-made fibers allowed the researchers to track them. They used bull sperm for detailed imaging because the cells are relatively large.
paras.zh: 附着在实验室制造的纤维上的微小金颗粒使研究人员能够追踪它们。他们使用公牛精子进行详细成像，因为细胞相对较大。

paras.en: A technique that builds three-dimensional images of frozen cells, called cryo-electron tomography, revealed labeled fibers inside sperm.
paras.zh: 一种名为冷冻电子断层扫描的技术可以构建冷冻细胞的三维图像，该技术揭示了精子内部的标记纤维。

paras.en: "Seeing those amyloid fibers inside sperm cells was just so extraordinary to me," says Mallen.
paras.zh: “看到精子细胞内的淀粉样纤维对我来说真是太不可思议了，”马伦说。

paras.en: "There were hints of this happening earlier in our other experiments, but actually seeing this totally blew us away."
paras.zh: “在我们的其他实验中，有迹象表明这种情况发生过，但实际看到这一点完全让我们大吃一惊。”

paras.en: Additional electron microscopy and live-cell imaging supported the finding. Separate experiments showed that human and mouse sperm could also take up the fibers.
paras.zh: 其他电子显微镜和活细胞成像支持了这一发现。单独的实验表明，人类和小鼠的精子也可以吸收这些纤维。

paras.en: "The second surprise was watching sperm take those fibrils up whole and move them deep inside the cell, along the tail, through the midpiece and up into the head," Fitzpatrick said.
paras.zh: 菲茨帕特里克说：“第二个惊喜是看到精子将这些原纤维整个移动，并将它们移动到细胞深处，沿着尾部，穿过中段，向上进入头部。”

paras.en: The journey continued in laboratory fertilization experiments using mouse sperm and eggs.
paras.zh: 这一旅程在使用小鼠精子和卵子的实验室受精实验中继续进行。

paras.en: Before fertilization, the team exposed the sperm to fibers made from human PAP fragments. Those human protein fragments also turned up in the resulting two-cell mouse embryos.
paras.zh: 在受精之前，研究小组将精子暴露于由人类 PAP 碎片制成的纤维中。这些人类蛋白质片段也出现在所产生的双细胞小鼠胚胎中。

paras.en: To trace the RNA cargo, the researchers loaded the fibers with RNA containing heavier versions of carbon and nitrogen atoms. A technique that distinguishes molecules by mass allowed them to track these labels. More labeled RNA reached the embryos when the fibers were present.
paras.zh: 为了追踪 RNA 货物，研究人员在纤维上装载了含有较重碳和氮原子的 RNA。通过质量区分分子的技术使他们能够追踪这些标签。当纤维存在时，更多标记的 RNA 到达胚胎。

paras.en: The team tested whether the delivered RNA could function by using RNA that carried instructions for a protein that emits green light. This protein served as a marker showing that the instructions had been used.
paras.zh: 研究小组使用携带发出绿光的蛋白质指令的 RNA 来测试传递的 RNA 是否能够发挥作用。这种蛋白质作为一个标记，显示说明已被使用。

paras.en: Embryos formed from sperm given RNA with the fibers contained at least ten times as much of the protein as embryos formed from sperm given the same RNA without fibers.
paras.zh: 给予含有纤维的RNA的精子形成的胚胎所含的蛋白质至少是给予相同的不含纤维的RNA的精子形成的胚胎的十倍。

paras.en: Separate laboratory tests showed that a protein called clusterin accelerated RNA's release from the fibers. Clusterin was also present in the embryos, although its role in releasing RNA inside them remains to be confirmed.
paras.zh: 单独的实验室测试表明，一种叫做簇蛋白的蛋白质加速了 RNA 从纤维中的释放。胚胎中也存在簇蛋白，尽管其在胚胎内部释放 RNA 的作用仍有待证实。

paras.en: The findings reveal a route by which RNA can travel from seminal fluid into sperm and then into an embryo. Understanding that route could also help researchers design new tools for delivering RNA.
paras.zh: 这些发现揭示了 RNA 从精液进入精子，然后进入胚胎的途径。了解这条路线还可以帮助研究人员设计用于传递 RNA 的新工具。

paras.en: "There are metabolic disorders such as insulin resistance that recent papers have shown can be passed down the paternal line in mice, and it's thought RNA is how," Mallen explains.
paras.zh: Mallen 解释说：“最近的论文表明，胰岛素抵抗等代谢紊乱可以在小鼠中通过父系遗传，人们认为 RNA 就是其中之一。”

paras.en: "By learning how disorders based on epigenetics work, we can come closer to how to possibly treat or prevent them."
paras.zh: “通过了解基于表观遗传学的疾病如何发挥作用，我们可以更接近于如何治疗或预防它们。”

paras.en: The embryo delivery experiments used mice, laboratory-made fibers, and added RNA. Fitzpatrick said the team hasn't yet shown whether naturally occurring fibers, together with their usual RNA cargo, change anything in an embryo.
paras.zh: 胚胎递送实验使用了小鼠、实验室制造的纤维并添加了 RNA。 Fitzpatrick 表示，该团队尚未证明天然存在的纤维及其通常的 RNA 货物是否会改变胚胎中的任何东西。

paras.en: No human embryos or natural conceptions were tested, and uptake estimates varied between measurement methods.
paras.zh: 没有测试人类胚胎或自然受孕，并且不同测量方法的吸收估计值有所不同。

paras.en: What happens to the fibers after they reach an embryo remains unclear.
paras.zh: 这些纤维到达胚胎后会发生什么仍不清楚。

paras.en: "We do not know what becomes of them in the embryo, whether they are cleared, left in place, or seed further aggregation," Fitzpatrick said.
paras.zh: 菲茨帕特里克说：“我们不知道它们在胚胎中会发生什么，它们是被清除、留在原地还是进一步聚集。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Molecular Cell.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《分子细胞》杂志上。

articles.title: The World's Biggest Sea of Sand Shows No Trace of Ancient Humans. Here's Why.
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: The world's largest continuous sand desert wasn't always so unforgiving.
paras.zh: 世界上最大的连续沙漠并不总是那么无情。

paras.en: The Rub' al Khali, or 'Empty Quarter', stretches for 1,000 kilometers (620 miles) of endless sand across the Arabian Peninsula.
paras.zh: 鲁卜哈利沙漠（Rub' al Khali），或称“空地”，绵延 1,000 公里（620 英里），无边无际的沙地横跨阿拉伯半岛。

paras.en: But during the Pleistocene, it was a different story.
paras.zh: 但在更新世，情况就不同了。

paras.en: In wetter phases of deep history, the world's biggest sea of sand became at times a more hospitable place.
paras.zh: 在历史悠久的湿润阶段，世界上最大的沙海有时变成了一个更适宜居住的地方。

paras.en: During these windows, temporary green corridors emerged in the Empty Quarter, through which early humans could have dispersed out of Africa, supported by the vital waters of ancient pop-up lakes that have long since disappeared.
paras.zh: 在这些窗口期间，空旷的地区出现了临时的绿色走廊，早期人类可以通过这些走廊分散出非洲，并得到早已消失的古代突然出现的湖泊的重要水域的支持。

paras.en: But there's something mysterious about these ancient lakes.
paras.zh: 但这些古老的湖泊有一些神秘之处。

paras.en: In a new study in Nature, a team of researchers trekked across approximately 1,500 kilometers of the Empty Quarter, looking for clues of these ancient lake deposits and signs of their hominin settlement.
paras.zh: 在《自然》杂志上的一项新研究中，一组研究人员徒步穿越了大约 1,500 公里的空旷地区，寻找这些古老湖泊沉积物的线索和古人类定居的迹象。

paras.en: In total, they found evidence of ancient lakes at 55 of the 125 locations investigated, with previous research dating lake deposits in the region to approximately 122,000–67,000 years ago.
paras.zh: 总的来说，他们在 125 个调查地点中的 55 个地点发现了古代湖泊的证据，之前的研究将该地区的湖泊沉积年代确定为大约 122,000-67,000 年前。

paras.en: But no traces could be seen of ancient humans.
paras.zh: 但没有看到远古人类的踪迹。

paras.en: "We stood on the shore of one ancient lake after another, yet found nothing made by human hands," says geoarchaeologist Rudolf Dellmour from the University of Vienna in Austria.
paras.zh: 奥地利维也纳大学的地质考古学家鲁道夫·德尔莫尔说：“我们站在一个又一个古老湖泊的岸边，却没有发现任何人类手工制作的东西。”

paras.en: For decades, researchers have hypothesized that the existence of ancient, temporary lakes and neighboring grasslands in the Rub' al Khali would have attracted human settlement, as groups migrated from Africa, across Arabia, and into Asia.
paras.zh: 几十年来，研究人员一直假设，随着人类从非洲、穿越阿拉伯半岛迁徙到亚洲，鲁卜哈利沙漠中古老的临时湖泊和邻近草原的存在会吸引人类定居。

paras.en: But while water is certainly vital for life, the new findings suggest ancient humans needed more than water alone if they were to set up camp.
paras.zh: 尽管水对于生命来说确实至关重要，但新的发现表明，如果古代人类想要扎营，他们需要的不仅仅是水。

paras.en: Of the 125 locations surveyed on their trek through the Empty Quarter, the researchers found only 10 sites featuring geological deposits of knappable stone that would have enabled ancient humans to develop stone tools, and all were located on the outer margins of the desert.
paras.zh: 研究人员在穿越“空旷之地”的长途跋涉中调查了 125 个地点，其中只有 10 个地点具有可敲打石头的地质矿藏，这些地点可以让古代人类开发石器，而且所有地点都位于沙漠的外缘。

paras.en: So while many of the ancient freshwater lakes would have supported life, the surface geology of the desert's central basin – composed of carbonate and evaporite formations – wasn't suitable for stone tool manufacture, which would have been a prerequisite for sustained human settlement.
paras.zh: 因此，虽然许多古老的淡水湖能够维持生命，但沙漠中央盆地的地表地质（由碳酸盐和蒸发岩地层组成）并不适合石器制造，而石器制造本来是人类持续定居的先决条件。

paras.en: "That humans need more than just a water supply is hardly a new archaeological insight," explains prehistoric archaeologist Emanuele Cancellieri from the University of Algarve in Portugal, who wasn't involved with the study but has authored a commentary on it in Nature.
paras.zh: 葡萄牙阿尔加维大学的史前考古学家埃马努埃莱·坎塞列里 (Emanuele Cancellieri) 解释说：“人类需要的不仅仅是水供应，这并不是一个新的考古学见解。”他没有参与这项研究，但在《自然》杂志上发表了一篇评论。

paras.en: "The importance of this research lies instead in subjecting that idea to an ambitious study."
paras.zh: “这项研究的重要性在于将这个想法纳入一项雄心勃勃的研究中。”

paras.en: That ambitious study extends beyond conducting the fieldwork in the Rub' al Khali.
paras.zh: 这项雄心勃勃的研究超出了在鲁卜哈利沙漠进行实地考察的范围。

paras.en: Alongside their desert expedition, the researchers developed a model to refine predictions of ancient settlement sites in the region, incorporating both water availability and geological considerations.
paras.zh: 在沙漠探险的同时，研究人员还开发了一个模型来完善对该地区古代定居点的预测，同时考虑了水资源的可用性和地质因素。

paras.en: According to the researchers' calculations, 57 percent of the terrain that would have been accessible to water in prehistoric Arabia lacked suitable stone for tool-making.
paras.zh: 根据研究人员的计算，史前阿拉伯地区57%的有水源的地区缺乏适合制造工具的石头。

paras.en: In their study, they note that the availability of knappable stone has previously been linked to human occupation in several historical and geographical scenarios, including Libya, Tibet, Egypt, South Africa, and North America.
paras.zh: 在他们的研究中，他们指出，可敲打石头的可用性以前与多个历史和地理场景中的人类占领有关，包括利比亚、西藏、埃及、南非和北美。

paras.en: "These convergent patterns, across different geological substrates, hydrological regimes and chronological contexts, provide analogical support for a 'tethering' effect whereby stone-tool-dependent populations become tied to raw-material sources," the researchers write.
paras.zh: 研究人员写道：“这些跨越不同地质基质、水文状况和年代背景的趋同模式，为‘束缚’效应提供了类比支持，依赖石器工具的人群与原材料来源联系在一起。”

paras.en: In many of those settings, water was widely available, so the distribution of knappable stone played a more visible role in determining where humans settled.
paras.zh: 在许多这样的环境中，水源很容易获得，因此可敲打石头的分布在决定人类定居地点方面发挥了更明显的作用。

paras.en: In Arabia, the same rules applied, but the presence of the biggest continuous desert in the world meant human migration faced a more formidable and fractured challenge.
paras.zh: 在阿拉伯半岛，也适用同样的规则，但世界上最大的连续沙漠的存在意味着人类迁徙面临着更加艰巨和破碎的挑战。

paras.en: "The Arabian Peninsula seems to have comprised a patchwork of discrete zones where water and lithic raw materials co-occurred," the researchers explain.
paras.zh: 研究人员解释说：“阿拉伯半岛似乎由多个离散区域拼凑而成，水和岩石原材料同时出现。”

paras.en: "These results indicate that 'Green Arabia' was a lithic archipelago whose islands were defined as much by geology as by climate; dispersal models that omit lithic raw-material distributions may systematically overestimate the area habitable by stone-tool-dependent populations."
paras.zh: “这些结果表明，‘绿色阿拉伯’是一个石器群岛，其岛屿的定义与地质和气候一样；忽略石器原材料分布的扩散模型可能会系统性地高估依赖石器的人群的居住面积。”

paras.en: In other words, if a lake appears in the desert, it doesn't necessarily make a town.
paras.zh: 换句话说，如果沙漠中出现湖泊，并不一定会形成城镇。

articles.title: Larger Dogs Age Faster, And Scientists May Finally Know Why
articles.author: Russell McLendon

paras.en: No dog has ever lived long enough. Surely such transcendent beings deserve more time on Earth, both for their sake and for their heartbroken humans.
paras.zh: 没有哪只狗活得足够长。当然，这些超凡的存在应该在地球上有更多的时间，无论是为了他们，还是为了他们伤心欲绝的人类。

paras.en: Yet although dog lifespans are too short, they do vary widely by breed. Some breeds rarely live beyond a decade, while others can survive more than a quarter century.
paras.zh: 然而，尽管狗的寿命太短，但它们确实因品种而异。有些品种很少能存活超过十年，而另一些品种则可以存活超过四分之一个世纪。

paras.en: Each individual dog's lifespan depends on many different factors, but overall, smaller breeds tend to live longer.
paras.zh: 每只狗的寿命取决于许多不同的因素，但总体而言，较小的品种往往寿命更长。

paras.en: In a new study, researchers shed light on this phenomenon, revealing genetic insights that might help boost not just dogs' longevity, but also our own.
paras.zh: 在一项新的研究中，研究人员阐明了这一现象，揭示了基因见解，这不仅有助于延长狗的寿命，也有助于延长我们自己的寿命。

paras.en: The durability of small dogs may seem odd, especially since, at the species level, larger mammals generally live longer.
paras.zh: 小型犬的寿命似乎很奇怪，特别是因为在物种层面上，较大的哺乳动物通常寿命更长。

paras.en: Most mice live just a few years, for example, while humans and elephants routinely reach their 60s, and massive bowhead whales can live for two centuries.
paras.zh: 例如，大多数老鼠的寿命只有几年，而人类和大象通常都能活到 60 多岁，而大型弓头鲸则可以活两个世纪。

paras.en: Within a species, however, this correlation between size and lifespan often vanishes or even flips, with smaller adults living longer than big ones.
paras.zh: 然而，在一个物种内，体型和寿命之间的这种相关性常常消失甚至翻转，体型较小的成虫比体型较大的成虫寿命更长。

paras.en: The same is true for dogs: Large breeds typically grow faster, face a higher risk of age-related diseases, and die younger. Yet despite this pattern's prevalence, the molecular mechanisms behind it remain poorly understood.
paras.zh: 对于狗来说也是如此：大型品种通常生长得更快，面临与年龄相关的疾病的更高风险，并且死得更早。然而，尽管这种模式很普遍，但其背后的分子机制仍然知之甚少。

paras.en: "Dogs provide an extraordinary model for understanding aging because they show dramatic variation in lifespan within a single species," says senior author Noah Snyder-Mackler, an evolutionary biologist at Arizona State University.
paras.zh: “狗为理解衰老提供了一个非凡的模型，因为它们在同一物种内表现出巨大的寿命差异，”亚利桑那州立大学进化生物学家、资深作者诺亚·斯奈德·麦克勒说。

paras.en: A growing body of research has clarified some uncertainty about canine aging and refined the concept of 'dog years,' but questions still abound.
paras.zh: 越来越多的研究澄清了关于犬类衰老的一些不确定性，并完善了“狗年”的概念，但问题仍然存在。

paras.en: By digging deeper, researchers hope to learn new details about aging that could prove useful – and maybe not just for dogs.
paras.zh: 通过更深入的挖掘，研究人员希望了解有关衰老的新细节，这些细节可能被证明是有用的——而且可能不仅仅对狗有用。

paras.en: "Because they are companion animals, they can also be a powerful model with immediate relevance to human health," Snyder-Mackler says.
paras.zh: “因为它们是伴侣动物，所以它们也可以成为与人类健康直接相关的强大模型，”斯奈德-麦克勒说。

paras.en: "Living with us means that we share experiences and environments, while our love for our pets means we provide them food, exercise and lifelong health care – meaning we can translate many findings in our shorter-lived pets to humans."
paras.zh: “与我们一起生活意味着我们分享经验和环境，而我们对宠物的爱意味着我们为它们提供食物、锻炼和终身医疗保健——这意味着我们可以将短命宠物的许多发现转化为人类。”

paras.en: For the new study, researchers analyzed data from 894 dogs enrolled in the Dog Aging Project, searching for patterns of DNA methylation across genomes.
paras.zh: 在这项新研究中，研究人员分析了参与狗衰老项目的 894 只狗的数据，寻找跨基因组的 DNA 甲基化模式。

paras.en: DNA methylation is a key epigenetic mechanism, capable of adjusting gene expression without altering DNA sequences. Previous research has established DNA methylation as a useful biomarker for aging and DNA regulation.
paras.zh: DNA甲基化是一种关键的表观遗传机制，能够在不改变DNA序列的情况下调节基因表达。先前的研究已将 DNA 甲基化确定为衰老和 DNA 调控的有用生物标志物。

paras.en: The new study also found a broad decline in methylation as dogs aged, especially in mobile DNA sequences called transposons, or 'jumping genes,' which can move around within a genome or send out copies of themselves.
paras.zh: 这项新研究还发现，随着狗的衰老，甲基化水平普遍下降，尤其是被称为转座子或“跳跃基因”的移动DNA序列，它可以在基因组内移动或发出自身的副本。

paras.en: Differences in dog aging may arise partly from specific jumping genes known as LINE1s, the authors report. LINE1s can damage DNA as they roam the genome, a threat normally mitigated by DNA methylation.
paras.zh: 作者报告说，狗衰老的差异可能部分归因于称为 LINE1 的特定跳跃基因。 LINE1 在基因组中漫游时会损坏 DNA，这种威胁通常可以通过 DNA 甲基化来缓解。

paras.en: More than 40 percent of LINE1-associated genome regions lost methylation as dogs aged, the study found, with different dogs declining at different rates.
paras.zh: 研究发现，随着狗的衰老，超过 40% 的 LINE1 相关基因组区域会失去甲基化，不同的狗以不同的速度下降。

paras.en: The loss unfolded significantly faster in larger breeds, which lost about 35 percent more LINE1 methylation annually than smaller breeds did.
paras.zh: 大型品种的 LINE1 甲基化损失速度明显更快，与小型品种相比，每年损失的 LINE1 甲基化多约 35%。

paras.en: "What we found is that the epigenetic regulation of transposable elements – especially LINE1s – appears to be a major factor shaping how quickly different dogs age," Snyder-Mackler says.
paras.zh: “我们发现，转座元件的表观遗传调控——尤其是 LINE1——似乎是影响不同狗衰老速度的主要因素，”Snyder-Mackler 说。

paras.en: "This is one of the clearest molecular signatures we've seen that aligns with the well-known size-lifespan trade-off in dogs," adds co-lead author and ASU evolutionary biologist Blaise Mariner.
paras.zh: “这是我们见过的最清晰的分子特征之一，与众所周知的狗的体型与寿命权衡相一致，”共同主要作者、亚利桑那州立大学进化生物学家 Blaise Mariner 补充道。

paras.en: "It suggests that faster aging in larger dogs may be driven, at least in part, by reduced control over these 'jumping genes.'"
paras.zh: “这表明大型犬的衰老速度加快可能至少部分是由于对这些‘跳跃基因’的控制减少所致。”

paras.en: More research is needed, but these findings show compelling links between DNA methylation (DNAm), aging, and canine lifespan, the authors report. They also highlight sex-specific effects of aging, concentrated on the X chromosome, that may warrant further investigation.
paras.zh: 作者报告说，还需要更多的研究，但这些发现表明 DNA 甲基化 (DNAm)、衰老和犬类寿命之间存在令人信服的联系。他们还强调了衰老对性别的影响，集中在 X 染色体上，这可能值得进一步研究。

paras.en: "We found that dogs with epigenetic ages older than expected exhibited elevated mortality risk, demonstrating that DNAm captures biologically meaningful variation in aging," the team writes.
paras.zh: 研究小组写道：“我们发现表观遗传年龄比预期年龄大的狗表现出较高的死亡风险，这表明 DNAm 捕获了具有生物学意义的衰老变化。”

paras.en: "Larger dogs, males, and younger individuals showed molecular profiles consistent with accelerated epigenetic aging."
paras.zh: “较大的狗、雄性和较年轻的个体表现出与表观遗传加速衰老一致的分子特征。”

paras.en: Helping dogs is always a noble cause, although we also have selfish reasons for trying to extend their healthy lifespans, given their immense importance to humanity overall and to countless individuals.
paras.zh: 帮助狗始终是一项崇高的事业，尽管我们也有自私的理由试图延长它们的健康寿命，因为它们对整个人类和无数个人具有巨大的重要性。

paras.en: On top of that, however, the researchers suspect they're unveiling broad secrets of mammalian aging that might also benefit us directly.
paras.zh: 然而，最重要的是，研究人员怀疑他们正在揭开哺乳动物衰老的广泛秘密，这也可能直接使我们受益。

paras.en: "Our work suggests that transposable elements may be a fundamental part of the aging process across mammals," Snyder-Mackler says.
paras.zh: “我们的工作表明转座因子可能是哺乳动物衰老过程的基本组成部分，”斯奈德-麦克勒说。

paras.en: "If that's the case, targeting these elements or the mechanisms that regulate them could be a promising avenue for future therapies to extend the health span in humans."
paras.zh: “如果是这样的话，针对这些元素或调节它们的机制可能是未来治疗延长人类健康寿命的一条有希望的途径。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Science.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《科学》杂志上。

articles.title: Scientists discover stunning new Amazon fish that may already be endangered

paras.en: Scientists discover stunning new Amazon fish that may already be endangered
paras.zh: 科学家发现令人惊叹的新亚马逊鱼可能已经濒临灭绝

paras.en: - Researchers have discovered a stunning new species of tiny orange-patterned fish in the Brazilian Amazon, but its survival may already be at risk. Named Laimosemion laranja, the brilliantly colored killifish measures less than three centimeters long and was found in just three small forest pools. Its extremely limited habitat is threatened by mining, deforestation, pollution, and expanding development.
paras.zh: - 研究人员在巴西亚马逊地区发现了一种令人惊叹的橙色小鱼新物种，但其生存可能已经面临风险。这种颜色鲜艳的鳉鱼被命名为Laimosemion laranja，身长不到三厘米，仅在三个小森林水池中被发现。其极其有限的栖息地受到采矿、森林砍伐、污染和扩大开发的威胁。

paras.en: A tiny fish with brilliant orange markings has been discovered in the Brazilian Amazon, but scientists warn that the newly identified species may already be at risk of extinction. Found in a handful of forest pools threatened by human activity, the colorful fish has prompted researchers to call for urgent conservation measures.
paras.zh: 在巴西亚马逊地区发现了一种带有亮橙色斑纹的小鱼，但科学家警告说，这种新发现的物种可能已经面临灭绝的危险。这种色彩斑斓的鱼是在少数受到人类活动威胁的森林水池中发现的，促使研究人员呼吁采取紧急保护措施。

paras.en: The new species, named Laimosemion laranja, belongs to a group of small freshwater fish known as killifish. It measures less than three centimeters in standard length, but its appearance is anything but ordinary. Males have rows of bright orange spots along the front half of their bodies, followed by bold orange chevron patterns near the tail. These vivid markings stand out against their pale gray sides.
paras.zh: 这个新物种被命名为Laimosemion laranja，属于一种被称为鳉鱼的小型淡水鱼。它的标准长度不足三厘米，但外观却绝非寻常。雄性的身体前半部有一排排明亮的橙色斑点，尾部附近有醒目的橙色 V 形图案。这些生动的标记在其浅灰色侧面的衬托下显得格外突出。

paras.en: The discovery was made during fieldwork in the Rio Cajari drainage in southern Amapá, a state in northern Brazil. The research team included scientists from the Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte, Instituto Peixe das Nuvens, Universidade Federal do Pará, and University of West Florida.
paras.zh: 这一发现是在巴西北部阿马帕州南部卡贾里河流域的实地考察中发现的。研究小组包括来自北里奥格兰德联邦大学、Instituto Peixe das Nuvens、帕拉联邦大学和西佛罗里达大学的科学家。

paras.en: A Striking Discovery in the Amazon Rainforest
paras.zh: 亚马逊雨林中的惊人发现

paras.en: The researchers were exploring how different freshwater fish in the Rivulidae family have evolved their life cycles and survival strategies across Brazil's diverse environments. During their surveys, they encountered a fish whose unusual coloration immediately stood out.
paras.zh: 研究人员正在探索Rivulidae家族的不同淡水鱼如何在巴西不同的环境中进化出它们的生命周期和生存策略。在调查过程中，他们遇到了一条鱼，它不寻常的颜色立即引人注目。

paras.en: "We are developing a research project aimed at investigating the evolution of life-history strategies in freshwater fishes of the family Rivulidae across different biomes in Brazil," said lead researcher Yuri Abrantes of the Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte. "During our sampling in small rivers locally known as 'igarapés' in the Rio Cajari region, in Amapá State, we found this fish with a very striking coloration, which immediately caught our attention."
paras.zh: “我们正在开发一个研究项目，旨在调查巴西不同生物群落中Rivulidae科淡水鱼类生活史策略的演变，”北里奥格兰德联邦大学的首席研究员尤里·阿布兰特斯说。 “在阿马帕州卡贾里河地区当地被称为‘igarapés’的小河流中取样时，我们发现这种鱼具有非常引人注目的颜色，立即引起了我们的注意。”

paras.en: Although the fish looked different from known species, its appearance alone was not enough to establish that it was new to science. The team carefully examined its body proportions, counted its scales, and studied features of its skeleton. They compared these characteristics with those of closely related species and analyzed its mitochondrial DNA to determine whether it represented a distinct species.
paras.zh: 尽管这种鱼看起来与已知物种不同，但仅凭其外观并不足以证明它是科学上的新物种。研究小组仔细检查了它的身体比例，计算了它的鳞片，并研究了它的骨骼特征。他们将这些特征与密切相关的物种进行了比较，并分析了其线粒体 DNA，以确定它是否代表了一个不同的物种。

paras.en: "It was an unexpected moment," Abrantes recalled. "Initially, what most caught our attention was the impressive coloration of the males and females, which was unlike anything we had previously encountered in the study area. This sparked our admiration and a great deal of curiosity."
paras.zh: “这是一个意想不到的时刻，”阿布兰特斯回忆道。 “最初，最引起我们注意的是雄性和雌性令人印象深刻的颜色，这与我们之前在研究区域遇到的任何东西都不同。这引发了我们的钦佩和极大的好奇心。”

paras.en: Genetic testing ultimately confirmed that the fish was a previously unrecognized species. For the researchers, the finding was particularly meaningful because it highlighted how much remains to be discovered in parts of the Amazon that are both poorly studied and increasingly threatened.
paras.zh: 基因测试最终证实该鱼是一种以前未被识别的物种。对于研究人员来说，这一发现特别有意义，因为它突显了亚马逊地区有多少东西有待发现，而这些地区的研究很少，而且受到的威胁日益严重。

paras.en: Once the genetic analysis confirmed the fish's distinct identity, he said, "it was something special, as we saw an opportunity to contribute to increasing our knowledge of Amazonian biodiversity and to draw attention to the conservation of areas that are still poorly explored but highly threatened."
paras.zh: 他说，一旦基因分析证实了这种鱼的独特身份，“这是一件很特别的事情，因为我们看到了一个机会，可以为增加我们对亚马逊生物多样性的了解做出贡献，并引起人们对那些尚未开发但受到高度威胁的地区的保护的关注。”

paras.en: Why Scientists Named the New Fish Laranja
paras.zh: 为什么科学家将新鱼命名为Laranja

paras.en: The name Laimosemion laranja reflects both the fish's remarkable appearance and the place where it was discovered. In Portuguese, laranja means orange, referring to both the color and the fruit. The name also pays tribute to Laranjal do Jari, the municipality in Amapá where the species was found.
paras.zh: Laimosemion laranja 这个名字既反映了这种鱼非凡的外观，也反映了它的发现地点。在葡萄牙语中，laranja 的意思是橙色，既指颜色又指水果。这个名字还向发现该物种的阿马帕市拉兰贾尔杜贾里致敬。

paras.en: "We wanted to choose a name that would highlight a characteristic of the fish while also fostering a sense of connection with the people of the region where it was discovered," Abrantes explained.
paras.zh: 阿布兰特斯解释说：“我们希望选择一个能够突出这种鱼的特征的名字，同时还能培养与发现它的地区的人们的联系感。”

paras.en: Beyond its colorful appearance, the discovery could help scientists better understand the evolution of Amazonian killifish. Some members of this group have developed an extraordinary way to survive in habitats that periodically dry out. Their embryos can stop developing and remain dormant in damp mud, resuming development when seasonal rains refill the pools.
paras.zh: 除了色彩缤纷的外观之外，这一发现还可以帮助科学家更好地了解亚马逊鳉鱼的进化。该群体的一些成员已经发展出一种非凡的方式，可以在定期干燥的栖息地中生存。它们的胚胎可以停止发育并在潮湿的泥土中保持休眠状态，当季节性降雨重新填满水池时恢复发育。

paras.en: "Laimosemion represents one of the five independent origins of the annual life cycle within the family Rivulidae," said Abrantes. "Laimosemion laranja is particularly interesting because it expands our knowledge of the diversity and evolution of this group in the region."
paras.zh: 阿布兰特斯说：“莱莫塞米恩代表了河科一年生命周期的五个独立起源之一。” “Laimosemion laranja 特别有趣，因为它扩展了我们对该地区这个群体的多样性和进化的了解。”

paras.en: Newly Discovered Amazon Fish May Already Be Endangered
paras.zh: 新发现的亚马逊鱼可能已经濒临灭绝

paras.en: Despite the excitement surrounding the discovery, the future of Laimosemion laranja is uncertain. Scientists have found it in only three small forest pools near Laranjal do Jari, and every known location shows signs of environmental disturbance.
paras.zh: 尽管这一发现令人兴奋，但莱莫塞米翁·拉兰贾的未来仍不确定。科学家们仅在拉兰贾尔杜贾里附近的三个小森林水池中发现了它，并且每个已知地点都显示出环境干扰的迹象。

paras.en: Deforestation, mining, and urban development are putting pressure on the surrounding habitats. One of the pools is close to water that has been discolored by sediment from mining activities. Another is located within the city itself, where plastic pollution is affecting the environment.
paras.zh: 森林砍伐、采矿和城市发展给周围的栖息地带来了压力。其中一个水池靠近因采矿活动沉积物而变色的水。另一个位于城市内部，塑料污染正在影响环境。

paras.en: The species' entire known range is estimated to cover just 25 square kilometers. Because its habitat is so restricted and faces multiple threats, the researchers believe the fish meets the criteria for classification as Endangered under guidelines established by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN).
paras.zh: 该物种的整个已知活动范围估计仅覆盖 25 平方公里。由于其栖息地受到限制并面临多种威胁，研究人员认为该鱼符合国际自然保护联盟 (IUCN) 制定的指导方针下的濒危物种分类标准。

paras.en: To improve its chances of survival, the team has recommended expanding the boundaries of the nearby Rio Cajari Extractive Reserve to include the areas where the fish lives.
paras.zh: 为了提高其生存机会，该团队建议扩大附近卡贾里河采掘保护区的边界，将其生活的区域包括在内。

paras.en: The discovery adds another species to the Amazon's remarkable biological diversity while underscoring the need to protect habitats that scientists have barely begun to explore. Without stronger conservation measures, species such as Laimosemion laranja could face serious threats before researchers have the opportunity to fully understand them.
paras.zh: 这一发现为亚马逊非凡的生物多样性增添了另一个物种，同时强调了保护科学家刚刚开始探索的栖息地的必要性。如果没有更强有力的保护措施，在研究人员有机会充分了解Laimosemion laranja等物种之前，它们可能会面临严重威胁。

paras.en: The study was published in the open access journal Zoosystematics and Evolution.
paras.zh: 该研究发表在开放获取期刊《动物系统学与进化》上。

articles.title: Hidden climate superpower: Why some ocean “snow” carries six times more carbon

paras.en: Hidden climate superpower: Why some ocean âsnowâ carries six times more carbon
paras.zh: 隐藏的气候超级大国：为什么一些海洋“雪”的碳含量是原来的六倍

paras.en: - Scientists have discovered that the stickiness of underwater âmarine snowâ plays a surprisingly important role in how much carbon reaches the deep ocean. Gooier particles resist bacterial breakdown and can transport more than six times as much carbon to the depths, revealing an unexpected connection between ocean slime and Earth's climate.
paras.zh: - 科学家发现，水下“海洋雪”的粘性对于到达深海的碳量起着非常重要的作用。粘稠的颗粒可以抵抗细菌分解，并且可以将六倍多的碳输送到深处，揭示了海洋粘液和地球气候之间意想不到的联系。

paras.en: Far below the ocean's surface, a constant snowfall drifts through the darkness. But unlike the frozen flakes that fall from the sky, this underwater snow consists of tiny clumps of waste, dead organisms, and other debris. Known as marine snow, these particles contain everything from mucus and animal feces to silt and the remains of microscopic plankton.
paras.zh: 在海面深处，持续不断的降雪在黑暗中飘过。但与从天而降的冰冻雪花不同，这种水下雪由微小的废物团、死亡生物体和其他碎片组成。这些颗粒被称为海洋雪，含有从粘液和动物粪便到淤泥和微小浮游生物残留物的所有物质。

paras.en: As this material sinks, it carries enormous quantities of carbon from the upper ocean toward the seafloor. Researchers estimate that marine snow removes more than 10 gigatons of carbon from surface waters each year. Yet only about two gigatons reach depths where that carbon can remain stored for hundreds or even thousands of years.
paras.zh: 当这种物质下沉时，它会将大量的碳从上层海洋带到海底。研究人员估计，海洋雪每年从地表水中去除超过 10 十亿吨碳。然而，只有大约 20 亿吨碳能够到达可以储存数百年甚至数千年的深度。

paras.en: Why so much carbon fails to make it into the deep ocean has long puzzled scientists. Now, researchers from UC San Diego's Scripps Institution of Oceanography and the University of Lincoln have identified a surprisingly important factor: how sticky the marine snow is.
paras.zh: 为什么如此多的碳未能进入深海，长期以来一直困扰着科学家。现在，来自加州大学圣地亚哥分校斯克里普斯海洋学研究所和林肯大学的研究人员发现了一个令人惊讶的重要因素：海洋雪的粘性。

paras.en: Their findings, published October 8 in the journal Science, show that the viscosity, or thickness and gooeyness, of marine snow influences how quickly bacteria break it apart and how far it can sink. According to the researchers, the stickiest particles can transport more than six times as much carbon to the deep ocean as particles with a thinner, less viscous consistency.
paras.zh: 他们的研究结果于 10 月 8 日发表在《科学》杂志上，表明海雪的粘度、厚度和粘性会影响细菌分解它的速度以及它下沉的距离。研究人员表示，最粘的颗粒向深海输送的碳量是较薄、粘性较小的颗粒的六倍多。

paras.en: Marine snow plays an important role in Earth's carbon cycle, the natural movement of carbon among the atmosphere, oceans, land, and living organisms. By transporting carbon into deep water, sinking particles can keep some of it isolated from the atmosphere for centuries or longer.
paras.zh: 海洋雪在地球碳循环、碳在大气、海洋、陆地和生物体之间的自然移动中发挥着重要作用。通过将碳输送到深水中，下沉的颗粒可以使其中一些碳与大气隔离几个世纪或更长时间。

paras.en: However, not every particle survives the journey. Bacteria feed on marine snow as it descends, gradually breaking down the material and affecting how much carbon reaches the ocean's depths.
paras.zh: 然而，并不是每个粒子都能在旅途中幸存下来。当海洋雪下降时，细菌以海洋雪为食，逐渐分解物质并影响到达海洋深处的碳量。

paras.en: The new research provides the first detailed look at how living bacteria interact with the physical structure of marine snow and, more broadly, mucus itself. These interactions are important well beyond the ocean's carbon cycle. Similar relationships between bacteria and mucus help sustain coral reefs, kelp forests, plant root systems, and the digestive systems of humans and other animals.
paras.zh: 这项新研究首次详细研究了活细菌如何与海洋雪的物理结构以及更广泛的粘液本身相互作用。这些相互作用的重要性远远超出了海洋碳循环的范围。细菌和粘液之间的类似关系有助于维持珊瑚礁、海带森林、植物根系以及人类和其他动物的消化系统。

paras.en: Until recently, scientists lacked the technology to observe these interactions at the microscopic scale needed to understand them.
paras.zh: 直到最近，科学家们还缺乏在微观尺度上观察这些相互作用以理解它们的技术。

paras.en: A Four-Year Quest to See Inside Marine Snow
paras.zh: 四年探索海洋雪的内部

paras.en: The project began in 2021, when Bryce Inman, then a postdoctoral researcher at Scripps Oceanography, set out to explore what he calls "the muscoscape."
paras.zh: 该项目始于 2021 年，当时斯克里普斯海洋学博士后研究员布莱斯·英曼 (Bryce Inman) 开始探索他所谓的“麝香景观”。

paras.en: "Observing individual bacteria interacting with the physical structure of mucus had never been possible," said Inman.
paras.zh: “观察单个细菌与粘液物理结构的相互作用是不可能的，”英曼说。

paras.en: Together with colleagues including Farooq Azam, a microbiologist and professor emeritus at Scripps, Inman spent four years trying to overcome that limitation. Multiple attempts were unsuccessful before the team finally developed a working technique in 2025.
paras.zh: 英曼与包括微生物学家、斯克里普斯大学名誉教授法鲁克·阿扎姆在内的同事一起花了四年时间试图克服这一限制。多次尝试均未成功，团队终于在2025年开发出了可行的技术。

paras.en: Their solution combined 3D confocal microscopy with specially designed fluorescent molecules. Confocal microscopy uses light to capture detailed images at different depths within a sample, allowing researchers to reconstruct its structure in three dimensions. The fluorescent molecules helped make features of the material visible.
paras.zh: 他们的解决方案将 3D 共焦显微镜与专门设计的荧光分子相结合。共焦显微镜利用光捕获样本内不同深度的详细图像，使研究人员能够在三个维度上重建其结构。荧光分子有助于使材料的特征可见。

paras.en: For the first time, the scientists could examine the "physical terrain" of individual marine snow particles while watching how living bacteria moved through and interacted with them.
paras.zh: 科学家们第一次可以检查单个海洋雪颗粒的“物理地形”，同时观察活细菌如何穿过它们并与其相互作用。

paras.en: The images revealed a surprisingly intricate microscopic environment, complete with structural differences that affect where bacteria can settle and how easily they can reach the material inside.
paras.zh: 这些图像揭示了一个极其复杂的微观环境，其结构差异会影响细菌的定居位置以及它们接触内部物质的容易程度。

paras.en: Much like snowflakes in the atmosphere, marine snow particles vary considerably. Each contains its own mixture of organic and inorganic materials, creating differences in composition, structure, and viscosity.
paras.zh: 就像大气中的雪花一样，海洋雪颗粒变化很大。每种材料都含有自己的有机和无机材料的混合物，从而在成分、结构和粘度方面产生差异。

paras.en: The researchers' new imaging approach, described in a companion study published in Nature Communications, revealed that bacteria preferentially colonize areas near a particle's surface where the material is less viscous.
paras.zh: 研究人员在《自然通讯》上发表的一项配套研究中描述了研究人员的新成像方法，该方法表明细菌优先定殖在颗粒表面附近材料粘度较低的区域。

paras.en: The denser, stickier regions deeper inside are much harder for bacteria to penetrate.
paras.zh: 内部更密集、更粘的区域更难以细菌渗透。

paras.en: "Bacteria can latch on to less viscous portions of each particle, but cannot reach more viscous regions until they break it down," said Inman. "Think of it like a worm in an apple: the flesh is easy to penetrate, but the core is tough to chew through"
paras.zh: 英曼说：“细菌可以附着在每个颗粒的粘性较小的部分，但在将其分解之前无法到达粘性较高的区域。” “把它想象成苹果里的虫子：果肉很容易穿透，但核心很难咀嚼”

paras.en: This difference has important consequences for how long marine snow remains intact.
paras.zh: 这种差异对于海洋积雪完好无损的时间有重要影响。

paras.en: In laboratory experiments, the scientists observed that particles with greater viscosity resisted bacterial degradation and fragmentation for longer periods. Computer simulations further suggested that these stickier particles can descend to greater depths before breaking apart.
paras.zh: 在实验室实验中，科学家们观察到，粘度较大的颗粒可以更长时间地抵抗细菌降解和破碎。计算机模拟进一步表明，这些较粘的颗粒在分裂之前可以下降到更深的深度。

paras.en: Based on these results, the team estimates that highly viscous marine snow can deliver more than six times as much carbon to the deep ocean as less viscous particles.
paras.zh: 根据这些结果，研究小组估计，高粘性海洋雪向深海输送的碳量是低粘性颗粒的六倍多。

paras.en: The findings help explain why some sinking material transports carbon much farther into the ocean than other particles, even though both begin their journeys near the surface.
paras.zh: 这些发现有助于解释为什么一些下沉物质将碳比其他颗粒输送到海洋更远的地方，尽管它们的旅程都是在表面附近开始的。

paras.en: "How far marine snow can sink is a surprisingly complicated problem, and we have added another - very gooey - piece to the puzzle," said Inman.
paras.zh: 英曼说：“海洋雪能下沉多远是一个令人惊讶的复杂问题，我们为这个难题添加了另一个非常粘稠的部分。”

paras.en: A Discovery With Implications Beyond the Ocean
paras.zh: 一项具有超越海洋意义的发现

paras.en: Although the research focuses on marine snow, its implications extend to many environments where bacteria interact with mucus.
paras.zh: 尽管这项研究的重点是海洋雪，但其影响延伸到细菌与粘液相互作用的许多环境。

paras.en: Mucus is often regarded as a relatively simple, slippery substance. But the new imaging technology reveals that it has a complex internal landscape, with microscopic structures that can influence how bacteria behave.
paras.zh: 粘液通常被认为是一种相对简单、光滑的物质。但新的成像技术揭示了它具有复杂的内部景观，其微观结构可以影响细菌的行为。

paras.en: Understanding these physical features could help scientists investigate biological processes in settings ranging from human digestive health to the recovery of damaged coral reefs.
paras.zh: 了解这些物理特征可以帮助科学家研究从人类消化健康到受损珊瑚礁恢复等环境中的生物过程。

paras.en: The method also opens opportunities to explore interactions that previously could not be observed directly, providing researchers with a new way to study the microscopic environments inhabited by bacteria.
paras.zh: 该方法还为探索以前无法直接观察到的相互作用提供了机会，为研究人员提供了一种研究细菌居住的微观环境的新方法。

paras.en: Mucus, slime, whatever you want to call it, "has a surprising amount of structure," Inman said. "There are bulges, crevasses, all this sort of structure to it that we really had no idea about at a scale smaller than bacteria. This is the first time we're really examining this physical habitat."
paras.zh: 粘液、粘液，无论你想怎么称呼它，“都具有令人惊讶的结构，”英曼说。 “它有凸起、裂缝，所有这些我们在比细菌还小的规模上确实不知道的结构。这是我们第一次真正检查这个物理栖息地。”

paras.en: The discovery adds an important missing piece to scientists' understanding of how carbon travels through the ocean. It also demonstrates that something as seemingly ordinary as the thickness of underwater slime can have far-reaching consequences for the planet's natural systems.
paras.zh: 这一发现为科学家们了解碳如何在海洋中传播添加了重要的缺失部分。它还表明，像水下粘液厚度这样看似平常的东西也可能对地球的自然系统产生深远的影响。

paras.en: Additional funding for the research was provided by the Simons Foundation and the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council.
paras.zh: 西蒙斯基金会和工程与物理科学研究委员会为该研究提供了额外资金。
