articles.title: Archaeologists Found a 3,300-Year-Old Sword at the Bottom of a Volcanic Lake in Italy—and It's Still Sharp

paras.en: Archaeologists have pulled a 3,300-year-old sword from a lake in Italy—and it’s still sharp.
paras.zh: 考古学家从意大利的一个湖中取出了一把有 3,300 年历史的剑，它仍然锋利。

paras.en: The bronze weapon was discovered at the bottom of Lake Mezzano, a small volcanic lake in central Italy, roughly 60 miles northwest of Rome.
paras.zh: 这件青铜武器是在梅扎诺湖 (Lake Mezzano) 的底部发现的，梅扎诺湖是意大利中部的一个小火山湖，距离罗马西北约 60 英里。

paras.en: It’s the third sword discovered in the lake since the 1970s, according to an announcement from Italy’s Superintendence of Archaeology, Fine Arts and Landscape for the Province of Viterbo and Southern Etruria.
paras.zh: 根据意大利维泰博省和南伊特鲁里亚考古、美术和景观管理局的公告，这是自 20 世纪 70 年代以来在湖中发现的第三把剑。

paras.en: Archaeologists think that between 1700 and 1150 B.C.E. the lake was home to a Bronze Age pile-dwelling village, a community lofted above the water on stilts.
paras.zh: 考古学家认为公元前 1700 年至 1150 年之间这个湖是一个青铜时代的木桩村的所在地，这是一个用高跷高高耸立在水面上的社区。

paras.en: The sword is thought to date to the 13th century B.C.E., which corresponds with the Late Bronze Age. At that time, the people living in central Italy maintained trade and connections with communities throughout the peninsula and across the Mediterranean. In that context, the researchers say, weapons were more than just combat tools—they were also symbols of prestige, identity and power.
paras.zh: 这把剑被认为可以追溯到公元前 13 世纪，相当于青铜时代晚期。当时，居住在意大利中部的人们与整个半岛和地中海地区的社区保持着贸易和联系。研究人员表示，在这种背景下，武器不仅仅是战斗工具，它们还是威望、身份和权力的象征。

paras.en: Archaeologists found the sword while excavating a largely unexplored area on the lake’s southern shore. During the same expedition, they found intact vases and numerous bronze artifacts, including axes, arrowheads, daggers, spearheads, pins and a razor. They found the sword and the razor lying near each other, which suggests they may have once belonged to the same person, possibly a high-status individual or an elite warrior.
paras.zh: 考古学家在湖南岸挖掘一片未开发的区域时发现了这把剑。在同一次探险中，他们发现了完整的花瓶和大量青铜器，包括斧头、箭头、匕首、矛头、别针和剃刀。他们发现剑和剃刀彼此靠近，这表明它们可能曾经属于同一个人，可能是一位地位很高的人，也可能是一位精英战士。

paras.en: Similar discoveries across Europe suggest that ancient people sometimes deliberately deposited weapons and other metal objects in lakes, possibly as part of religious rituals or offerings. According to Live Science’s Kristina Killgrove, the sword may have been tossed in the lake as an offering to a god.
paras.zh: 欧洲各地的类似发现表明，古人有时会故意将武器和其他金属物品放入湖泊中，这可能是宗教仪式或祭品的一部分。根据《Live Science》的克里斯蒂娜·基尔格罗夫的说法，这把剑可能被扔进湖里作为献给神的祭品。

paras.en: Geologist Lamberto Ferri Ricchi first discovered the now-submerged village in 1971, when he found the remains of three prehistoric pile-dwellings submerged between nine and 30 feet deep. He returned several years later at the request of regional archaeology officials and uncovered roughly 50 vases, three bronze axes, skeletal remains, wooden planks, millstones and other artifacts.
paras.zh: 地质学家 Lamberto Ferri Ricchi 于 1971 年首次发现了这个现已被淹没的村庄，当时他在 9 至 30 英尺深的水下发现了三座史前木桩住宅的遗迹。几年后，他应地区考古官员的要求返回，发现了大约 50 个花瓶、三把青铜斧、骨骼遗骸、木板、磨石和其他文物。

paras.en: Excavations continued into the mid-1990s, then came to a halt for nearly three decades until funding became available again. Last year, archaeologists returned to the site and mapped more than 600 wooden posts they believe once held up the Bronze Age settlement. The posts were embedded into the clay lakebed at various depths, ranging from eight feet to more than 32 feet deep. Researchers suspect the newly discovered posts represent roughly a third of the entire settlement.
paras.zh: 挖掘工作一直持续到 20 世纪 90 年代中期，然后暂停了近三十年，直到资金再次到位。去年，考古学家返回该地点，绘制了 600 多根木柱的地图，他们认为这些木柱曾经支撑着青铜时代的定居点。这些柱子嵌入粘土湖床的不同深度，从八英尺到超过 32 英尺深。研究人员怀疑新发现的柱子大约占整个定居点的三分之一。

paras.en: Across Europe, similar discoveries have been made in bodies of water, including a 1,000-year-old Viking sword in an English river, an Iron Age sword in a Swedish lake and rust-covered medieval sword in Poland’s Vistula River.
paras.zh: 在整个欧洲，人们也在水体中发现了类似的发现，包括英国河流中的一把具有 1000 年历史的维京剑、瑞典湖中的铁器时代剑以及波兰维斯瓦河中锈迹斑斑的中世纪剑。

paras.en: During the 2025 expedition, they also recovered numerous artifacts, including axes, spearheads, brooches, rings, a pin and a sickle. They also found bronze ingots that may have been used in casting, suggesting that residents were producing metal objects within the village.
paras.zh: 在 2025 年的探险中，他们还发现了许多文物，包括斧头、矛头、胸针、戒指、别针和镰刀。他们还发现了可能用于铸造的青铜锭，这表明居民正在村内生产金属物品。

paras.en: Researchers are still trying to interpret the findings of their latest expedition. In the meantime, they say they plan to display the newly discovered artifacts during an upcoming exhibition, per the statement. They also hope to continue their research in Lake Mezzano to gain an even deeper understanding of the people who once lived there.
paras.zh: 研究人员仍在试图解释他们最新探险的发现。与此同时，根据声明，他们表示计划在即将举行的展览中展示新发现的文物。他们还希望继续对梅扎诺湖的研究，以更深入地了解曾经居住在那里的人们。

articles.title: Strange Gas in Mars' Atmosphere Hints the Red Planet Is Still Volcanically Active—and Points to Places to Search for Alien Life

paras.en: Volcanic activity shaped the Red Planet for hundreds of millions of years. But today, researchers aren’t sure whether our neighbor has retained some of that volcanic feistiness or if it is truly dead inside.
paras.zh: 数亿年来，火山活动塑造了这颗红色星球。但今天，研究人员不确定我们的邻居是否还保留着火山爆发的活力，或者它是否真的已经死在里面了。

paras.en: In a study published November 4 in the journal Science Advances, scientists suggest that magma is, indeed, still on the move beneath the surface of Mars. Their evidence comes from unexpected gas detection in the planet’s atmosphere, which may have been spewed from fresh cracks on its Alba Mons volcano. If confirmed, their findings could shape how researchers search for signs of extraterrestrial life on Mars.
paras.zh: 在 11 月 4 日发表在《科学进展》杂志上的一项研究中，科学家们认为，岩浆确实仍在火星表面下方移动。他们的证据来自于在地球大气层中意外检测到的气体，这些气体可能是从阿尔巴蒙斯火山的新裂缝中喷出的。如果得到证实，他们的发现可能会影响研究人员在火星上寻找外星生命迹象的方式。

paras.en: It’s not the first time researchers have found possible hints of ongoing volcanic activity on the Red Planet. NASA’s InSight lander has previously detected marsquakes whose rumblings indicated potentially active subsurface fluid.
paras.zh: 这并不是研究人员第一次发现这颗红色星球上正在进行的火山活动的可能迹象。美国宇航局的洞察号着陆器此前曾探测到火星地震，其隆隆声表明地下存在潜在的活跃流体。

paras.en: “Some folks think it’s magma; others think it’s water,” Tracy Gregg, a planetary volcanologist at the University at Buffalo, who didn’t participate in the study, tells National Geographic’s Robin George Andrews. “I think it might be both.”
paras.zh: “有些人认为它是岩浆；另一些人认为它是水，”布法罗大学的行星火山学家特雷西·格雷格（未参与这项研究）告诉国家地理杂志的罗宾·乔治·安德鲁斯。 “我想可能两者兼而有之。”

paras.en: The new work provides the strongest evidence yet discovered of gases released by dormant Martian volcanoes, complementing Insight’s data, lead author Alexander Trokhimovskiy, a planetary scientist at the Space Research Institute at the Russian Academy of Sciences, tells Live Science’s Elizabeth Howell.
paras.zh: 俄罗斯科学院空间研究所的行星科学家、主要作者亚历山大·特罗希莫夫斯基 (Alexander Trokhimovskiy) 告诉《生活科学》杂志的伊丽莎白·豪厄尔，这项新研究提供了迄今为止发现的火星休眠火山释放气体的最有力证据，补充了《洞察》的数据。

paras.en: The gas in question is hydrogen chloride, a stinky substance that can come from volcanoes on Earth. In 2021, the ExoMars Trace Gas Orbiter (TGO), a collaboration between the European Space Agency and Russia’s Roscosmos, recorded unexpected spikes of the smelly gas above Mars’ northern hemisphere during its early summer. Usually, atmospheric hydrogen chloride peaks in the northern hemisphere’s winter and then almost disappears over the summer.
paras.zh: 所讨论的气体是氯化氢，一种可能来自地球火山的恶臭物质。 2021 年，欧洲航天局和俄罗斯航天局合作的 ExoMars 痕量气体轨道飞行器 (TGO) 在初夏期间记录到火星北半球上空的恶臭气体意外激增。通常，大气中的氯化氢在北半球的冬季达到峰值，然后在夏季几乎消失。

paras.en: The researchers found that the gassy deviation happened during multiple Mars years, each of which is nearly as long as two Earth years. What’s more, it always occurred in the early summer and over volcanic fissures on the edges of Alba Mons, a giant shield volcano spanning roughly the area of the contiguous United States.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，气体偏差发生在多个火星年中，每个火星年几乎有两个地球年那么长。更重要的是，它总是发生在初夏，发生在阿尔巴蒙斯边缘的火山裂缝上空，阿尔巴蒙斯是一座巨大的盾状火山，大约横跨美国本土。

paras.en: Images snapped by TGO’s high-resolution camera revealed new, narrow cracks. The photos also showed color changes on Mars’ surface, which the researchers suspect are related.
paras.zh: TGO 高分辨率相机拍摄的图像显示了新的狭窄裂缝。这些照片还显示了火星表面的颜色变化，研究人员怀疑这是相关的。

paras.en: Trokhimovskiy and colleagues propose that these cracks, which are blocked by ice during the winter, might emit hydrogen chloride in early summer. The strange coloring near the fissures could be caused by deposits left by substances in the gases that cool as they reach the surface, which happens around volcanic gas vents on Earth. Furthermore, the research indicates that this process is linked to a dormant magma chamber underground.
paras.zh: Trokhimovskiy 及其同事提出，这些在冬季被冰堵塞的裂缝可能会在初夏释放出氯化氢。裂缝附近的奇怪颜色可能是气体中的物质在到达地表时冷却后留下的沉积物造成的，这种情况发生在地球上的火山气体喷口周围。此外，研究表明这一过程与地下休眠岩浆室有关。

paras.en: “Looking at the spatial distribution of the seeping, it became instantly obvious to me that there was something volcanic behind it, but it had to be demonstrated,” study co-author Daniel Mège, a planetary scientist at the Space Research Center of the Polish Academy of Sciences, says in a statement. “A huge part of the work consisted of examining all the possible chemical processes going on in the Martian atmosphere. We needed to be rigorous, critical and creative to explain the presence of hydrogen chloride.”
paras.zh: 研究报告的合著者、波兰科学院空间研究中心的行星科学家丹尼尔·梅格（Daniel Mège）在一份声明中表示：“通过观察渗漏物的空间分布，我立刻意识到它背后有火山存在，但它必须得到证实。” “工作的很大一部分是检查火星大气中发生的所有可能的化学过程。我们需要严谨、批判性和创造性来解释氯化氢的存在。”

paras.en: More broadly, the findings indicate that Mars’ interior might still be hot enough to host magma activity, Trokhimovskiy tells Reuters’ Will Dunham. They also suggest that scientists searching for extraterrestrial life should home in on these fissures.
paras.zh: 特罗希莫夫斯基告诉路透社记者威尔·邓纳姆，更广泛地说，这些发现表明火星内部可能仍然足够热，可以进行岩浆活动。他们还建议寻找外星生命的科学家应该关注这些裂缝。

paras.en: “As rising magma moves through the crust, it can encounter, melt and heat underground water, creating environments shielded from the harsh surface conditions,” Trokhimovskiy tells the outlet. “Such active hydrothermal systems may provide the energy sources and favorable conditions needed to support microbial life. This makes warm subsurface environments one of the most promising targets in the search for life on Mars.”
paras.zh: 特罗希莫夫斯基告诉媒体：“当上升的岩浆穿过地壳时，它会遇到、融化并加热地下水，从而创造出免受恶劣地表条件影响的环境。” “这种活跃的热液系统可以提供支持微生物生命所需的能源和有利条件。这使得温暖的地下环境成为在火星上寻找生命最有希望的目标之一。”

paras.en: That would be consistent with life as we know it. On Earth, the chemistry that kicked off life may have occurred in hot, mineral-filled hydrothermal vents on the ocean floor.
paras.zh: 这与我们所知的生活是一致的。在地球上，引发生命的化学反应可能发生在海底炎热、充满矿物质的热液喷口中。

articles.title: For Centuries, Cave Visitors Walked Right by 280 Ice Age Engravings. The Newly Discovered Rock Art Is Rewriting Catalonia's Prehistory

paras.en: Tourists, explorers, archaeologists and others have been visiting the Cova de la Font Major, a cave system in Catalonia, Spain, since at least the 12th century. They’ve explored two miles of underground caves and rivers; left graffiti; and even opened a museum in the 1990s.
paras.zh: 至少从 12 世纪起，游客、探险家、考古学家和其他人就一直在参观位于西班牙加泰罗尼亚的 Cova de la Font Major 洞穴系统。他们探索了两英里长的地下洞穴和河流；左边的涂鸦；甚至在 20 世纪 90 年代开设了一家博物馆。

paras.en: But it wasn’t until recently that a team of archaeologists discovered what, for centuries, these relatively modern visitors had apparently failed to notice. Hidden in plain sight, left behind by some of the cave’s very first inhabitants, was the third-largest collection of Ice Age-era engravings to have ever been found on the Mediterranean side of the Iberian Peninsula.
paras.zh: 但直到最近，一组考古学家才发现了几个世纪以来这些相对现代的游客显然没有注意到的东西。洞穴中的一些最早的居民留下的，隐藏在众目睽睽之下，是伊比利亚半岛地中海一侧迄今为止发现的第三大冰河时代雕刻藏品。

paras.en: “At the moment of discovery, I experienced a mixture of excitement at encountering something both unexpected and extraordinary and profound disbelief,” Josep Maria Vergès, an archaeologist at the Catalan Institute of Human Paleoecology and Social Evolution (IPHES), tells Gizmodo’s Gayoung Lee. “It seemed inconceivable that none of the many visitors who had traversed the gallery … had ever noticed the presence of these prehistoric engravings.”
paras.zh: 加泰罗尼亚人类古生态和社会进化研究所 (IPHES) 的考古学家何塞普·玛丽亚·维尔格斯 (Josep Maria Vergès) 告诉 Gizmodo 的 Gayoung Lee，“在发现的那一刻，我感到非常兴奋，因为遇到了一些意想不到的、非同寻常的东西，同时又令人难以置信。” “令人难以置信的是，走过画廊的众多参观者中没有一个人注意到这些史前雕刻的存在。”

paras.en: During a series of excavations in 2019, researchers from IPHES identified some 280 Paleolithic engravings on the cave’s walls. The motifs were wide-ranging, comprising 55 distinct animals—horses, a bear, deer and early types of wild cattle among them—and dozens of abstract patterns, lines and loops. Their research was published this week in the journal Antiquity.
paras.zh: 在 2019 年的一系列发掘中，IPHES 的研究人员在洞穴的墙壁上发现了约 280 个旧石器时代的雕刻。图案范围广泛，包括 55 种不同的动物（其中包括马、熊、鹿和早期类型的野牛）以及数十种抽象图案、线条和循环。他们的研究发表在本周的《古代》杂志上。

paras.en: Paleolithic rock art on the Iberian peninsula is plentiful but unevenly distributed. Prior to the discovery at Cova de la Font Major, rock art identified in Catalonia was “very scarce compared with the abundant record of the neighboring Franco-Cantabrian region,” Vergès explains in a statement.
paras.zh: 伊比利亚半岛的旧石器时代岩画数量丰富，但分布不均。在 Cova de la Font Major 发现之前，在加泰罗尼亚发现的岩画“与邻近的弗朗哥-坎塔布连地区的丰富记录相比非常稀缺”，韦尔热斯在一份声明中解释道。

paras.en: It remains unclear how the markings had never been documented before. They are in a part of the cave that has been open to tourists since 1957. The general consensus was that the walls of the cave were too “irregular both in relief and color” to preserve art, per the article.
paras.zh: 目前还不清楚这些标记以前是如何从未被记录下来的。它们位于自 1957 年以来一直向游客开放的洞穴的一部分。文章称，普遍的共识是，洞穴的墙壁“无论是浮雕还是颜色都太不规则”，无法保存艺术品。

paras.en: The researchers speculate that lighting may have had a role to play in the belated discovery. “When you shine a light straight on the engravings, they are really difficult to see. You have to play with light from different directions to see the depressions,” Míriam Salas-Altès, an archaeologist with IPHES and a co-author of the study, tells Nature’s Chris Simms.
paras.zh: 研究人员推测，照明可能在这个迟来的发现中发挥了作用。 “当你用光线直射雕刻时，它们真的很难看到。你必须利用不同方向的光线才能看到凹陷，”IPHES 考古学家、该研究的合著者 Míriam Salas-Altès 告诉 Nature 杂志的 Chris Simms。

paras.en: The drawings appear to be advanced and distinct from the neighboring Franco-Cantabrian style of rock art. Some designs, the researchers posit, may represent the earth or bodies of water, and at least 20 inscriptions could form something like a prehistoric “movie or animation,” Salas-Altès tells Nature. These scenes show animals in repetition, with their limbs and heads changing positions, as though meant to depict running or movement.
paras.zh: 这些图画似乎很先进，与邻近的弗朗哥-坎塔布里亚风格的岩石艺术截然不同。萨拉斯-阿尔特斯告诉《自然》杂志，研究人员推测，一些设计可能代表地球或水体，至少 20 个铭文可以形成类似史前“电影或动画”的东西。这些场景重复地展示了动物，它们的四肢和头部不断变换着位置，仿佛是在描绘奔跑或运动。

paras.en: Using radiocarbon dating on bits of charcoal discovered inside one engraved groove—beside which a small flint bladelet was also recovered—the researchers estimated that the artworks are roughly 26,000 years old.
paras.zh: 通过对在一个雕刻凹槽内发现的木炭碎片（旁边还发现了一个小燧石刀片）进行放射性碳测年，研究人员估计这些艺术品大约有 26,000 年的历史。

paras.en: The researchers found that early humans traversed the sprawling cave system incrementally, visiting different sections over different periods of time. The earliest evidence of prehistoric activity inside dates to roughly 41,000 years ago. One cavernous area, near an entrance, was likely busier during the early Bronze Age, between 4,200 and 2,700 years ago. Here, fragments of a dagger, sword and axe were discovered. Another artery of the cave was occupied during the Neolithic era, up to 7,400 years ago.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现，早期人类逐渐穿越了庞大的洞穴系统，在不同时期访问了不同的部分。内部史前活动的最早证据可以追溯到大约 41,000 年前。入口附近的一个洞穴区域在 4,200 至 2,700 年前的青铜时代早期可能比较繁忙。在这里，发现了匕首、剑和斧头的碎片。洞穴的另一条动脉在新石器时代（距今 7,400 年前）就被占据。

paras.en: - Researchers recently discovered that traces of ancient DNA from humans can survive for millennia on cave walls and in rock art, based on findings from 11 sites in Spain and Portugal.
paras.zh: - 研究人员最近根据西班牙和葡萄牙 11 个地点的发现，发现古代人类 DNA 的痕迹可以在洞穴墙壁和岩石艺术中保存数千年。

paras.en: - The DNA likely appears in the rock art because prehistoric artists would apply red ochre paint with their hands or spit it from their mouths on to the cave wall.
paras.zh: - DNA 很可能出现在岩石艺术中，因为史前艺术家会用手涂抹红色赭石颜料或将其从嘴里吐到洞穴墙壁上。

paras.en: Despite identifying these timelines, the researchers have not yet determined how any one group of people may have used the cave—for shelter, rituals or other practices. What is clear, they say, is that Catalonia has a much richer Paleolithic history than previously thought. Following this finding, the researchers say, the region deserves more attention in Ice Age studies.
paras.zh: 尽管确定了这些时间线，研究人员尚未确定任何一组人可能如何使用这个洞穴——进行庇护、仪式或其他活动。他们说，显而易见的是，加泰罗尼亚的旧石器时代历史比以前想象的要丰富得多。研究人员表示，根据这一发现，该地区值得在冰河时代研究中得到更多关注。

paras.en: “Contrary to what was previously thought, northeastern Iberia holds first-rate Paleolithic rock art sites,” Salas-Altès says in the statement. “The Mediterranean art of western Europe is now enriched by a new body of rock art, which allows us to characterize in greater depth a Mediterranean graphic tradition with an identity of its own, distinct from that of the Franco-Cantabrian region.”
paras.zh: “与之前的想法相反，伊比利亚东北部拥有一流的旧石器时代岩石艺术遗址，”萨拉斯-阿尔特斯在声明中说。 “西欧的地中海艺术现在因新的岩石艺术而更加丰富，这使我们能够更深入地描绘地中海图形传统，使其具有自己的特色，与法国-坎塔布连地区的特色不同。”

articles.title: Wandrd’s Magnetic Camera Straps Are My New Favorite Accessory
articles.author: Julian Chokkattu

paras.en: More than a decade ago, Peak Design rethought the humble camera strap. This was a necessary development. When you buy a camera, manufacturers almost always toss in a chintzy, uninspired strap with their logo on it. These cheap straps have cheap mounting systems that make it hard to quickly remove the strap from the camera when you need to, like when you're attaching your camera to a tripod or gimbal and you’d rather not have a dangling strap whacking you in the face.
paras.zh: 十多年前，Peak Design 重新思考了不起眼的相机带。这是一个必要的发展。当你购买相机时，制造商几乎总是会赠送一条印有他们标志的廉价、平庸的背带。这些便宜的背带具有廉价的安装系统，因此在您需要时很难快速从相机上取下背带，例如当您将相机连接到三脚架或万向节时，并且您不想让悬垂的背带打到您的脸上。

paras.en: Peak Design solved this with its Anchor Links system, small circular nubs you leave attached to camera eyelets that make detaching or even swapping straps easy. The quick-connect mechanism is now the de facto industry standard and has inspired countless copycats.
paras.zh: Peak Design 通过其 Anchor Links 系统解决了这个问题，该系统是连接在相机孔眼上的小圆形小块，可以轻松拆卸甚至更换肩带。快速连接机制现已成为事实上的行业标准，并激发了无数模仿者。

paras.en: Now, Wandrd has outdone that design using magnets.
paras.zh: 现在，Wandrd 使用磁铁超越了这种设计。

paras.en: “We're photographers ourselves, so we're constantly ideating, tinkering, thinking of ways that things can be better,” Ryan Cope, Wandrd cofounder, tells WIRED. “A camera strap like this has been at the back of our minds for a while.”
paras.zh: “我们自己就是摄影师，所以我们不断地构思、修补、思考如何让事情变得更好，”Wandrd 联合创始人瑞安·科普 (Ryan Cope) 告诉《连线》杂志。 “像这样的相机背带已经在我们的脑海中浮现了一段时间。”

paras.en: Wandrd—known for its camera bags—launched its Magnetic Camera Strap system on Thursday. It features a circular anchor similar to Peak Design, called “Torus Links.” The anchors attach to your camera’s eyelets and are rated to carry up to 198 pounds—so unless you're bench-pressing your camera, they'll do the job. If the cord does start to wear down over time, you'll first see yellow under the black fabric—a sign you should replace the Torus Link. If it's red, you should stop using the link immediately—a warning system borrowed from Peak Design. (Wandrd offers a two-year warranty.)
paras.zh: 以相机包闻名的 Wandrd 于周四推出了磁性相机带系统。它具有类似于 Peak Design 的圆形锚点，称为“Torus Links”。这些锚固定在相机的孔眼上，额定承重达 198 磅，因此除非您卧推相机，否则它们就可以胜任。如果随着时间的推移，绳索确实开始磨损，您首先会在黑色织物下面看到黄色，这表明您应该更换环面链接。如果它是红色的，你应该立即停止使用该链接——这是一个借鉴自 Peak Design 的警告系统。 （Wandrd 提供两年保修。）

paras.en: Unlike Peak Design's anchors, the Wandrd anchors look like donuts, with a hole in the middle. When you attach the strap, the embedded magnets guide the Torus Link into the strap's CoreLock mechanism, which pinches into the hole to secure the camera body. The magnets make connecting a strap easier, and they keep the strap fastened to the anchor, but you can’t just pull the strap off like you’re pulling a MagSafe accessory on your phone. You’ll need to use the strap’s dual-pinch mechanism to remove it from the Torus Link, a design that’s more secure.
paras.zh: 与 Peak Design 的锚不同，Wandrd 锚看起来像甜甜圈，中间有一个洞。当您连接腕带时，嵌入式磁铁会将 Torus Link 引导至腕带的 CoreLock 机构中，该机构会捏入孔中以固定相机机身。磁铁使连接带子变得更容易，并且它们将带子固定在锚点上，但你不能像拉手机上的 MagSafe 配件那样直接拉掉带子。您需要使用表带的双捏机构将其从环面链接上取下，这种设计更安全。

paras.en: It’s a much faster way to connect and disconnect a strap, and that speed pays off in the field. This week, I had to photograph a product during a press briefing. Usually, I use Peak Design's Leash and, instead of taking off the strap, I bunch it up in my hand when it's not around my neck. It's not that it's hard to remove—it's just an extra step I have to think about. But Wandrd's magnetic system felt faster to unlock mid-shoot when I wanted to lower the camera for an awkward, low-angle shot, and reattaching the strap was practically instantaneous. I did the whole swap one-handed, with the magnets doing most of the work.
paras.zh: 这是一种更快地连接和断开表带的方法，并且这种速度在现场得到了回报。本周，我必须在新闻发布会上拍摄产品照片。通常，我使用 Peak Design 的皮带，当它没有挂在脖子上时，我不会取下带子，而是将它束在手中。这并不是说它很难删除——这只是我必须考虑的一个额外步骤。但当我想要降低相机进行尴尬的低角度拍摄时，Wandrd 的磁性系统感觉解锁速度更快，并且重新连接带子几乎是瞬间的。我用一只手完成了整个交换工作，大部分工作都是由磁铁完成的。

paras.en: “I love magnets, man,” Cope says. “I love the simplicity they create—guiding things into place. You don't always have a place to put your camera down; I like that magnets help guide them and are a lot more secure, and they're also just fun.”
paras.zh: “我喜欢磁铁，伙计，”科普说。 “我喜欢它们创造的简单性——引导物品就位。你并不总是有地方可以放下相机；我喜欢磁铁帮助引导它们并且更安全，而且它们也很有趣。”

paras.en: I have two Torus Links on my camera body, one on the right eyelet and another on the tripod baseplate. But my favorite configuration turns the strap into a single-point sling. The strap has a built-in “Torus Loop” on the buckle—clip one end directly into it to create a closed loop worn across your torso, leaving just a single magnetic connector to snap onto your camera. When you unclip the camera to shoot freely, the strap stays neatly in place across your body instead of sliding off your shoulder.
paras.zh: 我的相机机身上有两个环面连杆，一个位于右孔眼上，另一个位于三脚架底板上。但我最喜欢的配置是将带子变成单点吊带。该肩带的带扣上有一个内置的“环形环”，将一端直接夹入其中，形成一个穿在您躯干上的闭环，只留下一个磁性连接器来卡在您的相机上。当您松开相机自由拍摄时，肩带会整齐地固定在您的身体上，而不是从肩膀上滑落。

paras.en: The nylon felt comfortable across my chest and near my neck—there's no padding, but that's intentional. Cope says Wandrd spent two years developing this custom “liquid nylon” tubular webbing that is softer along the edges, so it won't feel like the strap is cutting into your neck after a long day of wear. The lack of metal throughout the strap system also prevents the strap from scratching up your camera gear.
paras.zh: 尼龙在我的胸部和脖子附近感觉很舒服——没有衬垫，但这是故意的。 Cope 表示，Wandrd 花了两年时间开发这种定制的“液体尼龙”管状织带，其边缘较柔软，因此在长时间佩戴后不会感觉带子割伤了您的脖子。整个表带系统没有金属，也可以防止表带划伤您的相机装备。

paras.en: Best of all, you don't have to replace your strap to use Wandrd's system. If you have a strap you love—maybe a fancy leather strap someone gifted you—Wandrd is selling a DIY kit ($29) that lets you attach its Magnetic CoreLock system to the ends of your preferred strap. Otherwise, the strap kit comes in a 30-mm size ($69), a 15-mm “Lite" ($49), and a wrist strap ($39).
paras.zh: 最重要的是，您无需更换表带即可使用 Wandrd 的系统。如果您有一条喜欢的表带（也许是别人送给您的精美皮革表带），Wandrd 正在销售一款 DIY 套件（29 美元），您可以将其磁性 CoreLock 系统连接到您喜欢的表带的末端。另外，表带套件有 30 毫米尺寸（69 美元）、15 毫米“Lite”尺寸（49 美元）和腕带（39 美元）。

paras.en: I don't know if Wandrd's system will see the same success as Peak Design's Anchor Links, but I don't see myself switching back anytime soon. Magnets are just too dang cool.
paras.zh: 我不知道 Wandrd 的系统是否会取得与 Peak Design 的 Anchor Links 相同的成功，但我不认为自己会很快切换回去。磁铁太酷了。
